Almighty and eternal God, who have granted your servants, in the confession of the true faith, to acknowledge the glory of the eternal Trinity and to adore the Unity in the power of its majesty: we beseech you that, by the firmness of this same faith, we may always be defended against every adversity. Through.

**Secret.** Sanctify, we beseech you, Lord God, through the invocation of your name [Same: through the power of your Only-Begotten], the sacrificial offering of this oblation, and, with the Holy Spirit working through it, perfect us ourselves for you as an eternal offering. Through.

**Preface.** It is worthy and just, [continuing], eternal [Col. 0445C] God. You, with your only-begotten Son and the Holy Spirit, are one God, one Lord—not in the singularity of one person, but in the Trinity of one substance. For whatever, by your revelation, we believe concerning your glory, this we also think concerning your Son and concerning the Holy Spirit, without distinction of difference [Same: without distinction of difference], so that in the confession of the everlasting [Same: true and everlasting] Godhead, the distinctiveness of the persons, the unity of the essence, and equality in majesty may be adored. Whom the angels praise.

### 7. Postcommunion

May the reception of this sacrament and the confession of the eternal Trinity [Same: the eternal confession of the Holy Trinity and of that same undivided Unity] advance us, Lord God, toward the salvation of body and soul. Through.

[Col. 0445D] **Another.** Lord God, almighty Father, bless and protect your servants subject to your majesty through your only Son, in the power of the Holy Spirit, so that, secure from every enemy, we may continually rejoice in your praise. Through the same.

**Reading from the Letter of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Corinthians.** Brothers, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with us all.

[Col. 0446B] **Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John.** At that time Jesus said to his disciples: When the Paraclete comes, whom I shall send you from the Father, the Spirit of truth.

**Mass for requesting the grace of the Holy Spirit.**

God, to whom every heart is open, every will speaks, and no secret is hidden: purify, by the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, the thoughts of our hearts, so that we may deserve to love you perfectly and praise you worthily. Through.

**Secret.** May this offering, Lord God, cleanse the stains of our heart, so that it may become a worthy dwelling place of the Holy Spirit. Through . . . in the unity of the same Holy Spirit.

**Preface.** It is worthy and just, [continuing], eternal [Col. 0446C] God. You inspect the secrets of our thoughts, and every intention of our mind lies open to the gaze of your providence. Look favorably upon the hidden chambers of our heart, and purify our thoughts with the dew of the Holy Spirit, so that we may think and act in ways worthy of your majesty. Through Christ.

**Postcommunion.** As we offer you the sacrifice of our salvation, grant us, Lord God, with purified minds to celebrate more frequently the mystery of your goodness. Through.

**Another.** Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that by our diligent prayers we may merit the Holy Spirit, so that by his grace we may be freed from every temptation and obtain the forgiveness of our sins. Through . . . in the unity of the same Holy Spirit.

**Also, a Mass of Saint Augustine.**

[Col. 0446D]

Grant me, Lord, as a sinner, a confession pleasing to you; bring forth in my heart the groans of utterance that may knock upon your ears. Grant me the disposition of mind by which, in humility of heart, I may receive your profound goodness. Grant me, Lord, to pray for that very thing which delights you to hear, so that you may grant it. Implant it in my soul, so that you yourself may be my constant delight. [Col. 0447A] Grant me inward tears arising from your love, tears that can loosen the bonds of my sins. Hear, my God, hear, light of my eyes; hear what I ask, and grant me what I should ask so that you may hear. For if you look away, I perish; if you look upon me, I live. If you regard me with justice, I stink as one dead. If you regard me with mercy, you raise the one who stinks from the grave. If you regard my evil deeds, the torments of hell scarcely suffice. If you look upon me with your customary compassion, you can change me for the better. What evil is there that I do not contain? Or what good is there that you do not contain? What evil is there that I, a corruptible creature, do not contain? What good is there that you, Creator and author of creatures, do not contain? Through my fault I fell from your hand; you are a powerful craftsman, able to fashion me again into something pleasing to you. Correct me in mercy; do not abandon me, and do not correct me in anger. Remove far from me what you hate in me, [Col. 0447B] and look upon me according to your will. Drive away from me the enemy of lust, and implant in me the spirit of chastity. Put every vice to death in me, and give life to my soul within me. Through the Lord.

**Secret.** Although these gifts are offered to you, holy Father and Lord, by my unworthy hands, and although I am not worthy even to invoke your name, nevertheless, because the offerings are presented through the holy and sanctified name of your Son, may they rise before you like incense, with the fragrance of sweetness. Through.

**Preface.** It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary for us always and everywhere to give you thanks, eternal God. But what worthy offering can an unworthy minister make to you, except that he confess the repentance of faith [Perhaps: through repentance], this very thing—that he is considered [Perhaps: to be considered] unworthy of so great an office? But you, God of great mercy, [Col. 0447C] we beseech you not to condemn us on the testimony of our own mouth, but strengthen us with the consolation of paternal forgiveness, and continually renew and reform us with your hands after our fall into sin. My soul invokes you, who made me, asking that you not forget the one who has forgotten you, and that you not abandon the one who seeks you, O life that will never die. Whoever knows you knows eternity. Love knows you. O eternal truth and true love! One God, triune God, in whose mercy I place great trust: be salvation for my weakness and the true raiser-up of my soul. Teach me patience to endure adversity. Teach me knowledge of the Scriptures, so that I may speak without becoming proud, and be silent without growing sluggish. Restrain me so that I do not fall. Bind me so that I do not let go. For you are my honor, my praise, and my trust. My God, [Col. 0447D] I give you thanks for your gifts, but preserve them for me. For in this way you will preserve me, and the things you have given me will increase and reach perfection. And you will be with me in all things, because you gave me both existence and what I am. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.** May the Lord mercifully attend to our vows and forgive our sins. May he grant what we desire and drive far away what we fear, so that, together with the whole company of the faithful, by making vows and offering to God the sacrifice of praise, we may reach the fruit of righteousness, by the granting of his divine mercy. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, his only-begotten Son, with whom God lives and reigns in the unity of the Holy Spirit, forever and ever.

## CHAPTER II. Monday: Mass for Sins

[Col. 0448A]

Hear, Lord, we beseech you, the prayers of those who entreat you, and spare the sins of those who confess to you, so that in your kindness you may grant us forgiveness and peace together. Through.

**Reading from the prophet Jeremiah.** If our iniquities rise up against us, Lord, deliver us, we beseech you; do it for the sake of your name.

**Reading from the holy Gospel according to Luke.** At that time Jesus said to his disciples: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.

**Over the offerings.** We offer you sacrifices of appeasement, Lord, so that in your mercy you may absolve our sins and direct our wavering hearts. Through.

[Col. 0448B] **Preface.** It is worthy and just, [continuing], eternal God. Save us from the mouth of the fiercest lion, who goes about roaring, seeking whom he may seize and devour from the unity of your Church. But you, most powerful Lord, from the tribe of Judah, crush the wickedness of his opposing power; preserve us in body, freed from his fiery assaults, and purify us in heart. Through the Lord.

**Within the Canon.** Therefore, Lord, this offering which we offer to you for our sins and offenses, that it may deserve to obtain remission of all our transgressions, we beseech you, that . . .

**At the Conclusion.** Grant us, eternal Savior, that, having received forgiveness of sins through this gift, we may thereafter avoid sins. Through.

**Another.** God, whose proper nature is always to have mercy and spare, receive our supplication, so that those whom the chain of sins binds may be released by the mercy of your compassion. Through.

**Also, for requesting tears.**

Most gentle almighty God, who brought forth from the rock a spring of living water for your thirsty people, draw tears of compunction from the hardness of our heart, so that we may be able to mourn our sins and, by your mercy, deserve to receive remission. Through.

**Within the Canon.** Look favorably, we beseech you, Lord God, upon this offering, which we offer to your majesty for our sins, and bring forth from our eyes [Col. 0448D] rivers by which the due fires of punishment may be extinguished. Through.

**Preface.** It is worthy and just, [continuing], through Christ our Lord. You looked upon the blessed Apostle Peter with a compassionate gaze, so that he might wash away the sin of his threefold denial with the bitterest tears. By the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, draw from us tears of repentance corresponding to the weight of our sins, so that we may bitterly lament what we have wickedly done; thus may the effect of our petition reach fruitfully before your compassionate regard, and through him may we be permitted to hope for forgiveness who was handed over for our offenses in order to redeem us by his blood, Christ our Savior. Whom the angels praise.

### 9. At the Conclusion

May the sacrifice that we have offered to your majesty, Lord, [Col. 0449A] advance us toward the forgiveness of our sins and grant us the consolation of your mercy. Through.

**Another.** Mercifully pour into our hearts, Lord God, the grace of the Holy Spirit, which may make us, through groans, wash away the stains of our sins with tears and, by your generosity, bring about for us the effect of the forgiveness we desire. Through the Lord, etc., in the unity of the same.

**Also, a Mass of Saint Augustine.**

Forgive me, we beseech you, Lord. The consciousness of a stained life makes me fearful, and the shame of my crimes makes me captive. Since I cannot obtain forgiveness for myself, I stand ready to pray for others; if you deign to hear, Lord, I bring before you the groans of captives, [Col. 0449B] the tribulations of peoples, the dangers of nations, the necessities of travelers, the poverty of the weak, the despair of the sick, the failing strength of the old, the sighs of the young, the vows of virgins, and the lamentations of widows. But since the same chain of sin binds me as binds the people, I mourn the common sufferings. May the prayer bound [Alternative: subjected] by sins not harm your people, Lord. Through me the vow is offered to you; through you may my ministry be completed. Through.

**Over the offerings.** We remember, eternal God, almighty Father, the most glorious passion of your Son, and also his resurrection and ascension into heaven. Therefore we ask your majesty, O God, that the prayers of our humility may ascend into the presence of your mercy, [Col. 0449C] and that the fullness of your divinity may descend upon this bread and upon this chalice. May that incomprehensible and invisible majesty of your Holy Spirit also descend, just as once it descended upon the sacrifices of the fathers. Through the same Lord.

**At the Conclusion.** Giving you thanks, we pray, Lord, that you may mercifully cleanse our heart from vices and continually fill us with spiritual gifts. Through our Lord.

## CHAPTER III. Tuesday: Mass for Requesting the Aid of Angels

Grant us the perpetual assistance of your mercy, Lord, to whom you have also granted that angelic aid not be lacking. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0449D] **Secret.** We offer you sacrifices of praise, Lord, humbly beseeching you that, with the angelic intercession assisting us, you may both accept them in favor and grant that they may bring about our salvation. Through the Lord.

**Postcommunion.** Filled, Lord, with heavenly blessing, we humbly implore you to grant that what we celebrate through fragile ministry may, by the help of the holy archangels, prove beneficial to us. Through our Lord.

**Over the people.** Guard your people, we beseech you, Lord, with perpetual goodness, so that, always secure and aided by the necessary forms of help, they may continually rejoice in the devout worship of spirits pleasing to you. Through our Lord Jesus.

**Reading from the Apocalypse of the blessed Apostle John.** In those days [Col. 0450A] the angel said to me: Write: Blessed are those at the supper of the wedding.

**Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John.** At that time Jesus went up to Jerusalem. Now at Jerusalem there is a sheep-pool.

**Also another, for temptations of the thoughts.**

Most gentle almighty God, look favorably upon our prayers and free our hearts from the temptation of evil thoughts, so that we may deserve to become a worthy dwelling place of the Holy Spirit. Through the Lord.

**Secret.** We offer these oblations to you, Lord God, for our salvation, so that you may deign to illuminate our souls with the grace of the Holy Spirit. Through our Lord.

**Preface.** It is worthy and just, [continuing], eternal [Col. 0450B] God. We humbly implore your mercy: deign mercifully to pour the grace of the Holy Spirit into our souls, so that we may deserve to love you perfectly and praise you worthily. Through Christ.

### 10. At the Conclusion

Through this sacrifice, Lord, which we have offered to your goodness, cleanse our hearts from every temptation, we beseech you. Through our Lord.

**Another.** God, who enlighten every person coming into this world, enlighten our hearts, we beseech you, with the splendor of your grace, so that we may be able to think and love what is worthy of your majesty. Through our Lord.

**Also, a Mass of Saint Augustine.**

[Col. 0450C] Offering you a sacrifice of exultation for our sins, Lord, we ask your goodness to incline your ear with merciful kindness to our petitions, to accept our vow with gracious favor, to gladden the tribulations of our heart through manifold mercy, and to grant us, through your mercy, what our tongue is not sufficient to express in prayer—what the devout mind desires—you who know the thoughts of the heart and search the kidneys. Through the Lord.

**Secret.** Terrible and most loving God, deign to accept this sacrifice, which we offer to you for the remission of our sins or for the repose of our departed brothers, because our vows are your gifts. We offer you nothing better than what you have given; above all, this is what we offer in remembrance, as is right, of the Lord’s institution, in honor and glory of our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, the King and Judge who is to come. Through the same Lord our Jesus Christ.

**Postcommunion.** May almighty God graciously receive our vows, and, appeased, look upon us, his servants; may he fulfill our desires in good works and defend us from the snares of our enemies. Through the Lord.

## CHAPTER IV. Wednesday: Mass of Holy Wisdom

God, who through Wisdom co-eternal with you created humanity when it did not exist and mercifully restored what was lost, [Col. 0451A] grant, we beseech you, that, with the same Wisdom inspiring us, we may love you with our whole mind and run toward you with our whole heart. Through the Lord.

**Reading from the Letter of the blessed Apostle Paul.** Brothers, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.

**Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Matthew.** At that time Jesus answered and said: I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden . . .

**Secret.** May the gift of this offering of ours be sanctified, we beseech you, Lord God, with your Wisdom working with it, so that it may be pleasing to you for praise and profitable to us for salvation. Through the Lord.

**At the Conclusion.** Through these holy things that we have received, pour, we beseech you, Lord, the light of your Wisdom into our hearts, so that we may truly acknowledge you [Col. 0451B] and faithfully love you. Through the same.

**Over the people.** God, who sent your Son and showed the Creator to creation, look favorably upon us, your servants, and prepare in our hearts a dwelling worthy of *agiae sophiae* (holy wisdom). Through the same.

**Mass for Requesting Humility.**

God, who resist the proud and grant grace to the humble, increase in us the virtue of true humility, whose form your only-begotten Son displayed to the faithful in himself, so that we may never provoke your indignation by exaltation, but rather, in submission, always receive the gifts of your goodness. Through the same.

**Secret.** May this offering, Lord, obtain for us, we beseech you, the remission [Col. 0451C] of all sins and the grace of true humility; and at the same time may it remove from our hearts the desire of the flesh and of the eyes, and worldly ambition, so that, living soberly, justly, and devoutly before you, we may obtain eternal rewards. Through the Lord.

**Postcommunion.** May reception of this sacrament, Lord, wipe away the stains of our sins and lead us to the heavenly kingdoms. Through the Lord.

### 11. Also, a Mass of Saint Augustine

Lord God, incomprehensible, eternal, everlasting, blessed, who said: “I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance”; and although you have no need of our progress, you nevertheless rejoice more over one sinner doing penance than over ninety-nine righteous who have no need of repentance: because you alone are God, and besides you there is no other; you who do not desire the death of a sinner, but that he should be converted and live: convert us, Lord, to yourself, and we shall be converted. Convert us, God our Savior, and turn your anger away from us. Do not destroy us with our sins; do not hand over to beasts the souls that confess you; do not abandon us forever. Do not enter into judgment with your servants, nor correct us in the anger of your fury. Have mercy on us, Lord; have mercy on us. We are the work of your hands; let us not perish. Remember your congregation, which you created from the beginning. Direct us in the right way; teach [Col. 0452A] us to do your will, for you are our God. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

**Secret.** Deign also, Lord, we beseech you, mercifully to bless and graciously to sanctify this offering, which we offer to you for the remission of our sins or for the repose of our departed brothers, so that your sanctification may be the salvation and protection of all souls. Through.

**Preface.** It is worthy and just, [continuing], eternal God, King of heaven, King of kings, God of gods, Lord of lords, and to offer sacrifices of praise. Hear the prayer and supplication of your male and female servants, of all the orthodox; receive their tears with your ears. “Abba, Father,” fulfill the duty of your name over this congregation of yours [Col. 0452B] and over your entire Catholic Church, spread throughout the whole world in peace. Rule them, almighty Father; protect them; preserve them; sanctify them; govern them; discipline them; console them. Just as you did not disdain to gather and call them, so may they be inflamed by your love, that they may not be despised by you, most merciful and loving Father. We pray you, Lord, that the work of your redemption and calling may not perish from us. Just as you deigned to call those who were wandering, so may you deign to guard those who dwell and gather in this sheepfold. Through Christ the Lord.

**At the Conclusion.** Those whom you have satisfied with a heavenly gift, Lord, grant, we beseech you, that just as in your most loving mercy you gave us the will to come to you, so you may deign to grant us, your servants, understanding of wisdom, strength, and ability, so that we may deserve to serve you according to your will. Through the Lord.

## CHAPTER V. Thursday: On Charity

Almighty and eternal God, who write the justice of your law with your finger in the hearts of believers, grant us increase of faith, hope, and charity; and, so that we may deserve to attain what you promise, make us love what you command. Through.

**Another.** God, who make all things work for the good of those who love you, grant our hearts an inviolable love, so that desires conceived through your inspiration may not be changed by any temptation. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0452D] **Reading from the Letter of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Corinthians.** Brothers, charity is patient, charity is kind; charity is not jealous.

**Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Matthew.** At that time Jesus said to his disciples: Little children, I am with you only a little while; you will seek me.

**Secret.** Send, Lord, we beseech you, the Holy Spirit, who may make these gifts now present into your sacrament for us and purify our hearts for receiving it. Through . . . in the unity of the same Holy Spirit.

God, who renew us in your image through sacraments and commandments, perfect our steps in your paths, and through these things that we offer cause the gift of charity, which you have made us hope for, [Col. 0453A] to be grasped as a sacrifice. Through our Lord.

**Preface.** It is worthy and just, [continuing], eternal God. You have made your faithful harmonious through a mutual law and bound them together by such a covenant of your peace [Perhaps: through your peace] that no one should attempt to inflict upon another what he would not wish inflicted upon himself, and that each should also provide for another the good that, by natural fellowship, he would desire for his own interests; so that, while through mutual affection they find one another [Perhaps: are diminished], there may be in each a common [Perhaps: would be] love loving itself, and there may be one mind among all. Through Christ.

**Postcommunion.** Pour into us, Lord, the Spirit of your charity, so that those whom you have satisfied with one heavenly bread you may make harmonious in one [your] goodness. Through the Lord . . . [Col. 0453B] of the same.

May the grace of the Holy Spirit, we beseech you, Lord, illuminate our hearts and abundantly refresh us with the sweetness of perfect charity. Through the Lord . . . in the unity of the same Holy Spirit.

God, life of the faithful, glory of the humble, blessedness of the righteous, mercifully receive the prayers of those who entreat you, so that souls thirsting for your promises may always be filled from the abundance of your charity. Through the Lord.

**Also another, against temptations of the flesh.**

Burn our kidneys and our heart with the fire of the Holy Spirit, Lord, so that we may serve you chastely in body and please you in heart [Supplement: and with a pure heart]. Through.

**Secret.** Break apart, Lord, the bonds of our sins, so that we may sacrifice to you a sacrifice of praise in complete [Col. 0453C] freedom; repay what you previously granted, and save us through forgiveness, whom you deigned to save through grace. Through the Lord.

**At the Conclusion.** Lord, our helper and protector, we beseech you: may our flesh bloom again with the strength of purity and the freshness of holiness; and, rescued from the hand of Tartarus, may you command it to be presented in the joy of the resurrection. Through the Lord.

**Also, a Mass of Saint Augustine.**

Lord, almighty God, who save those who hope in you; most merciful Lord, who call back those who wander; merciful Lord, who do not despise those who confess; Lord Father, when the righteous falls, you extend your hand; you are exalted in the heavens, and you promised to dwell on earth wherever two or three are gathered in your name, to be in their midst. Lord, we hold you to your promise, that you may grant forgiveness to penitents and that all who seek you may find you. For we know you to be the searcher of our consciences, and therefore we ask forgiveness for our offenses. You are a great Lord and greatly worthy of praise. We implore you and ask that you be favorable to us. We confess our evils to you so that we may deserve to obtain your good things. Through.

**Secret.** Therefore, trusting in your goodness and devoted to your praise, Lord, we bring you this spotless sacrifice of a unique offering, so that you may grant forgiveness of our sins to us, your living servants, and eternal rest to our departed brothers. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0454A] **Preface.** It is worthy and just, [continuing], eternal God. We implore your mercy, so that we who exist by your authorship may be directed by your governance. Let us not be abandoned to our own senses, but, always led along the path of your truth, let us strive to practice what you command, so that we may be able to receive the gifts you promise. Through Christ.

**Postcommunion.** Giving you thanks, we pray, Lord, that you may mercifully cleanse our heart from vices and continually fill us with spiritual gifts. Through the Lord.

## CHAPTER VI. Friday: Mass of the Holy Cross

God, who willed the standard of the life-giving cross to be sanctified by the precious blood of your only-begotten Son, grant, we beseech you, that those who rejoice in the honor of this same holy cross may also rejoice everywhere in your protection. Through.

**Reading from the Letter of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Philippians.** Brothers, Christ became obedient to the Father for us, even unto death.

**Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Matthew.** At that time, as Jesus went up to Jerusalem, he took . . .

**Secret.** May this offering, Lord, cleanse us from every offense; on the altar of the cross it also bore the offenses of the whole world. Through our Lord.

### 13. Preface

It is worthy and just, [continuing], eternal God. You established the salvation of the human race upon the wood of the cross, so that from the place where death arose, life might arise, and the one who conquered on the wood might also be conquered on the wood. Through Christ.

**At Communion.** Be present with us, Lord our God, and defend forever with its aid those whom you have made rejoice in the honor of the holy cross. Through.

**Also, Mass for tribulation and need, on the same day.**

Almighty and eternal God, look favorably upon our prayers and give abundance of water to our head and a fountain of tears to our eyes, so that, washed from the stain of sin, we may overcome the consuming flames of vengeance by the abundance of our weeping. Through our Lord.

**Secret.** Through these offerings, we beseech you, Lord, grant that you pour not only tears into our eyes but also profound mourning for our sins into our heart. Through.

[Col. 0454D] **Preface.** It is worthy and just, [continuing], eternal God. Hearing the sound of the divine word that says, “Blessed are those who mourn now, for they shall be comforted,” we greatly desire to weep for our sins; but our eyes are stony, and because of the hardness of our heart we cannot shed tears. Therefore we ask you, Lord, first to soften the fountain of the hardness of our heart through our repentance, and afterward, through the gift of your grace, abundantly pour rivers of tears into our eyes. Through Christ the Lord.

**Postcommunion.** Satisfied with your body and blood, Lord, we beseech you to grant us continual compunction of heart for our sins, mourning, and rivers of tears, so that we may deserve heavenly consolation in the future. Through.

**Mass of Saint Augustine.**

[Col. 0455A]

Almighty and eternal God, look favorably upon the prayers of your Church; give us right faith, perfect charity, and true humility. Grant, Lord, that there may be in us a simple affection, strong patience, persevering obedience, perpetual peace, a pure mind, a right and clean heart, good will, a holy conscience, spiritual compunction, strength of soul, an undefiled life, and blameless perfection, so that, running manfully, we may happily deserve to enter your kingdom. Through.

**Secret.** As we offer you the libations of sacrifices, Lord, look upon the confession of our humility, so that you may sanctify these offerings that we present to you for the remission of our sins or for the repose of our departed brothers, [Col. 0455B] and so that the abundance of your blessing may sustain the dryness of those who receive them. Through the Lord.

**Postcommunion.** May God, with whom abundant mercy dwells, make us the purest vessels for himself and refresh our weakness with spiritual delights, so that our hearts may always hunger and thirst for him, and the vows of our humility may cry out. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## CHAPTER VII. Saturday: Mass of Saint Mary

Grant us, your servants, we beseech you, Lord God, to rejoice in perpetual prosperity of mind and body, and through the glorious intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin to be freed from present sorrow and to enjoy future [Col. 0455C] joy. Through our Lord.

**Reading from the Book of Wisdom.** From the beginning and before the ages I was created, and unto . . .

**Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Luke.** At that time Jesus entered a certain village, and a woman . . .

**Secret.** Through your propitiation, Lord, and through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin, may this offering advance us toward perpetual and present prosperity. Through our Lord.

**Postcommunion.** Having received the aids of our salvation, Lord, grant, we beseech you, that we may everywhere be protected by the patronage of her in whose honor we have offered these things to your majesty. Through.

### 14. Over the people

Almighty God, protect your servants from every danger by the right hand of your power, [Col. 0455D] and, with blessed Mary ever-virgin interceding, make us rejoice in present and eternal prosperity. Through.

**Also, a Mass in commemoration of Saint Mary.**

Forgive the sins of your servants, we beseech you; and since by our deeds we are unable to please you, grant that, through the intercession of the Mother of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, we may always meditate upon what pleases you and continually carry it out in word and deed with a pure heart.

**Secret.** Having received our offerings and prayers, we beseech you, with blessed Mary ever-virgin interceding, cleanse our sins; mercifully compel our rebellious wills also toward you, and grant us eternal life. Through.

[Col. 0456A] **At Communion.** We beseech you, Lord our God, that you may make the holy mysteries, which you have bestowed for the protection of our restoration, both a present remedy for us and a future one.

**Also at Communion.** We beseech you, Lord, with blessed Mary ever-virgin interceding, purify your faithful in body and mind alike, so that, moved by your inspiration, they may be able to avoid harmful pleasures; and, so that we may not be caught by their allurements, may we continually be nourished by your sweetness. Through.

**Also, a Mass of Saint Augustine.**

Lord our God, great and almighty, who heal the brokenhearted and bind up their contrition: may your goodness make you favorable to us, whom the condition of human frailty has placed in sorrow. Hear, [Col. 0456B] Lord, our prayers, and forgive all our offenses. May we be freed from every distress by the strength of your hand, so that with your saints we may rejoice here and forever. Through our Lord.

**Secret.** Deign also, Lord, we beseech you, mercifully to bless and graciously to sanctify this offering, which we have offered to you for the salvation of the living and the repose of the dead, so that your sanctification may be the salvation and protection of souls. Through the Lord.

**Preface.** It is worthy and just, [continuing], through Christ our Lord. Through him we humbly beseech you, almighty God the Father, to accept this sacrifice that we offer to you and mercifully grant us, your servants, the consolation of your goodness. It is yours, Lord, to heal the brokenhearted; it is yours to console [Col. 0456C] those who mourn. May it now please your goodness to rescue the oppressed, recall captives, and gladden those placed in distress. Through him we pray to you, supreme Father, whom heavenly and earthly beings alike praise with you and with the Holy Spirit, and proclaim this hymn in sweet harmony, saying: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of hosts.

**Postcommunion.** May almighty God mercifully regard the groans of our heart, incline the ear of his goodness to our petitions, and gladden us, defended from every sorrow; may he fortify our mind with the aid of his mercy and graciously grant us the remedies of everlasting joy. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## CHAPTER VIII. Mass in Veneration of One Apostle

[Col. 0456D]

God, who make the minds of the faithful one in will, grant us, through the intercession of your blessed apostle, to love what you command and desire what you promise, so that amid worldly changes our hearts may be fixed where true joys are found. Through the Lord.

**Reading from the Letter of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Ephesians.** Brothers, you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household.

**Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John.** At that time Simon Peter said to Jesus: Behold, we have left everything and followed you.

### 15. Secret

Through the mysteries, with the supplication of your blessed apostle, may there be conferred upon us, Lord, the grace that, by moderating earthly desires, we may learn to love heavenly things and, with purified minds, be transferred day by day into the activity of heavenly life. Through the Lord.

**Postcommunion.** Grant us, Lord, through the intercession of your blessed apostle, fellowship in the power of the heavenly table, to desire what is right and to receive what we desire. Through the Lord.

## CHAPTER IX. Mass in Veneration of Several Apostles
The continuous prayer of your blessed apostles, Lord, we beseech you, guard us, so that the Church may be guided by those same men whose leadership is her glory. Through [them].

Reading from the Letter of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Romans. Brothers, for one believes with the heart unto righteousness, but confession is made with the mouth unto salvation. [Col. 0457B]

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “This is my commandment: that you love one another, as I have loved you. Greater …”

Prayer over the offerings. Look favorably, Lord, we beseech you, upon the gifts that we bring in commemoration of your holy apostles N., so that, as their honor is pleasing to you, so through their intercession these gifts may be beneficial to us. Through the Lord.

Preface. It is worthy and just, unto you, eternal God. Humbly entreating you, we ask that you, eternal Shepherd, not abandon your flock, but guard it continually through your blessed apostles N., so that it may be guided by those same rulers whom you appointed as pastors to preside over it, as vicars of your work. Through Christ our Lord. [Col. 0457C]

Prayer after Communion. Having received the pledge of eternal life, we humbly implore you that, strengthened by apostolic protection, we may receive in the manifest participation of the sacrament what we have touched in its image. Through [you].

Prayer over the people. God, protector of those who hope in you, look graciously upon your family, and through your blessed apostles N. defend us from every adversity by the arm of your power. Through our Lord.

## CHAPTER X. Mass in Veneration of One Martyr

God, strength of those who hope in you, graciously attend to our invocations through the glorious intercession of your martyr; and because mortal weakness can do nothing without you, [Col. 0457D] grant us the help of your grace, so that in carrying out your commands we may please you both in will and in deed. Through our Lord.

Prayer over the offerings. Receive, Lord, the prayers of the faithful together with the offerings of sacrifices, so that through the prayers of your glorious martyr, by these dutiful acts of devotion, we may receive forgiveness of all sins and pass over into heavenly glory. Through our Lord.

Prayer after Communion. Having received your gifts, Lord, we beseech you that, through the intercession of your blessed martyr, you may cause us to possess continually both fear and love of your holy name, so that, through frequent participation in the mystery, the effect of our salvation may increase. Through the Lord.

## CHAPTER XI. Mass of One Apostle, or Martyr, or Confessor

[Col. 0458A]

### At the Vigil

Grant us, almighty God, we beseech you, to anticipate with fitting honor the approaching solemnity of blessed N., your apostle, confessor, or martyr, and to celebrate his coming with worthy devotion. Through the Lord.

Prayer over the offerings. May the offering of our devotion be acceptable to you, Lord, and make us come more purified to the apostolic feast. Through [you].

Prayer after Communion. May we receive the grace of your blessing, Lord, through the intercession of your blessed apostle, confessor, or martyr N., so that we may experience, by our supplication, the help of the one whose glory we celebrate in anticipation. Through [you].

### 16. Likewise, the Mass on the Day Itself

[Col. 0458B]

God, who are the wondrous splendor of all your saints, and who have consecrated this day through the martyrdom of your apostle N., grant that your Church may rejoice in the anniversary feast of so great a pontiff, so that we may be protected before your mercy by his example and merits. Through the Lord.

Reading from the Book of Wisdom. Blessed is the man who was found without blemish and who did not go after gold.

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Matthew. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless a grain of wheat …”

Prayer over the offerings. As we celebrate the solemnity of your blessed apostle N., Lord—[perhaps: “as we celebrate, we beseech you”]—may we receive your benefits through the help of the one for whom we offer sacrifices [Col. 0458C] of praise. Through the Lord.

Prayer after Communion. Having received the sacraments, Lord, we humbly beseech you that, through the intercession of your blessed apostle N., what we perform in veneration of his passion may profit us for healing. Through our Lord.

Another prayer. Grant us, Lord our God, we beseech you, to be raised up through the intercessions of your blessed apostle N., so that through those by whom you bestowed upon your Church the beginnings of heavenly gifts, you may grant through them the aids of perpetual salvation. Through our Lord.

## CHAPTER XII. Mass of Many Martyrs

God, who bestowed upon the holy martyrs an abundant gift of grace by which to attain everlasting glory, [Col. 0458D] grant us, your servants, forgiveness of our sins, so that, through the interceding merits of your saints, we may be found worthy to be freed from every adversity, and so that you may cause us to reach their eternal joys, whose power you grant us to celebrate with daily solemnity. Through [you].

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of the blessed Apostle John. In those days I saw a great multitude, which no one could count …

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Matthew. At that time, when Jesus saw the crowds, he went up the mountain. And when he had sat down, his disciples came to him; and opening his mouth, he taught them, saying: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for …”

Prayer over the offerings. Receive, Lord, the gifts that we bring to you from your bounty in honor of your holy martyrs, [Col. 0459A] so that, through their intercession, these sacred mysteries, by the working power of your grace, may sanctify us in the conduct of our present life and lead us to everlasting joys. Through [you].

Prayer after Communion. May the heavenly mystery be for us, Lord, the restoration of mind and body; and by its working we pray that our vices may be cleansed and, through the intercession of your holy martyrs, our righteous desires fulfilled. Through [you].

Another prayer. Almighty and eternal God, whose abundant goodness surpasses both the merits and the petitions of those who entreat you, pour out your mercy upon us, so that through the merits of your martyrs you may forgive us everything that our conscience fears and add what our prayer does not presume to ask. [Col. 0459B] Through [you].

## CHAPTER XIII. Mass in the Church of the Holy Martyrs

Be gracious to us, your servants, Lord, through the glorious merits of these your martyrs who now rest in this church, so that through their devout intercession we may be protected from every adversity. Through the Lord.

Reading from the Book of Wisdom. The tongue of the wise adorns knowledge, but the mouth of fools pours forth foolishness.

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Luke. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning.”

Prayer over the offerings. May your Church [graciousness] receive, Lord, we beseech you, from your [our] hands the gift offered, and through the prayer of these blessed martyrs of yours [Col. 0459C] cleanse us from every sin. Through [you].

### 17. For the Completion

Having partaken of the divine mysteries that we have offered to your majesty in veneration of your holy martyrs, grant, we beseech you, Lord, that through them we may merit forgiveness of sins and be refreshed by the gifts of heavenly grace. Through the Lord.

Another prayer. Father of eternal consolation, grant your people peace and salvation through the prayers of your blessed martyrs, so that they may cling to your commands with complete love and accomplish with their whole will whatever is pleasing to you. Through our Lord.

## CHAPTER XIV. On the Feast of Saints Whose Relics Are in One House

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the holy Mother of God, your holy apostles, martyrs, confessors, virgins, and all the saints whose relics are contained in this church may everywhere assist us by their patronage [perhaps: “through their patronage”], so that here, by their present intercession, we may rejoice in your praise in tranquil peace. Through [you].

Likewise, another prayer. Graciously grant us your help, Lord, we beseech you, and, through the intercession of your saints whose patronage we have taken care to gather in this church, make us free from every adversity and cause us to rejoice with them in eternal happiness. Through [you].

Merciful God, graciously receive the gifts offered to your majesty, we beseech you, so that through the prayers of those whose most sacred relics are kept in this basilica [Col. 0460A] they may become saving for us. Through the Lord.

Prayer after Communion. Having partaken of the divine mysteries, we beseech you, Lord, that the intercession of those whose sacred presence we rejoice in here may protect us everywhere. Through the Lord.

Prayer over the people. Hear graciously, Lord God, in this house of yours the prayers of your servants, so that by the merits of those whose patronage we venerate here we may obtain your grace. Through [you].

## CHAPTER XV. Daily Mass of the Saints

God, who continually gladden us with the solemnity of blessed Mary ever-virgin, of the blessed apostles, martyrs, confessors, virgins, and all the saints together, grant, we beseech you, that those whom we venerate in our daily office we may also follow by the example of a devout life. Through [you].

Prayer over the offerings. We offer to you, Lord, the gifts of our devotion; may they be pleasing to you in honor of your saints and, through your mercy, be made beneficial to us.

Prayer after Communion. Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that through the merits of all your saints interceding for us, we may receive with a pure heart what we have touched with our mouth. Through our Lord.

Prayer over the people. Make us, Lord God, to be raised up by the assistance of holy Mary ever-virgin and defended by the glorious protection of the blessed apostles, martyrs, confessors, virgins, and all the saints together, so that, while we celebrate their feasts together each day, we may likewise be protected from every adversity each day by their help. Through [you].

## CHAPTER XVI. Mass for Enemies

God, lover and guardian of peace and charity, give all our enemies true peace and charity, grant them forgiveness of all their sins, and powerfully rescue us from their snares. Through [you].

Prayer over the offerings. Be appeased, Lord, we beseech you, by the gifts offered, and graciously rescue us from our enemies and grant them pardon for their offenses. Through our Lord.

For the Completion. God, who endowed your servants Moses, Samuel, and Stephen the protomartyr with the virtue of patience, so that they might pray calmly for the sins of their enemies, grant us, we beseech you, through the merits of all the saints, to love our enemies with the love of true devotion and to pour forth before the sight of your majesty continual prayers for their transgressions with the full attention of our mind. Through [you].

## 18. CHAPTER XVII. Mass for One Confessing His Sins

Almighty and eternal God, who are true, holy, and protector of all the saints, to you, our devout Lord, we offer sacrifices of praise with devoted hearts, and we humbly beseech you on behalf of your servant N., that you grant him forgiveness of all his offenses and graciously deign to guard him, so that he may not again return to the will of sin. Through our Lord. [Col. 0461A]

Prayer over the offerings. Receive, most merciful Father, the sacrifice of reconciliation and praise that I, your unworthy and sinful servant, presume to offer to you for the honor of the glory of your name and for the safety of your servant N., so that he may deserve to obtain forgiveness of all his offenses. Through our Lord.

Prayer after Communion. We beseech you, Lord, that through the intercession of your saints on behalf of your servant N. you grant him forgiveness of all sins, bring his work to a good completion, grant him your grace, fill him with faith, hope, and charity, raise his mind to heavenly desires, defend him from every adversity, and lead him to good perseverance. [Col. 0461B] Through our Lord.

## CHAPTER XVIII. Mass for the Salvation of the Living and the Rest of the Dead

Almighty and eternal God, who rule over both the living and the dead, and [add: have mercy upon] all whom you know beforehand will belong to you in faith and works, I humbly beseech you that those for whom I have resolved to pour out prayers—and whom either the present age still retains in the flesh or the future age has already received after their departure from the body—may, through the kindness of your mercy, obtain forgiveness of their sins. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Prayer over the offerings. God, to whom alone is known the number of the elect who are to be placed in heavenly happiness, grant, I beseech you, that the book of blessed predestination may retain written in it the names of all whom I have received as commended in prayer, or the names of all the faithful. [Col. 0461C] Through [you].

Prayer after Communion. Giver of divine bounty [perhaps: “God, giver of forgiveness”] and lover of human salvation, we beseech your mercy: by the grace of your compassion command that the names of your servants and handmaids, which we have written here together in the devout service of love, be written in the book of life. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

[Note: [Col. 0461D] The following material was appended, as an appendix, in the manuscript used by Quercetanus.]

# VARIOUS BLESSINGS

May the Lord bless you from Zion, he who made heaven and earth, in his wisdom and eternal blessing; he who blessed all our holy fathers and our patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, may multiply his spiritual grace in you, just as he multiplied their offspring like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore. May he himself protect and defend you throughout all the days of your life and lead you into the kingdom of his glory. Amen.

May the eternal Creator look upon you, preserve in you the grace that he has poured over you, guide your mind, direct your ways, enlighten your thoughts toward what is good, strengthen and confirm you, forgive past sins, and protect and defend you in the present and the future. May the hand of the Lord be your helper, and may his holy arm grant you assistance throughout all the days of your life. Amen.

May the Lord bless our hearts and bodies and grant us blessing, as Isaac blessed Jacob. May the hand of the Lord be upon us; may he send his guardian angel, who will guard us in all our ways and perfect our steps, so that our footprints may not be moved. May he protect and defend us outwardly and strengthen and confirm us inwardly in every good thing and in happiness. Amen.

## Collect to Be Said over Judgment

Almighty and eternal God, who by an unchangeable disposition decree your judgments as a just judge everywhere, in this judgment of yours, graciously declare, at the invocation of your holy name, what the intention of the faithful implores from you, through your most just examination. Through [you].

[Note: [Col. 0461D] This agrees in certain respects with the blessing of water that Martène presents from an old manuscript of the monastery of Utica in *De antiquis Ecclesiae ritibus*, vol. III, p. [Col. 0462D] 467, and with another on p. 474 and p. 482.]

Likewise, another prayer. God, just, strong, and patient judge, who are the author of peace and judge equity: judge what is just, Lord, and your judgment is right—you who look upon the earth and make it tremble. You, almighty God, who through the coming of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, saved the world and through his most holy passion redeemed the human race: sanctify this water boiling with fire, or this heated iron. You who, when King Nebuchadnezzar commanded it, saved the three young men—namely Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—unharmed in the furnace, in the fiery kiln, and brought them out through your angel.

You, most holy and merciful ruler, grant that if an innocent person places his hand in this water boiling with fire, or upon this heated iron, concerning this theft or sexual offense, just as you delivered the three young men mentioned above from the fiery furnace and freed Susanna from a false accusation, so may he withdraw his hand from this water boiling with fire or from the heated iron safe and unharmed.

But if, with the devil aggravating his guilt, he presumes with a hardened heart to place his hand in this water boiling with fire or upon this heated iron, may your most just truth reveal this and manifest your truth in his body, so that his soul may be saved through repentance. And if the guilty person wishes to conceal his sins through any magic or herbs, may your right hand deign to bring this to nothing. Through your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, who with you lives and reigns as God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

[Note: [Col. 0462D] These prayers are also inserted for the canonical hours in the *Prayer Book of Charles the Bald*, pp. 24–25.]

# Prayers for the Canonical Hours

## Prayer at Prime

God, who by your grace have brought us to the beginning of this day, save us by your power, so that on this day we may turn aside toward no sin, but that our words may always proceed toward doing your righteousness. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0463A]

## Prayer at Terce

Lord God Jesus Christ, who at the third hour of the day were led to the cross of your passion for the salvation of the world, we humbly beseech you to blot out our sins, so that concerning our past evils we may always find forgiveness and concerning those to come may continually have protection. You who live …

## Prayer at Sext

Lord God Jesus Christ, who at the sixth hour ascended the wood of the cross for the redemption of the world, so that the whole world, which was in darkness, might be enlightened, we humbly beseech you always to grant that light to our mind and body by which we may deserve to reach eternal life. You who live …

## Prayer at None

Lord God Christ Jesus, who at the ninth hour caused the penitent thief to pass from the gibbet of the cross [Col. 0463B] into the glory of paradise, we humbly beseech you to cause us, after our death, to enter joyfully through the gates of paradise. You who live and reign.

# Prayers of the Holy Cross

Be present, merciful and compassionate God, to your family, so that you may hear our prayers in adversity and prosperity; and through the help of the holy cross deign to crush the wickedness of our adversaries, so that they may be able to reach the harbor of your salvation. Through our Lord Jesus.

God, to whom all creatures obey, and by whose wisdom you made all things through your Word, we humbly beseech your ineffable mercy: you who deigned to redeem us through the wood of your Son’s holy cross by his devoted blood, you who are the tree of life and restorer of paradise, extinguish the serpent’s deadly poisons in all who believe in you, and through the grace of the Holy Spirit continually pour out the cup of salvation. Through [you].

# Prayers to Be Said at the Cross

From all guilt and dangers graciously absolve us, Lord, we beseech you, whom you have deigned to redeem through the wood of the holy cross. You who live and reign.

Guard, we beseech you, Lord, the people who implore you with your right hand, and through the glorious passion of your Son may it absolve them from all sins. Through our Lord.

## 20.

May your mercy, God, through the power of the holy cross, guard us from every adversity and restore us with everlasting remedies. Through the Lord.

Be present to our supplications, almighty God, and defend everywhere from every adversity [Col. 0463D] and sin those whom you have redeemed by the triumph of the cross. You who …

Grant, we beseech you, almighty and merciful God, that through the power of the holy cross we may be freed from every adversity of mind and body. Through our Lord Jesus.

We beseech you, almighty God, that we may be freed from every tribulation, whom you have redeemed through the passion of your Son. You who are with the Father …

Absolve, we beseech you, Lord, the bonds of our sins, and guard us everywhere by the power of the holy cross. Through [you].

Drive away by the power of the holy cross our sins by which we are attacked, Lord, and by your mercy defend us from every adversity. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0464A]

Guard us, we beseech you, Lord, with your protection, and absolve us from all sins by the standard of the life-giving cross, through you, Jesus Christ, who by the trophy of the holy cross deigned to redeem the world. Graciously grant that we who rejoice in redemption may, by your gift, deserve to enjoy eternal joys. You who live …

# Prayers of Holy Mary

Grant that we, your servants, we beseech you, Lord God, may rejoice in perpetual health of mind and body, and through the glorious intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin be freed from present sorrow and enjoy future joy. Through the Lord.

May almighty God protect his servants from every danger by the right hand of his power, and, with blessed Mary ever-virgin interceding, cause them to rejoice in present and future prosperity. Through [you].

Stretch out your right hand to us, and through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary, ever-virgin Mother of God, grant us the help of heavenly power. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Protect your servants, Lord, by the aids of peace and the patronage of blessed Mary; make those who confess you secure from every enemy. Through the Lord.

May the merits of blessed and glorious Mary, ever-virgin Mother of God, accompany us, Lord, we beseech you, and may they always implore your indulgence for us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who …

# Blessing of Canons

[Col. 0464C]

Grant, Lord, we beseech you, that the doors of your grace may be opened to your servants who renounce worldly pomp and flee beneath the name of Christ after despising the devil. Command that those who come to you be received with a serene countenance, lest the enemy prevail over them. Grant them the tireless arm of your help; surround their minds with the breastplate of faith; and, [perhaps: “so that”] enclosed by a fortunate wall, may they rejoice that they have escaped the world. Through our Lord.

# Prayer over the Weekly Servants

God, to whom the vows of humble souls are always acceptable, look favorably upon the service of these your servants, our brothers, and cause them to attain your grace, so that, because they have now completed the services of this week with devoted mind, they may obtain the fullest and most abundant forgiveness. Through our Lord Jesus.

Merciful and most devout God, who everywhere protect and help your servants, increase the vow of these your servants, our brothers; enlarge their desire, so that they may rightly render service to their brothers. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

# Prayers for the Washing of Feet

Be present, Lord, to the duty of our service, because you deigned to wash the feet of your disciples. Do not despise the work of your hands, which you commanded us to observe, so that, just as outward impurities are washed here, so the sins within all of us may be washed away by you. May you yourself grant this.

[Col. 0465A]

God, who, washing the feet of your disciples, gave them an example through devoted affection and gave them a commandment, graciously grant that through obedience to your commands we may, by their intercession, rejoice forever in the sight of you. You who live and reign.

[Col. 0465]

## 21. SECOND OPUSCULE. A BOOK ON THE USE OF THE PSALMS, WITH VARIOUS FORMULAS ADAPTED TO DAILY AFFAIRS. (G)*

### FIRST PART

This work, this poem that you see along the path, reader, Alcuin made for the honor of the Lord.

[Col. 0465]

[Note: [Col. 0465] This preface does not belong with the following little book, but with another, *Offices for the Weekdays*.]

# PREFACE

[Col. 0465B]

The spirit of prophecy is not always present to the minds of prophets, so that, since they do not always possess it, when they do possess it they may recognize that they have it as a gift. Thus the prophet Elisha, when he was questioned about future events and acknowledged that the spirit of prophecy was lacking to him, had a harpist brought in, so that the spirit of prophecy might descend upon him through the praise of psalmody [Quercetanus reads *spalmodiae spalmis*, an anomalous phrase perhaps meaning “psalmody with psalms”; likewise throughout] and fill his mind concerning future things (2 Kings 3:15).

For when the voice of psalmody is produced through the concentration of the heart, by means of it a path to the heart is prepared for almighty God, so that he may pour into the attentive mind either the mysteries of prophecy or the grace of compunction. Thus it is written: “The sacrifice of praise will honor me, and there is the path by which I will show him the salvation of God” [Col. 0465C] (Psalm 49:23). In the sacrifice, therefore, of divine praise, a path of revelation to Jesus is made, because when compunction is poured out through psalmody, a way is made in our heart by which we may come to Jesus.

It is fitting, indeed, that the mind cleanse itself from all present things as far as it is able and cling to divine praises and spiritual things, so that heavenly realities may be revealed to it. In this mortal life there is nothing by which we can cling more familiarly to God than by praising him. Therefore no mortal can explain, either in word or in mind, the power of the psalms when they are sung in praise of almighty God—not merely on the surface of the lips, but with an attentive mind [another reading: *qui non*, “who do not”].

In the psalms, therefore, if you search them with an attentive mind and reach spiritual understanding, you will find the incarnation, passion, resurrection, and ascension of the Lord Word. In the psalms you will find such intimate prayer, if you search them with an attentive mind, as you could in no way devise entirely by yourself. In the psalms you will find intimate confession of your sins and a complete supplication for divine and lordly mercy.

In the psalms also you will find intimate thanksgiving for everything that happens to you. In the psalms you confess your weakness and misery, and by that very confession you call forth the mercy of God toward you. You will find every virtue in the psalms, if you deserve from God that he reveal to you the secrets of the psalms. [Col. 0466B]

# First Use of the Psalms

If you wish to do penance for your sins and ask forgiveness for your offenses by confessing your sins, sing, as attentively as you can—not with a display of words, but by reflecting and searching with your mind—seven Davidic psalms, whose openings are two beginning “Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger,” and two “Lord, hear me”; “Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven”; “Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy”; and “Out of the depths.” And you will very quickly find the mercy of God.

# Second Use

If you wish to illumine your mind with spiritual joy and gladness and to promise yourself great hope in God’s indulgence; and if you wish to pray, direct your mind toward the power of the psalms whose openings are: “Hear, Lord, my justice”; “To you, Lord, I have lifted up”; “O God, in your name”; “May God have mercy on us”; “O God, come to my assistance”; “In you, Lord, I have hoped” [the Cologne edition adds: “LXX”]; “Incline, Lord.”

You will in no way be able, in your own language or with human understanding, to express your misery, tribulation, and distress amid various temptations as perfectly as in these psalms and others like them, or to implore his mercy.

# Third Use

If you wish to praise almighty God and give thanks for his majesty and for all his benefits, by which from the beginning of the world in the Old Testament he showed mercy to the patriarchs and prophets of the human race, and in the New Testament through the incarnation of his eternal Son: sing those psalms whose title is “Praise the Lord” (*Alleluia*) and whose opening is “Vel” [uncertain reading]. And you will offer almighty God a gift sweeter than every honey and honeycomb if in these psalms you continually praise and magnify him.

Or: Psalms 71, 72, and 73; “The Lord said,” and so forth, through “To the Lord, when I was in distress”; “Give thanks to the Lord”; “Praise the Lord, O my soul”; “Praise the Lord, for he is good”; “Praise Jerusalem”; [Col. 0467A] “Praise the Lord from the heavens,” through “Let every spirit praise the Lord.”

# Fourth Use

If you are afflicted by various temptations and are constrained on every side by either human or spiritual temptations, and you seem to yourself to have been abandoned by God—who often abandons his saints for a time so that they may be tested—and for that reason the temptation seems greater than you can bear, sing with your inmost mind those psalms whose opening is: “O God, my God, look upon me”; “Hear, O God, my prayer when I plead”; “Save me, O God.” And the merciful God will immediately help you and enable you to endure the temptation you are suffering.

# Fifth Use

If the present life has become wearisome to you, and your mind delights in contemplating the heavenly homeland and in seeking almighty God with ardent desire, sing with attentive mind these psalms: “As the deer longs”; “How beloved”; “O God, my God.” And the merciful God will quickly console your mind.

# Sixth Use

If you understand that you have been abandoned by God in your tribulations, sing with a contrite heart these psalms: “How long, Lord”; “O God, we have heard with our ears”; “Have mercy on me, O God”; “Hear, O God, my prayer, and do not despise it”; “In you, Lord, I have hoped.” And God will immediately gladden you in all your distresses.

# Seventh Use

After receiving rest, and in a time of prosperity, sing these psalms in praise: “I will bless the Lord”; [Col. 0467C] “Bless the Lord, O my soul”; and “I will exalt you, my God and king.” And at all times, whether in prosperity or adversity, always sing the Hymn of the Three Young Men. No one can explain the power of this name, in which every creature is summoned to praise the Creator.

# Eighth Use

If you wish to exercise yourself inwardly in divine praises, precepts, and heavenly commandments, sing the psalm “Blessed are the undefiled in the way.” And although you contemplate and search out the power of this psalm until the end of your life, you will never, I think, be able to understand it perfectly.

There is no verse in it that does not contain either the way of God, or a law, or a commandment, or a precept of God, or words, or ordinances, [Col. 0467D] or judgments, or teachings. Therefore there is no need for you to spread your mind through different books.

# Ninth Use

In the Psalter, until the end of your life, you have material for reading, searching, and teaching. In it you will find the prophetic, evangelical, apostolic, and all the divine books treated and described spiritually, or [perhaps: “and intelligibly”] in part; and there you will find the first and second coming of the Lord foretold.

You will also find in the psalms the Lord’s incarnation, passion, resurrection, and ascension, and all the power of the divine sayings, if you search with your inmost mind [Col. 0468A] and by God’s grace reach the marrow of inner understanding.

## I. A Brief Form of Private Prayer: What It Is Fitting to Pray

Let us imitate the holy Church, whose members we are. She herself says: “On my bed by night I sought him whom my soul loves” (Song 3:1). And this to the Lord: “I remembered you upon my bed” (Psalm 62:7).

Therefore, when you awaken from sleep and trace the sign of the cross upon your lips, repeat three times: “Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise.” Immediately add the third psalm: “Lord, how they have multiplied.” And the twenty-fourth: “To you, Lord, I have lifted up.” And eight verses of the hundred-and-eighteenth psalm [Col. 0468B], whose opening is: “My soul clings to the dust.”

Then: “Lord, have mercy” (*Kyrie eleison*); the Lord’s Prayer; “Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth”; the Apostles’ Creed; “Bless the Lord, all works of the Lord”; “We praise you, O God”; “Praise is fitting for you.” At this verse you should rise. “For your name’s sake, Lord”; “Be my support, my refuge, and my guide, Lord my God.” As soon as you enter the church, you will be able to adore the holy Trinity in these words.

### Another Prayer

Lord God almighty, eternal and ineffable, without end or beginning, whom we confess to be one in Trinity and threefold in unity: you alone I adore, you I praise, you I bless, and you I glorify.

To you, O merciful and gracious one, I give thanks, because you have granted me, stripped of the night of unbelief and error, to become a participant in your grace. Complete, I beseech you, Lord, the work of your mercy begun in me. Grant me always to think, speak, and do what is pleasing to you; and, guarding me everywhere by your freely given goodness, make me, unworthy and miserable as I am, reach your vision. Amen.

## II. That It Is Good for a Person to Praise the Lord Every Day in the Four Psalms and Three Hymns Listed Below

The divinely inspired Scripture exhorts us, saying: “You who fear the Lord, bless the Lord” (Psalm 134:20). Nor should we be frightened by what is written: “Praise is not beautiful in the mouth of a sinner” (Sirach 15:9), for to be silent about the praise of the Creator is much worse.

Although many psalms are suitable for this work, in these you can diligently render praise to God in the following manner. After the opening verse, “O God, come to my assistance,” let the psalm follow: “Praise the name of the Lord; praise him, servants of the Lord,” in which, with the names of many false gods rejected, the one great and true God is praised.

“Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me,” and so forth, a psalm full of numerous virtues and praises. “I will exalt you, my God and king,” David’s most delightful and sweetest praise of the Lord. “Praise the Lord from the heavens,” in which all creatures are invited to praise the Creator of all things. The Hymn of the Three Young Men is dearer to God than every praise; in it all creatures, both together and individually, are urged to praise the Creator.

“We praise you, O God,” inferior to no praise. “A hymn is fitting for you.”

### Verses after the Lord’s Prayer

May almighty and merciful God bless us, he who made heaven and earth. We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit; we praise and exalt him above all forever.

Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers, and worthy of praise and glorious is your name forever. You who fear the Lord, bless the Lord; blessed is the Lord from Zion, who dwells in Jerusalem.

Sing to the Lord and bless his name; proclaim his salvation from day to day. We who live bless the Lord, from this time forth and forever.

Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who alone has done great wonders; and blessed is his majestic name forever and throughout the age of the age.

I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise is always in my mouth. I will praise the name of my God with a song and magnify him in praise.

Let the heavens and earth, the sea, and all that is in them praise him. I will sing to the Lord throughout my life; I will sing psalms to my God as long as I exist.

May my praise be pleasing to him, while I rejoice in the Lord. May the glory of the Lord be forever and ever; may the Lord rejoice in his works.

My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord, and let all flesh bless his holy name forever and throughout the age of the age.

Blessed be the name of the Lord, from this time forth and forever.

# Thanksgiving
[Col. 0469C] I give thanks to you, Lord God almighty, whose mercy is infinite, because through the water of holy baptism and the renewal of the Holy Spirit you have freed me from the bonds of original sin. I give thanks to you, who have enabled me rightly to believe in you and have deigned to join me to the number of your faithful. I praise and glorify you, most merciful Lord, because, although I was rushing headlong through every kind of crime, you did not allow me to perish; rather, graciously calling me back and rescuing me from the depth of my iniquity, you led me to repentance. I praise and glorify you, who have thus far freed me from destruction by eternal death, from punishments, and from the torments of this flesh, in which I deserve to be afflicted. I offer you praise and thanks, because, after removing me from many deaths, many disgraces, calamities, and miseries, from the most savage snares of the devil, and from unclean desires, [Col. 0469D] breaking the bonds by which I was held fast, you have deigned to lead me into your service. I offer you praise and thanks, because, rescuing me from the storms of quarrels, you grant me to enjoy the love of your servants, and bestow upon me bodily health and peace of mind. To you, Lord, I sing praise, honor, and glory, because every day, without ceasing, although I continue to sin and set aside your commandments, you still await my amendment with such great patience.

I beg you, my Lord God, who have deigned to bestow your mercy upon me up to this present hour: complete the work of your mercy. Free me from all the evils that oppress me, as you have begun; save me to the end through Jesus Christ, [Col. 0470A] our Savior and Redeemer, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

Thanks be to God, thanks be to God, thanks be to God.

Blessed is the glory of the Lord from his dwelling-place.

## III. Repentance and the Lamentation of Public Penitence

We read concerning the Lord Christ that he spent the night in prayer (Luke 6:12). What then are we doing, conceived in iniquities and sins, as we pamper ourselves delicately in bed, if he spent the night in prayer—he who was wholly free from every contagion of sin? Let us therefore examine our ways and make a twofold lament in repentance in this world: plainly, because [Col. 0470B] we have both failed to do the good that we ought to have done and have done the evil that we ought not to have done.

Moreover, let us sing with diligent alternation these seven Davidic psalms, which nearly all spiritual men have assigned as especially suitable for repentance, namely: “Have mercy on me, O God”; “O Lord, rebuke me not in your anger”; “Blessed are those whose”; “O Lord, rebuke me not in your anger . . . for your arrows,” etc.; “O Lord, hear my prayer, and my cry”; “Out of the depths”; “O Lord, hear my prayer, with your ears.”

### Verses after the Lord’s Prayer

I said, “Lord, have mercy on me, for my iniquities have risen above my head; they have multiplied beyond the hairs of my head.” Where shall I go from your Spirit? Rescue me from my enemies, my God. Receive me according to your word. Cleanse me from my hidden faults, O Lord. For your name’s sake, Lord, you will be gracious to my sin. For I acknowledge my iniquity. My sin is known [Supplement: “I have committed it against you”]. Be my helper; do not abandon me. For you are my patience. You are my helper.

Blessed be the name of the Lord.

### [Another version: “The following”] Confession of Sins

To you, Lord God, I confess my crimes and sins. Because of your ineffable goodness and mercy, receive, I beg you, my confession; indeed, grant that I may confess with my whole heart. For you, most merciful Lord, have deigned to say: “I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he should turn and live” (Ezekiel 33:11).

I, wretched man, serve without ceasing the vices of gluttony, drunkenness, and excess; because of this my soul [Col. 0470D] and my body are weighed down. Hence, drowsy and sluggish, I hurry late to prayers and duties, and always stand before them distracted and negligent. I have rotted through fornications and the filth of lust, and am wholly polluted within and without. My mouth is defiled, as are my lips, my eyes, and my ears; my taste, smell, and touch alike are polluted, and even to this hour my heart is stained by vain and filthy thoughts.

I am sunk in sadness, dissolved in listlessness, inflamed by the torches of anger, consumed by the fire of greed, infected by the poisons of envy, poisoned by hatred of my brother, convulsed by slander, made putrid by every kind of malice, dulled by forgetfulness and laziness; overwhelmed by fraud and hypocrisy, weakened by frailty and negligence, [Col. 0471A] stained by perjuries, falsehood, and lies, and swollen with the lightness of empty glory.

Often I have despised the commands of my superiors. Often I have rebelled and murmured. Often, with a swollen heart, I have offered false excuses. I have promised to amend these and similar evils, yet I always fall back into the same things. Because of these sins I sought the monastery, but I am always becoming worse there. Without ceasing I despise your commandments. Every moment I violate my promises by which I vowed to examine [Alternative: “to observe”] the holy Rule. Always wretched, I hurry toward buffoonery, idle talk, and idleness.

Alas for me! How many impieties, how many blasphemies, how many different darknesses tear my mind apart! Unless your ineffable goodness mercifully drive them all away and wipe them out, [Col. 0471B] my soul is dead in sins.

Many are the evils into which I have fallen through ignorance; many are those that have slipped from my mind. Innumerable altogether are the evils that I, miserable man, have committed, and I cannot recount how many. For all of them, eternal torments, worms, and fire are prepared for me, lost as I am.

Come to my aid, Lord Jesus Christ, most wretched and captive that I am; do not allow me to perish, since you have deigned to redeem me with your precious blood. Do not destroy me together with my sins, nor preserve my evils forever. Do not cast me away from your presence; do not despise me or confound me, a sinner against you. Remember your mercies. You who do great and wondrous things beyond number, save me by your gratuitous gift.

You who did not reject the tax collector, do not reject me. You who helped the thief hanging on the cross, help me. You who had mercy on the sinful woman weeping at your feet, have mercy on me. To you belongs, with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, equal honor in the divine substance [Perhaps something is missing: “one”], and equal glory forever and ever. Amen.

### Another Prayer concerning the Confession of Sins

Almighty and merciful God, essentially good alone: whether he wills or not, the thought of a human being will confess to you (Psalm 75:11). But I too willingly confess that I have sinned and acted impiously in your sight, according to all the abominations that the wicked are accustomed to commit. Yet by the greatness of your mercy the greatness of my sins is overcome. For your mercy is greater than the sins of the whole world, and therefore hope of pardon remains for me, because certainty of mercy remains for me [The word “all” is redundant].

Having therefore washed away the filth of my past, grant me both the will and the power to cut away the causes of my present evils and henceforth to give no entrance to their suggestions. I ask that you not deny me a suitable place and time, nor worthy fruits of repentance.

It is certain that he [Perhaps: “for it is certain that”] brings your joy to fulfillment for the salvation of mortals—you who do not will the sinner’s death, but that he should turn and live with you, O God who live and reign in three persons forever and ever. Amen.

## IV. [Note: “In earlier editions this rubric or title appears to have been omitted; it has here been supplied by us.”] Supplication for Grace to Attain Every Virtue and Amend the Opposing Vices

[Col. 0472A]

Truth promises us—and surely it does not know how to lie: “Knock, and it will be opened to you” (Matthew 7:7). Let us therefore knock at the door of the psalms, so that he may open it for us, he who dwells in the psalms. For he himself is the door, and he himself is the doorkeeper.

Moreover, let us diligently examine these seven psalms that are to be sung, and we shall see that they can accomplish more in prayer than human speech is capable of expressing. In them are the sweetest love of the divine law, the most steadfast hope of attaining the other life, strong weapons against spiritual battles, and a unique refuge in tribulation.
