They drive away temporal fear and sadness and cheer the mind with spiritual delight and joy:

“Hear, O Lord, my justice”; “To you, O Lord, I have lifted”; “The Lord is my light”; “In you, O Lord, I have hoped”; “O God, in you I have hoped, Lord”; “Incline, O Lord, your ear” [Note: “The seventh psalm is missing here.”]

### Verses after the Lord’s Prayer

Guard my soul and rescue me, Lord; let me not be put to shame, for I have called upon you. Let those who slander my soul be put to shame and fail; let those who seek evil for me be covered with shame and disgrace. Arise, Lord, go before them and overthrow them; rescue my soul from the wicked, and the sword of my enemies from your hand.

My God, rescue me from the hand of the sinner, and from the hand of the lawless and unjust. Attend to my soul and deliver it; rescue me from my enemies. Be for me a protecting God and a fortified place, [Col. 0472C] so that you may save me.

Hear, Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to you; have mercy on me and hear me. Hear, Lord, the voice of my supplication, while I pray to you and lift up my hands toward your holy temple. Let my prayer enter your presence; incline your ear to my supplication, Lord. Let my petition enter your presence, Lord; according to your word, rescue me.

Rescue me, Lord, from the evil man; free me from the violent man. Rescue me from those who practice iniquity, and save me from men of blood. Let my enemies turn back on whatever day I call upon you; behold, I have known that you are my God. Deal with me, Lord, for good, as a sign, so that those who hate me may see and be confounded.

Blessed be the name of the Lord, from this [Col. 0472D] time forth and forever.

### Petition

Grant me, Lord, the spirit to seek you with the whole intention of my heart; then, to ask for worthy things; finally, to obtain the fulfillment of my petitions. Strip me of past sins, guard me from those that threaten, fortify me against those to come.

Grant me suitable abstinence from food and drink, the belt of chastity, purity of heart and lips. Bestow upon me patience, forbearance, kindness, modesty, spiritual joy, and perfect contempt for the world. Grant that I give [no one] occasion for scandal, that I love simplicity [Col. 0473A] and purity, and earnestly pursue the things that make for peace.

Put hypocrisy far from me; grant me true humility, full confession, and perfect amendment. Remove from my tongue the habit of swearing, the fog of lies, the plague of slander, the gluttony of murmuring, and the vanity of buffoonery and foolish talk.

Set a guard over my mouth and a door of restraint for my lips. Grant me, I beg you, to submit to the commands of my superiors and, with a cheerful heart, hasten without delay to obedience, compassion, and concord.

Give me discernment in all things, so that I may distinguish between good and evil, exhort the good toward better things, and recall those who walk perversely to the line of your righteousness. Awaken my sluggishness and my laziness by your goads, and make me [Col. 0473B] persevere vigorously in your commandments and praises.

Grant me prudence, justice, courage, and temperance. Bestow upon me right faith, unshaken hope, and perfect charity. Pour into my heart the spirit of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and fortitude, of knowledge and piety, and of your fear.

Grant me, Lord, a blessing from the dew of heaven and from the richness of the earth; give me the upper irrigation and the lower irrigation. Grant that my wretched soul may melt in the fire of your charity; make me be wholly consumed by desire for you [Perhaps: “by your desire”] and extinguished to the world.

Grant me always to have a contrite and humbled heart before you. Grant that, in your sight, I may become a living sacrifice through the fire of compunction.

Highest eternal light, illumine me. Highest eternal power, free me. [Col. 0473C] Highest eternal strength, strengthen me. Highest eternal wisdom, drive away the darkness of my ignorance. Highest eternal mercy, have mercy on me.

Grant that with my whole heart, my whole soul, and all my strength I may always seek your face. And in your mercy lead me to your most holy vision.

May the loving protection of your blessed angels be with me, I beg you; and grant that the most blessed hosts of your saints may intercede for me before you. Grant me, most frail as I am, to follow and imitate the footsteps of your beloved one, my father Benedict, so that I may deserve to obtain your mercy and reach the promised joys.

Through Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit throughout endless ages. Amen.

### Another Prayer to the Father in the Name of the Son

[Col. 0473D]

Ineffable God, of uncircumscribed nature, founder of all things, and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who sent that same beloved Son from your bosom into our public sphere [reading uncertain] to assume our life, so that he might give us his own, and that he might be perfect God from the Father and perfect man from his mother, wholly God and wholly man; one and the same Christ, eternal and temporal, immortal and destined to die, creator and created, strong and weak, nourisher and nourished, Shepherd and sheep, dead in time yet living with you forever, who gave his lovers citizenship in life and promised it to them, saying: “Whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give [the text reads *adbit*] you” (John 14:13).

I beseech you to grant me, together with that same Son of yours, to bless and glorify you in all things, because where there is one substance, there is one gift. Grant me also through him and with him forgiveness of all sins and observance of your commandments; love of you and brotherly love; strong weapons against the devil and perfect charity toward the brethren; moderation in food and drink and continence from lust; chaste hearing and a simple gaze; purity of heart and cleanliness of body; a pure thought and custody of mouth and heart, so that my heart may neither conceive iniquity within nor my tongue give birth to it outside; so that I may neither speak falsehood nor be silent about truth, neither conceal what brings salvation nor utter what brings death.

I therefore pray that you grant me constancy in prayer and regularity in reading, so that I may read your commandments tirelessly, love them insatiably, fulfill them effectively, and correct whatever I discover to be perverse in myself; that I may hold fast what is upright, set right what is deformed, cultivate what is beautiful, preserve what is sound, and strengthen what is weak.

Grant me also to despise temporal things and love eternal things, so that I may regard the world as dead to me; neither rejoicing nor grieving over temporal matters, so that I may neither fear nor love anything temporal, neither be corrupted by flatteries nor shaken by adversities.

And because your only-begotten one himself said: “No one comes to me unless the Father who sent me draws him” (John 6:44), I beseech and humbly ask you, Lord: draw me to him, and may he lead me to you, to that place where there is [Col. 0474C] everlasting and eternally blessed life; eternal security and secure tranquillity; blessed eternity and eternal blessedness; where there is perfect love and no fear; where there is an eternal day and one spirit among all; where you, with him, and he, with you, live and reign eternally and forever in communion with the Holy Spirit, O God.

Throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

## V. For Contemplation and the Desire for the Heavenly Homeland, Which Is Perceived Only by Those Who Despise the World

The blessed Apostle admonishes us, saying: “If you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God” (Colossians 3:1). And again: “Our citizenship is in heaven” (Philippians 3:20).

If, then, our citizenship is in heaven, let us mourn during this troubled journey, as long as we are exiles from our homeland. Let us rise on the small wings of contemplation above all things that began in time and come to an end with time; and let us fly in spirit with every desire toward that homeland to which one travels in time but in which one lives beyond time.

To kindle our desires, therefore, let us sing daily in spirit and mind these five psalms: “As the deer”; “Judge me, O God, and distinguish”; “Praise befits you, O God”; “How lovely are”; “With my voice I cried to the Lord; with my voice to the Lord.” These also console and lift up the mind in tribulation.

### Verses after the Lord’s Prayer

[Col. 0475A]

Praise befits you, O God, in Zion, and the vow shall be paid to you in Jerusalem. For there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord, a testimony for Israel, to confess your name.

Lord, hear my prayer; let every prayer come to you. Blessed is the one whom you have chosen and taken up; he shall dwell in your courts. Alas for me, that my exile has been prolonged! I have dwelt with the inhabitants of Kedar; my soul has been a long-time exile.

My soul refused consolation; I remembered God and was delighted. My heart and my flesh have failed; God is the God of my heart and my portion forever. For what remains for me in heaven, and what have I desired from you upon earth? For I am an exile with you on earth, and a pilgrim like all my fathers.

My soul thirsted for you [Col. 0475B] in many ways, and so did my flesh. Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house and the place of the dwelling of your glory. Hold my right hand, guide me according to your will, and receive me with glory.

That I may see the will of the Lord and be protected by his holy temple; that I may hear the voice of your praise and recount all your wonders; and that I may dwell in the house of the Lord for length of days.

But I shall appear in your presence with righteousness; I shall be satisfied when your glory is revealed. Lord my God, I shall confess you forever.

Blessed be the name of the Lord, from this time forth and forever.

### Confession of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit

I shall confess you, Lord, King of heaven and earth, and honor you with a sacrifice of praise. Since outward gifts are lacking to me, I shall return to you the vows of praise that are within me.

With my whole heart I believe, and with my mouth I confess, the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit: a trinity in persons and a unity in substance; not a body or something placed in a body, nor formed from different species or mixed together, nor fashioned from the joints of limbs, but of one, simple, incorporeal, and invisible nature.

There is nothing in you greater or lower, but in every way and in every respect you are perfect, without deformity; great without quantity; good without quality; everlasting without time; life without death; strong without weakness; truth without falsehood; wholly everywhere without place; present everywhere without position; filling all things without extension; everywhere encountering all things without contraction; transcending all things without movement; remaining beneath all things without fixed location; creating all things without need; governing all things without labor; giving all things their beginning without having a beginning of your own; making all mutable things mutable without changing yourself [Alternative: “without changing you”].

Infinite in greatness, omnipotent in power, supreme in goodness, beyond estimation in wisdom, awesome in counsels, just in judgments, most secret in thoughts, truthful in words, holy in works, abundant in mercies, most patient toward those who sin, compassionate toward those who endure; always the same, eternal and everlasting, immortal and unchangeable.

You are not enlarged by expanses, nor confined by the smallness of places, nor restricted by any receptacles, [Col. 0476A] nor altered by will, nor corrupted by necessity, nor disturbed by sad things, nor delighted by joyful things. Forgetfulness does not remove anything from you, nor does memory restore anything to you; past things do not pass away from you, nor do future things succeed to you. Neither origin gives you a beginning, nor times an increase, nor calamity an end; rather, before the ages, in the ages, and throughout the ages, you live forever.

And to you belong perennial praise and eternal glory, supreme power and unique honor, perpetual kingship and dominion without end, throughout the tireless and immortal ages of ages. Amen.

## VI. For Preserving Humility and Recognizing Human Frailty

Scripture recalls us to the rule of humility when it commands: “The greater you are, humble yourself in all things” (Ecclesiasticus 3:20). How well Abraham knew the rule of humility! Although he could have been exalted by conversation with the Lord, he declared himself lowly and contemptible, saying: “I shall speak to my Lord, although I am dust and ashes” (Genesis 18:27).

Therefore, so that we may always think humbly of ourselves, let us daily recite before the Lord these psalms: “I said, I will guard”; “Is it not, Lord?” [That is: “Will it not be subject to God?”]; “Lord, my heart is not exalted.”

### Verses after the Lord’s Prayer

Remember, Lord, that we are dust; man is like grass—his days—and like the flower of the field, so he shall bloom. For the spirit will pass away from him, and he will be no more, [Col. 0476C] and he will no longer know his place. His spirit will go out, and he will return to his earth; on that day all their thoughts will perish.

I said in the ecstasy of my mind: “Every man is a liar.” Remember, Lord, what my substance is; for you did not establish the children of men in vain. Lord, what is man, that you have made yourself known to him, or the son of man, that you reckon him worthy of regard?

I have been humbled exceedingly, Lord; give me life according to your word. See my humility and rescue me, for I have not forgotten your law. The Lord guards the little ones; I was humbled, and he delivered me. But I am needy and poor; the Lord takes care of me.

Blessed be the name of the Lord, from this time forth and forever.

### Prayer

[Col. 0476D]

Lord Jesus Christ, who came into this world from the bosom of the Father for the sake of sinners, so that you might redeem us from that same sin—for I know and believe that you chose to dwell on earth not for the sake of the righteous but for sinners—hear me, Lord God, a sinner and guilty, unworthy, negligent, and liable to punishment.

To you I confess all my sins and all my evils, whatever I have done in this world, whether by my fault, my actions, or wicked thoughts; for all of them I ask pardon. I have sinned; I have sworn oaths; yet I have not denied you, because I know and believe that you are the Father. Forgive me, Christ.

I praise you, I magnify you, I glorify you, holy Trinity. I give you thanks in all my weaknesses, because I have no hope in anyone except [Col. 0477A] you, my God.

I flee to the harbor of your Church, Christ, and prostrate before the pledges of your saints, I ask pardon. I pray and beseech you, God, to deign, according to your mercy, to grant me mercy and loving-kindness until the end of my life, and in that dreadful hour when my soul is about to depart from my body.

Grant me right understanding, right faith, and true belief. Almighty God, my God, hear me, so that you may deign to free my soul from the lower hell. Almighty God, free me from infernal punishment. Almighty God, free me from unquenchable fire. Almighty God, free me from Satan, the first-formed one. Almighty God, free me from immortal worms. Almighty God, free me from the dwelling-place of the wicked. Almighty [Col. 0477B] God, free me from eternal anguish. Almighty God, free me from every evil. Almighty God, deign to free my soul from the outer darkness.

Because I trust in you, because I am the work of your hands, do not despise me, Christ. I ask our holy and most blessed mother Mary; I ask the twenty-four elders; I implore all your holy angels; I beseech all the holy patriarchs and prophets; I ask all your apostles, martyrs, confessors, and virgins. Likewise I invoke all your saints and God’s elect for my help.

And in that dreadful hour when my soul is about to leave my body, holy archangel, I implore you—you who have received authority to receive souls—to deign to receive my soul [Col. 0477C] when it departs from my body, and free it from the power of the enemy, so that I may pass through the gates of hell and the ways of darkness, so that the lion or dragon, accustomed to receive souls in hell and drag them away to eternal torments, may not oppose me [Perhaps: “set himself against me”].

I implore you, holy Peter, prince of the apostles, who hold the keys of the kingdom of heaven and have received authority to receive souls: deign to open for me the gate of paradise.

Lord Jesus Christ, Son of Mary, I submit my case to you, so that you may deal with my soul in pity and mercy, for I have hoped in you. Christ, Redeemer of the world, when shall I meet you? May I not be driven from your presence, since I deserve neither a crown nor forgiveness unless you deign to grant it to me.

May the holy Trinity be my helper. Hear me, Lord, who are my living God and my strength, the just judge. You are the most powerful physician. You are the priest forever. You are the guide to the homeland. You are my true light. You are my holy sweetness. You are my clear wisdom. You are my pure simplicity. You are my catholic [universal] soul. You are my peaceful harmony. You are my complete protection. You are my entire perfection. You are my everlasting salvation. You are my great mercy. You are my unstained life. You are my strongest patience. You are my accomplished redemption. You are my holy resurrection. You are everlasting life.

I ask you, I beseech you, that through you I may walk, reach you, rest in you, and rise again to you. Hear me, Lord.

Remember, Lord, David, as you swore to our fathers, so that you may turn your anger away from your servant. May the angel Michael, the angel Gabriel, the angel Raphael, all angels, all archangels, all thrones, all dominions, all principalities and powers, all patriarchs and prophets, all apostles and martyrs, all confessors and virgins stand by me for aid and assistance, through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Matthew, Mark, Luke, John. Holy [Col. 0478A] George, my servant [Perhaps: “servant of Christ”], intercede for me, your servant. Holy Christopher, intercede for me.

Lord, you formed me from the clay of the earth; you joined me together with bones and veins. Lord, in your loving-kindness save me. Peace is here; God is here.

Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you. For against you alone I have sinned and done evil before you, because my sins are exceedingly innumerable. [Col. 0478B] For these sins and negligences of mine I ask pardon, Lord: for empty glory, carnal desire, pleasure, pollution, murmuring, envy, pride, sleepiness, visions, my wicked thoughts, adultery, fornication, and for the fact that I come late to the work of God.

I can neither speak nor name my sins. I am guilty; I have not concealed my iniquities or my wickedness, because I know and believe that you are a merciful Father. Do not abandon me, merciful Father, but deign to forgive the evil I have done.

Come to my aid, merciful, invisible, sweet, and lovable one, before the gate of hell swallows me, before the portion of my enemy comes. Stretch out your hand to me and show me the light, so that no power of hell [Col. 0478C] may invade me in that hour when my soul is about to be taken [Perhaps: “is to be taken”] from my body.

Most compassionate God, merciful God, most clement God, I praise you, I magnify you, I give you thanks. You who saved me through the night, command that I be kept safe through the day. Make me, Lord, find your grace, love you, praise you and fear you, serve you, and love you all the days of my life.

God, to you I commend my life. Have mercy on me, Lord of glory, who are one and true, alone and just, and in whom all things and through whom all things have been made.

Hear me, Lord, as I pray, just as you heard the three youths from the furnace of blazing fire, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Hear me, Lord, as I pray, just as you heard Peter at sea and Paul in chains. Spare my soul; spare my evils and all [Col. 0478D] my crimes.

Christ my God, set yourself before me if my enemy rejoices against me. I shall sleep, and my heart shall keep watch. May your angels, Lord, guard me both by day and by night. Almighty God, send forth your good and upright Spirit, to guard my soul and my body.

I have sinned, Lord; I have sinned against the law of God in words, deeds, and thoughts. Many are my sins. I was negligent regarding the work of God and my order.

I pray you, blessed Virgin Mary, and all the saints of God: pray for me, a sinner. May almighty God have mercy on me, and may the Lord God grant true humility, true repentance, true forgiveness, sobriety, endurance, good faith, and good perseverance.

[Col. 0479A] May the Holy Spirit illumine me; may the Lord forgive me all my sins, here and in the future. Amen.

## VII. In the Temptations of Unclean Spirits

In demonic temptations the outstanding preacher consoles us, saying: “God is faithful, and he will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear; but with the temptation he will also provide a way out, so that you may be able to endure it” (1 Corinthians 10:13).

Accordingly, we must understand that there is a measure belonging to the hidden judgment: both when the storm of temptation breaks forth and when it subsides. Certainly, the Gospel bears witness that the demon could neither remain in the possessed man nor, unless commanded, presume again to invade the brute animals, saying: “If you cast us out, send us into the herd of pigs” (Matthew 8:31).

When, then, would this being dare of his own accord to harm human beings made in God’s image, if supreme power did not grant him permission? If it did not, he would not even be able to rage against pigs. Therefore, there is no doubt that, by permission of the most just Judge, the devil receives power for a time to tempt the elect. Yet the merciful Judge grants what the cruel enemy seizes.

Hence the Lord says concerning that same being to his faithful servant: “I shall not rouse him as a cruel one” (Job 41:1). Hence, when the faithful soul has been wearied by temptations, he refreshes it with gentle consolations, saying: “Your Lord God said: For a brief moment, for a little while, I abandoned you, but with great mercies I shall gather you. Again there: I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting mercy I have had mercy on you” (Isaiah 54:7–8).

Since, therefore, we temporarily fall under the will of the tempter, let us cry out from the depths, let us cry out boldly, before we slip into the abyss of pleasure or evil consent, singing these psalms: “O God, my God, look upon me”; “O God, in your name”; “Have mercy on me, Lord, for they have trampled me”; “O God, come to my aid”; “Lord God of my salvation”; “Rescue me, Lord, from the evil man.”

### Verses after the Lord’s Prayer

Hear, O God, my prayer when I am afflicted; rescue my soul from fear of the enemy. The troubles of my heart have multiplied; rescue me from my necessities. You have set my feet in a spacious place; have mercy on me, Lord, for I am afflicted.

Arise; why do you sleep, Lord? Arise, and do not cast us away forever. Do not hand me over to the desire of the sinner; they have plotted against me. Do not abandon me, lest we ever be exalted.

Arise, Lord; let man not prevail. Let the nations be judged in your presence. Arise, Lord my God; let your hand be exalted; do not forget the poor forever.

But you, Lord, do not put your help far from me; look upon me for my defense. Send forth your hand from on high; rescue me and free me from many waters and from the hand of foreign sons. For foreigners have risen up against me, and the strong have sought my soul; they have not set the Lord before their eyes.

And you, Lord, deal mercifully with me for your name’s sake, [Col. 0480A] for your mercy is sweet. Free me, for I am needy and poor, and my heart is troubled within me. Do not hand me over to the souls of those who persecute me, for unjust witnesses have risen against me.

Scatter them by your power and destroy them, my protector, Lord. Be my helper and deliverer, Lord; do not delay. And my tongue shall meditate upon your justice when those who seek evil for me have been confounded and put to shame.

Blessed be the name of the Lord, from this time forth and forever.

Lord God of hosts, restore us and show us your face, and we shall be saved. Arise, Lord, help us and free us for your name’s sake.

### Prayer
[Col. 0480B] Grant me, Lord, progress in seeking your law and remission of all sins, so that, while I desire with great longing to reach the light of your Scriptures, my eyes may not be darkened by any obscurity of sins. Draw me to yourself by the power of your omnipotence. Do not abandon me to wander according to my own will, whom you redeemed with your precious blood. Do not allow your image in me to become obscured; if it is defended by your gracious aid, it is always excellent. Do not let the devil overturn your gifts, because everything that strives to oppose you is altogether fragile. Hear me, merciful King, crying out over my sins, and remove them from me before you condemn me for them in your judgment. Why does my own iniquity lie in wait for me? Why do my offenses [Col. 0480C] contend against me? They desire to overthrow your creature, which does not subsist with any firmness of substance. Let the devil say, indeed, why does he pursue me with insatiable anguish? Did I give him the opportunity to become proud against you, Lord, and to fall from the blessed state in which he had been placed, when he possessed such distinguished power? Let it suffice him that he destroyed me in Adam. Why does the impious accuser pursue me with daily deceptions? And just as he fell from your grace through his own fault, why does he seek me also, in order to separate me from that same grace? Grant me, Lord, against the most cruel enemy, the merciful aid of your protection, so that, just as he never ceases to attack my frailty, he may likewise be compelled by your strength to depart in confusion. Do not permit, good King, the most savage enemy to fulfill his desires against me, [Col. 0480D] he who chose to offend you grievously. Why does he circle around me like a roaring lion? Why does he strive to devour me? Once, in holy baptism, I renounced him; once, I professed that I believed in you, Lord. Grant that I may be preserved by perpetual protection as the one whom, most high Creator, you made me through the water of regeneration. And because I have begun to be yours, let me know no other lord, so that, because I have been redeemed by your glory, I may, with your gift, fulfill your commandments. But if you abandon me, that trickster immediately attacks—the one who, tireless [Alternative: “unfailing”] and shameless, always stands ready, counting his profits in human ruin. He flatters in order to deceive; he incites in order to destroy. Above all, he deceives our souls through our body, and so spreads himself through human desires that he is perceived scarcely at all, [Col. 0481A] with no foresight and absolutely no judgment. It would take too long to go through everything. Who could resist such an enemy unless you, Lord, determined to oppose him? For what could he not do to me, since he dared to test you in my body through his treacherous contrivances? Hear me, guardian of human beings, and by your indulgence free me from him who strives to drag me to Gehenna. Let me have no share with him, so that I may have a share with you, Lord. Claim your handiwork from him who destroys it. Let him not cause others to be condemned, since he condemned himself; rather, let him perish with his own followers, he who hastens to destroy everything. But deliver me, the Almighty, and rescue me from the enemy of the human race, and lead me to eternal joys, where I may deserve to rejoice without end. Amen.

### VIII. On the various tribulations inflicted by human beings

[Col. 0481B]

“Call upon me,” says the Lord through the Prophet, “in the day of my tribulation [Reading: “your tribulation”], and I will rescue you” (Psalm 49:15). This promise of the Lord is sweeter to our mouth than milk and honey. Therefore, when we suffer tribulations from false brothers, let us call upon him who urges us to call upon him. For it is certain that he who wishes to be invoked wishes to hear. In these five suitable psalms, then, let us cry out to the Lord in the face of the one who troubles us:

“Save me, Lord, for the holy one has failed”;  
“Judge, Lord, those who harm me”;  
“Hear, God, my prayer, and do not despise my supplication”;  
“Deliver me from my enemies, my God”;  
“Save me, God, [Col. 0481C] for the waters have reached my soul”; and, further, “They gave gall for my food.”

As for the remaining words that follow, since they spiritually strike Christ’s slayers, we do not wish such destructive curses to be hurled against Christians.

**Verses as above. The prayer follows.**

Christ, Son of the living God, power and undivided majesty, the whole substance of my prayer: I invoke your holy name. Hear me as I struggle in my heart, acknowledging the sins of my crimes and confessing the offenses of my thoughts. Break, Lord, the devil’s schemes, by which, as other things creep in, he suggests one thing after another. For by this very means he captures prayer and turns it toward alienation. Look upon my tears, Lord; and when there are no [Col. 0481D] tears, pour them forth through the indulgence of your mercy. Preserve undefiled faith in me, and always reconcile me in peace with my neighbors. Distribute your fruits—bread and wine—by your own generosity. To you I incline my neck; to you I bend my knees. I confess you as my Lord, although you are one [Alternative: “living”], in the holy Trinity. Break, Lord, every power directed against me; raise me up when I lie fallen; and grant as requests those things that I cannot accomplish. Amen.

### IX. That it is most beneficial, after tribulation, to give thanks by reciting the five psalms for the joy received

Therefore, when the merciful Lord had said, “Call upon me in [Col. 0482A] the day of your tribulation, and I will rescue you” (the cited Psalm), seeking from us a debt of praise for that very rescue, he immediately added: “and you will honor me.” Hence David says: “My vows are upon me, O God; I will repay them to you with praise. For you have delivered my soul from death” (Psalm 55:12). Again he says: “For you have become my helper and my refuge; in the day of my tribulation, you have received me; I will sing psalms to you” (Psalm 58:18).

Therefore, when we have fallen into various temptations, whether from false brothers or from raging demons, hurling against both of them the darts of the divine word, and when we see that they have failed and that we have grown strong, let us at once raise the pure intention of our heart, our eyes, and our hands toward heaven, and in a voice of praise and confession bless him who sent from heaven, delivered [Col. 0482B] us, and gave those who trample us over to disgrace. With a concordant heart let us say to him:

“I will exalt you, Lord, for you have received me, and have not delighted my enemies over me.”

And, following the conscience [passage corrupt], let us continue to him to the end:

“I will bless the Lord at all times”;  
“Let all the earth rejoice in God”;  
“Sing a psalm to his name”;  
“Unless the Lord had been with us—let Israel say now”;  
“I will confess to you, Lord, with my whole heart, for you have heard all the words of my mouth.”

Yet consider, reader, and you will see clearly that in no psalms can thanks be rendered to the Lord better or more suitably after tribulation for joy received than in these five.

**Verses after the Lord’s Prayer**

“When I called upon you, you heard me, God of my righteousness; in tribulation you enlarged me. I will confess to you, Lord, with my whole heart; I will recount all your wonders. I will rejoice and exult in you, and sing a psalm to your name, Most High. My heart has exulted in your salvation; I will sing to the Lord, who has bestowed good things upon me, and I will sing a psalm to the name of the Most High. I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I will praise you. For you have regarded my lowliness; you have preserved my soul from troubles, and have not shut me into the hands of the enemy. I will confess to you, Lord, forever, because you have done this; and I will await your name, for it is good in the presence of your saints. You have protected me from the assembly of the malicious and from the multitude of those who work iniquity. Therefore I will confess to you among the peoples, Lord, and [Col. 0482D] I will sing a psalm to your name. God, your way is in the holy place; what god is great like our God? You are the God who alone works wonders. But I have always hoped in you, Lord, and I will add to all your praise. But for me it is good to cling to the Lord and to place my hope in the Lord God. Each day I will bless you, and I will praise your name forever and unto ages of ages. For you, Lord, have helped me and comforted me. Blessed be the name of the Lord, from this time forth and forever.”

**Prayer**

Blessed is your name, Lord God of our fathers, who, when you are angry, show mercy, [Col. 0483A] and in the time of tribulation forgive sins to those who invoke your name. To you, Lord, I turn my face; to you I confess all my sins. You know everything before it happens. You know that after baptism I despised your precepts and did not keep your commandments; and the good that I was able to do, I failed to do through negligence, while the evil that I ought not to have done, I committed through presumption. Through desire I committed many evils in sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch; in thought, speech, and deed. And what I promised in holy baptism before your angels and saints, I did not keep as I ought; nor did I fulfill it, but I consumed [Perhaps: “despised”] it, and I did not obey your commands as I ought [Note: [Col. 0483] In the Cologne edition: “And what I promised before the most holy altar, before you and before the angels . . . and I did not obey the command of my superior as I ought, etc.”]. Rather, through pride, anger, contempt, negligence, [Col. 0483B] doing my own will, murmuring, slandering, and judging, I incurred guilt. God, you know my foolishness, and my offenses are not hidden from you. Look upon me confessing my sins before you, and have mercy on me. Grant me to practice true repentance in this age, and in the future grant me pardon, because you deigned to say: “I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he should turn and live” (Ezekiel 33:11). Pour your mercy over me, and forgive all my sins, which my conscience fears, and add what my prayer does not presume to ask. Grant me perseverance in good works, so that, by your mercy, I may deserve to attain the glory of your kingdom, Savior of the world, who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

### X. That it is sufficiently beneficial to anticipate the Lord with prayers at the very beginning of the day

[Col. 0483C]

The holy prophets teach us by their examples, worthy of imitation, to anticipate the face of the Lord in the morning with our prayers. David indeed says: “In the morning my prayer will anticipate you, Lord” (Psalm 87:14). Isaiah says likewise: “My soul desired you in the night; but in my spirit, in my inmost being, I will keep watch for you from the morning” (Isaiah 26:9). Therefore, with these three highly suitable psalms, let my spirit keep watch for the Lord in the morning, and let us pray at the rising of the dawn, so that from first light until evening his eyes may be upon us, and his ears attentive to our prayers; and so that he may direct our steps in the way of peace, so that, walking without any stumbling-block of error, [Col. 0483D] no injustice may rule over us. Let us therefore sing these psalms at the very beginning of the day:

“My words”;  
“I cried with my whole heart; hear me, Lord”;  
and, further, “Forever you founded it”;  
“Lord, hear my prayer; receive my supplication with your ears.”

**Verses after the Lord’s Prayer**

“Preserve me, Lord, for I have hoped in you; I said to the Lord, ‘You are my God,’ for you have no need of my goods. Make your mercy known to me in the morning, for I have hoped in you, Lord. Make known to me the way in which I should walk, for to you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul. Lead me in your truth and teach me, for you are my saving God, and I have awaited you all day. Lead me, Lord, in your way, and I will walk in your truth. Turn my eyes away, so that they may not see vanity; enliven me in your way. Establish your law for me in your way, and direct me in the straight path because of my enemies. Lead me in the path of your commandments, for I have desired it. And let your mercy follow me all the days of my life. My tongue also will meditate on your righteousness; all day long I will praise you. Blessed be the name of the Lord, from this time forth and forever.”

**Prayer**

I give you thanks, almighty Father, who have deigned to guard me during this night. I implore your clemency, [Col. 0484B] most merciful Lord, that you grant me to pass through the coming day in your holy service, with such humility and discernment that our service may please you; and grant me today to offer you service pleasing to you with the greatest patience. Send, I beg you, Lord, your angel around us, and rescue us from the wicked who walk about us, so that we may run on an unhindered path in your commandments, without any stumbling-block of error, through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

### XI. The praise of Psalm 118 and what should be frequently recited by us [Reading: “and that it should be frequently recited by us”]

I have also read in the vision of a certain monk that [Col. 0484C] he was earnestly admonished by an angel of light to repeat often in prayer Psalm 118, that is, “Blessed are the undefiled,” in which moral virtue is described. Indeed, it is endowed with various spiritual virtues, so that, even if no other psalm were present, it alone would suffice in prayer. For apart from the mysteries of prophecy, all the necessities of human life that are described more fully in the other psalms are offered to us in this one, as though gathered together on a single platter. Therefore, in accordance with the salutary command of the angelic power, let us sing this psalm of singular benefit every day until we bring our mortal life to its end.

After the *Kyrie eleison* and the Lord’s Prayer, let the verses mentioned above be said.

**Prayer**

[Col. 0484D]

Merciful and readily hearable Lord Jesus Christ, hear me, the most unworthy sinner, as I entreat you, through the intercession and merit of your blessed and glorious ever-virgin mother Mary and of all the citizens of heaven. Increase the faith of your holy catholic Church; grant peace to our pope N., our bishop N., our abbot N., and this entire congregation; also to our princes, relatives by blood, parents, and those joined to me by your love; likewise to those who generously bestow their gifts upon us, and to those who persecute and slander us; to all who implore [Col. 0485A] your holy name for us, or who have wished us wretched ones to plead for them before your mercy. Grant also to us sinners remission and pardon of all sins; to the sick, health; to the fallen, restoration; favorable weather to those at sea; and to travelers a prosperous journey and a safe harbor; to the troubled, joy; to the oppressed, relief; and mercifully grant to captives, prisoners, and exiles remission, release, and return to their homeland. Amen. Grant us here and everywhere your holy angel as guardian and defender; mutual charity to those at odds; true faith to unbelievers; and to our deceased parents, fathers, brothers, and all who rest in your faith, pardon of their sins. Amen.

[Note: [Col. 0485D] Here the first part is declared to end in Quercetanus and in the Cologne edition, but incorrectly. For the scribe himself of the manuscript used by the first editor states that the praise of the hymn of the three young men belongs to the preceding part, and that this part should be ended after the prayer: “For preserving discretion in silence and speech,” below, § 17.]

### XII. The praise of the hymn of the three young men, and that it should be frequently recited in the praise of God [Reading: “and that it should be frequently recited in the praise of God”]

[Col. 0485B]

We ought to imitate the holy Prophet, who says: “I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth” (Psalm 33:2). And also: “In every place of his dominion, bless the Lord, my soul” (Psalm 102:22). And if God is rightly believed to be everywhere, we most rightly confess that he rules everywhere. Let us therefore bless him at all times, who governs us in every place and at every time; who created and recreated us, guards and nourishes us; in whom we live, move, and exist. Therefore, let one small and great praise always be on our lips, [Col. 0485C] in which every creature, according to genus and species, is urged to praise the Creator. And not only every day, but also in the evening, morning, and midday—indeed, at each and every hour of the day—let us offer it to the Lord with the full intention of our heart. For this praise is more praiseworthy than all other praises and more beloved by God than all the rest. This is that singular praise with which we praise him, sweeter than honey and the honeycomb: namely, the hymn that the three beloved young men of God joyfully sang and played amid the devouring flames: “Bless all the works of the Lord; bless the Lord.” Of this I confidently say that, just as we say “Holy of holies” and “Song of songs,” so this too may be called “Hymn of hymns.” In it God, the God of gods, is praised more briefly and abundantly than in all other places; he who, three in persons and one in substance, lives and reigns everywhere throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

**Verses after the Lord’s Prayer**

“Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers, and praiseworthy, glorious, and exalted above all forever. And blessed is the holy and praiseworthy name of your glory, exalted above all throughout all ages. Blessed are you in the temple of your glory, and supremely praiseworthy and supremely glorious forever. Blessed are you on the throne of your kingdom, and supremely praiseworthy and supremely exalted [Col. 0486A] forever. Blessed are you who behold the depths and sit above the cherubim; praiseworthy and supremely exalted forever. Blessed are you, Lord; teach me your ordinances.”

**Confession and praise of the Holy Trinity**

I praise and bless you, just and good God, parent of all creation, three in persons and one in substance; true Father of the only-begotten majesty, deriving his beginning from no one and giving a beginning to all; generating the Son not by bodily descent or from outside himself, not by necessity or will, but by nature. True Son, ineffably born from the Father without an interval of time, before the ages. True Holy Spirit, ineffably proceeding from the Father and the Son, remaining substantially in the Father and the Son. Eternal Father [Col. 0486B] without birth; eternal Holy Spirit, with procession but without birth. The whole Father in the Son and the Holy Spirit. The whole Son in the Father and the Holy Spirit. The whole Holy Spirit remaining in the Father and the Son, with one power and one kingdom, one might and one eternity. Reigning everywhere, then and now. Throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

### XIII. That we ought to pray daily with tears for the various wounds that we suffer

Because we see that we have fallen into the lament of Jeremiah, which says: “If I go out into the fields, behold, those slain by the sword; and if I enter the city, behold, [Col. 0486C] those weakened by hunger” (Jeremiah 14:18); and because that terrible threat of the Lord has also been fulfilled in us, by which the Lord consumes them with sword, famine, and pestilence, let us ask, with the same Prophet, for water for our head and a fountain of tears for our eyes, and let us weep day and night for the slain of our people. We can never lament this better than if, with a contrite and humbled heart, we frequently recite before the Lord these five psalms:

“God, with our ears”;  
“God, you have rejected us”;  
“Why have you rejected us, God, forever?”;  
“God, the nations have entered”;  
“Give ear, you who rule Israel.”

**Verses after the Lord’s Prayer**

“I said: Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against you. We have sinned with our [Col. 0486D] fathers; we have acted unjustly and committed iniquity. Do not remember our ancient iniquities; may your mercy, Lord, quickly anticipate us. Help us, God our Savior, and for the honor of your name, Lord, deliver us. Remember us, Lord, in the favor shown to your people, and visit us with your salvation. Convert us, God our Savior, and turn your anger away from us. Deliver us from our enemies, our God, and free us from those who rise up against us. Lord, do not go far from us; God, [Col. 0487A] look upon us for our help. Turn again, Lord, for a little while, and have compassion on your servants. Save us, Lord our God, and gather us from the nations, so that they may confess your holy name and glory in your praise. Arise, Lord, help us, and deliver us for your name’s sake.”

**Prayer**

We pray to you, merciful and readily hearable Lord Jesus Christ our God, and with every supplication we ask that, through the intercession of the blessed and glorious ever-virgin Mary and of all the holy angels, archangels, patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs, confessors, virgins, monks, and all the citizens of heaven, you may increase the faith of your holy [Col. 0487B] catholic Church, grant peace, and grant us pardon and remission of sins. Amen. Grant health to the sick, restoration to the fallen, favorable weather to those at sea, and to faithful travelers a prosperous journey and a safe harbor; grant joy to those in tribulation [Perhaps: “to the troubled”], relief to the oppressed, and to captives, prisoners, and exiles remission, release, and return to their homeland. Amen. Deign graciously to grant your holy angel as guardian here and everywhere, mutual charity to those at odds, true faith to unbelievers, and eternal rest to the faithful departed.

### XIV. That, according to the Apostle’s command, all should pray for all

[Col. 0487C]

The apostolic word commanded us: “Pray for one another,” it says, “that you may be saved” (James 5:16). We must obey this salutary command and pray for all, so that all may be saved with all. There are also seven psalms through which, if we become one body, we pray for the whole body of the Church. Yet consider, reader, and test what we say. In these psalms there is mention simultaneously of priests, kings, and rulers, as well as of the people and the multitude. The opening words, therefore, of the psalms we mentioned are these:

“Remember, Lord, David”;  
“Lord, in your strength”;  
“To you, Lord, I cried; my God”;  
“May God have mercy on us”;  
“You have blessed, Lord”;  
“Lord, you have been our refuge”;  
“I will confess to you, Lord, with my whole heart, for you have heard all the words of my mouth.”

Indeed, lest anyone reproach us for having placed first the psalm “Remember, Lord, David,” which is later in order, we will give this answer: order is not to be weighed in the psalms, but their power. And because the priestly order is first within the Church, we placed it first in the prayers.

**Verses after the Lord’s Prayer**

“I said: Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against you. Let your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let your saints rejoice. Lord, save the king, and hear us on the day when we call upon you. Save your people, Lord, and bless your inheritance; rule them and exalt them [Col. 0488A] forever. Remember your congregation, which you established from the beginning. You redeemed the rod of your inheritance. Do not hand over to beasts the souls of those who confess you; do not forget the souls of your poor forever. Lord God of hosts, convert us and show us your face, and we shall be saved. Show us, Lord, your mercy, and give us your salvation. Lord God of hosts, hear our prayers; give ear, God of Jacob. And you, Lord, Lord, show mercy to us for your name’s sake, because your mercy is sweet. Protect us from the assembly of the malicious and from the multitude of those who work iniquity. Send us help from the holy place, and protect us from Zion. Hear us, Lord, for your mercy is kind; according to the abundance of your mercies, [Col. 0488B] look upon me. Extend, Lord, your mercy to those who know you, and your righteousness to those who are upright in heart. May it please you, Lord, to deliver me; Lord, look upon us for our help. Arise, Lord, help us, and deliver us for your name’s sake.”

**Prayer**

Be gracious, Lord, I ask, to your entire holy catholic Church, spread throughout the whole world. Grant it right faith, excellent works, and perpetual peace. Be gracious to all your faithful who labor under the yoke of the nations. Be gracious to your servant N. [Alternative: “I.”], the pope, and to all priests and ministers, and to all their clergy. Be gracious to your servant N. [Col. 0488C] the abbot, and to this entire congregation of yours, and to all who are gathered throughout the whole world in your name. Be gracious to your servant N. the king, to all Christian rulers, and to their entire army. Be gracious to all my brothers, whether those joined to me by your love or by blood relationship. Be gracious to all who invoke your holy name for me, or who have wished me, wretched as I am, to plead before your mercy. Be gracious to virgins, married women, and widows; to orphans, captives, penitents, the sick, the afflicted, those at sea, travelers, prisoners, and all who are placed in any need or misery; and to your entire Christian people, whom you redeemed with your precious blood. Be gracious also to miserable pagans, Jews, and heretics, [Col. 0488D] and to the fallen, so that they may believe in you as the true Lord and God and return to you with all their heart. Grant, I ask, to every sex, every age, and every condition of the Christian order the observance of your commandments, pardon for all their sins, and have mercy on us. Amen.

### XV. That it is good to pray for the faithful departed

The holy Apostle rebuked certain Corinthians for unbelief because they were wavering concerning the glory of the resurrection: “If Christ,” he says, “is preached as having risen from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the good [Alternative: “of the dead]” (1 Corinthians 15:12)? Therefore, since we [Col. 0489A] truly believe and await the resurrection without any hesitation, let us pray daily for our brothers who sleep and will rise again. In these five psalms we can in some way commemorate them, because in them the resurrection of the dead is proclaimed in a certain sense:

“Have mercy on me, God, according to your great mercy”;  
“I have loved, because the Lord heard”;  
“I believed, therefore I spoke”;  
“Confess to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy is forever”;  
“Let Israel say now”;  
“Praise the Lord in his holy places.”

**Verses after the Lord’s Prayer**

“May the souls of our dying brothers dwell among good things, and may their offspring possess the earth as an inheritance. May the foot of pride not come upon them, and may the hand of sinners not move them. May they receive blessing [Col. 0489B] from the Lord and mercy from God their Savior. May they exult in the presence of God and delight in joy. But you, Lord, do not remove your mercies far from me; may your mercy and truth receive them. Give them, Lord, the protection of your salvation, and may your right hand receive them. Send forth your light and your truth; may they themselves lead them to your holy mountain, to your tabernacles. And may they dwell in your tabernacles forever; may they be protected under the shelter of your wings. But you, Lord, have mercy on them, raise them up, and strengthen them in your presence forever, so that they may dwell in your house for length of days.”

**Prayer**

[Col. 0489C] Do not reckon, most merciful Lord, the sins of my brothers who rest, or of those who were joined to me through your love; but deign to grant them and all the departed in your faith eternal rest.

**Another prayer**

Grant, I ask, Lord, rest to all our brothers who departed from this light in confession of your name, and have mercy on us. Amen.

### XVI. That one should pray in the dormitory cell before giving the body rest

After the entire span of the day has passed, when we approach our beds to sleep, let us ask [Col. 0489D] the Lord with every desire, saying with the Prophet: “Enlighten my eyes, lest I ever sleep in death” (Psalm 12:4). For one who sleeps is no better than a dead person when, from evening until morning, with his mouth hardened [Perhaps: “stopped up”] against the praise of the Creator, he snores supine in his bed, overcome not so much by sleep as by lethargy. Yet because it is contrary to nature for a human being to live without sleep, let us, when we are about to sleep, ask him who will neither slumber nor sleep, so that, while sleeping, we may satisfy not our will but necessity. Moreover, let us sing before the bed the sixth psalm, namely, “Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger,” for it is suitable both to the matter and to the time. [Col. 0490A] If anyone wishes and is not overcome by laziness, the twelfth psalm may also be joined to it: “How long, Lord?”; and the hundred and twentieth: “I lifted up my eyes to the mountains.”

**Verses after the Lord’s Prayer**

“Send us help from the holy place, Lord, and protect us from Zion. Protect us from the assembly of the malicious and from the multitude of those who work iniquity. Make your face shine upon your servant, and save me in your mercy. Lord, let me not be confounded, for I have called upon you. Make your face shine upon your servant, and teach me your ordinances. For you enlighten my lamps, Lord my God; enlighten my darkness.”

**First prayer in the dormitory cell**

[Col. 0490B] Bless this cell, Lord, I ask, so that we who hope in the shadow of your wings may be protected by the power of your strength from all the snares of demons. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns forever and ever. Amen.

**Another**

Be present, I ask, Lord, to this cell, so that the host of demons may be crushed and driven away.

**Another prayer**

Lord, whom neither expanses enlarge nor the narrowness of places constrains, fill this cell, I ask, with the light of your presence, so that the author of darkness may depart in confusion. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

**Another**

[Col. 0490C] From the face of the wicked, I ask, Lord, protect us under the shadow of your wings, so that, rising to praise your name, we may sleep securely while you keep watch over us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

**Another**

I give you thanks, holy Lord Father, almighty eternal God, who have deigned to guard me on this day through your holy mercy. Grant me to pass through this night with peaceful and pure heart and body, so that, rising in purity for the vigils, I may be able to offer you pleasing service.

**39. Prayer of Saint Jerome for the safeguarding of the following day**  
[Note: [Col. 0489] It appears in Martene, *Ancient Discipline of the Church*, p. 621, in the booklet of Charles the Bald, p. 6, with a certain difference.]

Be with me, Lord of hosts. When I rise in the morning, [Col. 0490D] attend to me and govern all my actions, my words, my thoughts, and my works, so that I may pass the whole day according to your will. Give me, Lord, your fear, compunction of heart, humility of mind, and purity of conscience, so that I may despise the earth, look up to heaven, hate sins, and love righteousness. Cut away from me, Lord, the appetite of gluttony, the lust of fornication, the love of money, the plague of anger, worldly sorrow, the sluggishness of the mind, empty joy, and the tyranny of pride. Plant in me, Lord, the virtue of abstinence, bodily restraint, purity of mind, voluntary [Col. 0491A] poverty, true patience, spiritual joy, stability of spirit, contrition of heart, unfeigned humility, and fraternal charity. Guard my mouth, so that I may not speak empty things, chatter about worldly matters, slander those absent, or curse present parents [The word “parents” is redundant]; so that I may not answer a curse with a curse, but, on the contrary, bless the Lord at all times: “His praise is always in my mouth.” Guard my eyes, so that they may not look upon a woman in order to desire her, nor desire my neighbor’s property or the delights of this age; but let me say with the spirit of David: “Enlighten my eyes, lest I ever sleep in death, lest my enemy ever say, ‘I have prevailed against him’” (Psalm 12:4). And let me say: “My eyes are always toward the Lord,” and so forth. And again let me say: [Col. 0491B] “To you I have lifted up my eyes, you who dwell in the heavens.” Guard my ears, so that they may not hear a slandering tongue, hear falsehood, or hear an idle word; but let them always be open every day to hear the word of God. Guard my feet, so that they may not wander idly around the house, but stand in the prayer of God. Guard my hands, so that they may not often be extended to receive gifts, but rather be raised in the Lord’s prayers, clean and pure, without anger and dispute, so that I may be able to say that prophetic utterance: “Let my prayer be directed like incense in your sight. The lifting of my hands is an evening sacrifice.” May it be so. Amen.

### XVII. For preserving discretion in silence and speech

[Col. 0491C] It is written, as the Apostle affirms: “Life and death are in the power of the tongue” (Proverbs 18:21). And again: “No human being can tame the tongue” (James 3:8). Therefore, what a pure human being cannot tame, let us ask God and man to tame. Thus, in order to obtain the virtue of discreet silence, let us sing these psalms to the Lord with humble devotion:

“My words”;  
“I said, ‘I will guard my ways’”;  
“Lord, I cried to you; hear me.”

**Verses after the Lord’s Prayer**

“Lord, hear my prayer; give ear to the words of my mouth. Guard me, Lord, like the apple of the eye; protect me under the shadow of your wings. Place, Lord, a guard over my mouth and a door of restraint around my lips, so that my heart may not incline toward an evil word, but my mouth may be filled with your praise, so that I may be able [Col. 0491D] to sing your glory and your greatness all day long. And may the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart always be pleasing in your sight. My tongue also will meditate on your righteousness; all day long I will praise you. Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.”

**Prayer**
Lord our God, we believe that you are Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. For Truth would not say, “Go, baptize all nations in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit” (Matt. 28:19), unless the Trinity existed. Nor would you command us, Lord God, to baptize in the name of one who was not God; nor would it be said by his voice, “Hear, O Israel: the Lord your God is one” (Deut. 6:4), unless the Trinity were one God. And unless you yourself were God the Father, and the Son himself were your Word, Jesus Christ, and your gift were the Holy Spirit [perhaps: “the Holy One”], we would not read in the writings of Truth: “God sent his Son” (Gal. 4:4). Nor would you, Only-Begotten, say concerning the Holy Spirit: “Whom the Father will send in my name,” and “whom I will send to you from the Father” (John 14:26; 15:26).

Directing my intention toward this rule of faith, insofar as you enabled me, I sought you and desired, by understanding, to see what I believed; and I debated and labored with myself. Lord my God, my one hope, hear me, lest, wearied, I should become unwilling to seek you; rather, make me always seek your face with ardor. Give strength for seeking, you who have enabled me to find you, and have given me ever greater hope of finding you [Col. 0492B] [Cologne edition: “Before you are my strength and my weakness; preserve the one, heal the other”]. Before you are my knowledge and my ignorance. Where you have opened to me, receive me as I enter; where you have closed, open to me as I knock, so that I may remember you, understand you, and love you. Increase these things in me until you restore me whole.

I know that it is written: “In much speaking you will not escape sin” (Prov. 10:19). But would that, in proclaiming your word and praising you, I spoke only in this way; then I would not merely flee sin, but would gain merit, however much I spoke thus. For blessed Paul would not in this way have commanded Timothy, his son, to whom he wrote, saying: “Proclaim the word; be urgent in season and out of season” (2 Tim. 4:2). Should he be said not to have spoken much, since he did not keep your word, Lord, silent—not only in season but also out of season? Yet it was not “much,” because only what was necessary was spoken.

Deliver me, my God, from the much speaking that I suffer inwardly in my soul, wretched as I am before you and fleeing to your mercy; for I am not silent in my thoughts, even when I am silent in my voice. Indeed, if I did not think anything except what pleased you, I would surely not ask you to deliver me from this much speaking. But many of my thoughts are of the kind you know human thoughts to be: they are vain. Grant me not to consent to them; and, whenever they delight me, nevertheless to reject them and not linger in them as though half-asleep. Yet do not let them prevail with me so that anything proceeds from them into my actions; rather, while you guard me, let my judgment and my whole conscience at least remain free from them [Col. 0492D] [perhaps: “safe”].

A certain wise man, speaking of you in his book, which is properly called Ecclesiasticus, said: “We say many things and fail in words. But the consummation of all speech is he himself” (Eccl. 43:29). When, therefore, we have come to you, these many things that we say will cease and will not remain; but you alone will remain, all in all. And without end we shall say one thing, praising you as one, and, having been made one in you, we too shall be one.

Lord God, one God, Trinity, whatever I have said about what is yours in these books, may your people acknowledge; and if anything is from what is mine, may you acknowledge [perhaps: forgive] it—and may your people do so as well. Amen.

## PART TWO. PRAYERS IN ORDER.

### I. Prayer for singing the psalms [after the psalms have been sung] for oneself.

Deliverer of souls and Redeemer of the world, Jesus Christ, Lord God eternal, immortal King, I, a sinner, implore your immense and great clemency: through the singing of the psalms that I, wretched and unworthy, have sung, deliver my soul from sin; draw my heart away from evil, perverse, and faithless thoughts; withdraw my body from slavery to sin; drive carnal desires far from me; rescue me from every hindrance of Satan and of his visible and invisible servants, and from your unbelievers who seek to hinder my soul.

### II. Prayer when psalms are sung [have been sung] for others.

Lord God almighty, creator of heaven and earth, mercifully hear my prayer, in which I, a sinner, entreat your majesty for your servant N. Receive, I beseech you, through your great mercy, my petition, on account of the singing of the psalms that I, unhappy as I am, have sung; and grant him in this present age life and health, and time in this life to practice repentance; and in the age to come grant him pardon, indulgence, or remission of all sins, and, with all your saints, to receive everlasting life. Amen.

### III. Prayer for father, mother, and all relatives.

Sovereign Lord God almighty, who wondrously fashioned all things and created everything by your ordering, who ordained that the human race should be propagated from man and woman, and commanded that love and affection be shown toward father and mother: hear me, merciful God, as I cry to you for my father N. and my mother N., both of whom, by your providence, you have deigned to prepare for me, most humble though I am; and also for my brothers and sisters, and all my relatives who are joined to me by bodily kinship, a sinner though I am, both the living and the dead, whose names and merits are known to you, Lord God of all. Protect them and defend them from every evil, and set them on the way of salvation; do not allow their days to end before, through true confession and true amendment of all their transgressions, you have forgiven their sins and made them, once freed from the flesh, worthy of heavenly participation.

Hear me also, most wretched as I am, most merciful God, as I supplicate you for the souls of your male and female servants, those who have given us their alms, whose names are written among us, and who have commended themselves to our prayers [Col. 0494A]; grant them the benefits of your mercy and deign to place them in the dwelling pleasing to you, Savior of the world, who with God the Father and the Holy Spirit live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

### IV. Prayer for an abbot or a community.

Eternal and incomprehensible Lord God, you alone know the hearts of the children of men. You know that my iniquity is immeasurable; how, then, can I pray for others when I am not fit to pray for myself? Nevertheless, most merciful Father, according to the abundance of your mercy, receive the prayers of your servant, which I pour out before your majesty for your servant N., the abbot, or for all the brothers whom we see living under his governance. Grant that all of us may have true charity toward one another and harmony that is pleasing to you. Take away from us, Lord, every evil, and send us every good, which no one can possess without you. Grant us perseverance in good works, so that, through your mercy, we may deserve to reach the glory of your kingdom, Savior of the world, who live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

#### Another prayer.

Sovereign Lord God almighty, all things are placed in your will; you know everything before it comes to be. Look upon us and have mercy on us. Most merciful God, you permitted this community to gather in this place for the glorification of your holy name; grant us, your servants, your holy help from heaven, lest we suffer the loss of our souls. Do not hand this community over to dispersion, but preserve it for the sake of your holy name. Fill our hearts with faith, hope, and charity, with obedience, humility, and patience. Make our ruler and Father according to your heart, so that he may do your will for his salvation and ours, so that we may always deserve to have you, Lord, as our shepherd and, in all things, our protector. May your will be done in all of us, Lord, so that, through your mercy, we may deserve to reach the glory of your kingdom, Savior of the world, who live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

### V. Prayer for household members and all Christians, and for all those commended to us.

Lord God almighty, who have deigned to spread your Church throughout the whole world among all nations, and have commanded that you be served by all the ranks faithfully included within it, and to whom the merits of each person are known: have mercy on all our household members and on all orthodox bishops, abbots, presbyters, deacons and subdeacons, acolytes, exorcists, readers, doorkeepers, monks, clerics, virgins, widows, married people, the continent, penitents, kings, princes, dukes, judges, tribunes, centurions, commanders of fifty, and decans, and on all the ranks that are commonly included in your Catholic Church in the faith of the holy Trinity.

Have mercy also on all who, in faith in and love of your holy name, have given us their alms or commended themselves to our prayers, and on those whom we have promised to include in our prayers, both living and dead, healthy and ill, whose names and merits are known to you, Lord God of all, for your wisdom is without number.

Hear me, most loving and merciful God, and have mercy on all Catholics who still dwell in the body. Deign to turn those who have turned away from the way of truth back to you, so that they may seek you with their whole heart. Preserve all by eternal protection, so that no temptations may separate them from you. Grant that this prayer of your servant may benefit the dead for the amendment of their sins or the removal [variant: “alleviation”] of their punishments. You are the great and terrible God, merciful and lover of humankind; you know what is expedient for each person. We beseech your clemency: according to your will, may it be done for all of us, both the living and the faithful dead, Savior of the world, who live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

### VI. Prayer for alms.

Lord God almighty, great and eternal Physician, who in your mercy promised your faithful, through the distribution of alms, the remedy of souls, indulgence, and remission of sins: hear me, gracious and kind, for all your faithful who have given us their alms or commended themselves to our prayers in faith in your majesty, both the living and the dead, the healthy and the ill. May my prayers, which I pour out before you for their salvation, reach the ears of your mercy.

Do not look upon my sins, Lord, but upon the faith of those men and women who, in faith in your name, have bestowed temporal goods upon us, so that you, God, the rewarder of all good things, may deign to repay them great things for small and everlasting rewards for earthly things, Savior of the world, who live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

### VII. Confession of majesty and petition for pardon.

Lord, hear my prayer; give ear to the words of my mouth. God, let my prayer enter into your presence. Incline your ear to my prayers, Lord. God, who hear those who ask rightly, do not be inexorable because of my excessive sins and crimes; rather, because of your immeasurable goodness, hear my prayer, give ear to my tears, and forgive me, so that I may recover before I depart and exist no longer.

God, who desire to save all human beings and desire no one to perish, save me from the snare of death, from the punishments of hell, and from every ambush of the enemy against mind and body. God, who do not desire the death of a sinner but that he should turn and live, help me to turn to you with my whole heart and deserve to cling to your commandments.

God, who kill and make alive, lead down to the underworld and bring back, grant me the mortification of the flesh and the vivification of the spirit. God, who raise the needy from the dust and lift the poor from the dungheap, raise me, as I cry to you, from the pit of misery and the mire of filth, and set my feet upon a rock; put into them and into my mouth a new song, a hymn of your glory.

God, who alone possess immortality and dwell in inaccessible light, free me from everlasting death, show me the light of your mercies, blot out my iniquities, and teach me to do your will all the days of my life. God, who know past and future things, grant me forgiveness for my past offenses, and grant me continence concerning present and future things, so that I may deserve to reach your mercy.

God, who desire us to be corrected rather than to perish through neglect, do not destroy me in my many and grievous offenses. According to your mercy and compassion, correct me; do not cast me away from your mercy; do not let me fall before my adversaries, lest my enemy say, “I have prevailed against him.”

God, whose eyes look upon the ways of the children of men, look upon me and have mercy on me. Drive from me what you hate, and mercifully grant what you love. Drive from me, Lord, every harmful thought, every evil mouth, and every perverse deed. Forgive what my wretched conscience fears, and add what prayer does not presume to ask.

God, because you care for all things, do not abandon me to the counsel of my own heart or leave me to my own judgment without help, for no living person will be justified in your sight. Since human mortality slips without you, may my frailty always be withdrawn from every harmful thing by your help and directed toward what brings salvation.

God, who examine hearts, give me a heart that fears you, understanding that comprehends you, and conduct that pleases you, so that by fearing you I may always turn away from evil, and by loving you I may always be guarded by you in what is good. Give me strength to resist vices and those who ambush every virtue.

God, who are the giver of all good things, grant me faith, the work of knowledge, continence, charity, chastity, true patience and humility, voluntary poverty, and good perseverance in your service. God, who are the way, the truth, and the life, lead me in your way, so that I may walk in your truth. Let my heart rejoice so that it may fear your name, and lead me to eternal life.

God, who are the true light that illumines the hearts of the faithful, illumine my heart with the light of your understanding. Give me true knowledge, drive every darkness of ignorance from me, and expel from me, Lord, the darkness of my sins, so that I may always deserve to walk in the splendor of your light.

God, who alone perform great wonders, make with me a sign for good, so that those who hate me may see it and be put to shame, for you, Lord, have helped me and comforted me, and let them say, “Let this be the change of the right hand of the Most High.”

Lord, deal with your servant according to your mercy, and teach me your statutes. I am your servant; give me understanding, so that I may learn your commandments and keep them with my whole heart, for there is great reward in keeping them. Lord, deal with me according to your mercy, for your mercy is sweet.

Deliver me, for I am needy and poor, and my heart is troubled within me. Deliver me from those who persecute me, for they have grown strong against me. Deliver me, God of Israel, from all my iniquities. Deliver me from bloodguilt, God, God of my salvation, and my tongue shall exalt your righteousness. Deliver me from the lion’s mouth and from the horns of the unicorns (unicornium; variant: unicorniorum), so that I may declare your name to my brothers.

My deliverer from my angry enemies, you will exalt me above those who rise against me; you will rescue me from the unjust man. Do not allow me to be tested beyond what I can bear, for you know my formation; you know the frailty of my body and mind. You know my foolishness, and my offenses are not hidden from you.

My God, rescue me from the hands of my enemies and from those who persecute me; lead me out of the snare that they have hidden for me, for you are my protector. Make your face shine upon your servant, and save me in your mercy. Lord, let me not be put to shame, for I have called upon you.

### VIII. Prayer for knowledge of God, for forgiveness of offenses, and for the elimination of various tribulations.

Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ; you who are my mercy, have mercy on me. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may ask you rightly. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may make me worthy to be heard. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ. Hear me, so that I may know your will; teach me, so that you may nourish me in your charity.

Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may believe in you, know you, and love you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may hope in you.

Have mercy, Lord, because my understanding is defiled by every unlawful desire, and by every arrogance, anger, suspicion, and hypocrisy. Have mercy, Lord God almighty, so that I may steadfastly know and love the bond of charity. Have mercy, God, so that you may rescue me from everlasting death. Have mercy, God, so that you may grant me true repentance and pardon for all my sins and crimes.

Have mercy, God, so that you may grant me remission of all my sins, rescue me from every tribulation, free me from every impurity of heart and body, extinguish completely in me the tinder of lust, and free me from every ambush of the devil and from every evil.

Have mercy, Lord God; have mercy, so that my soul may live in you and my life may advance in you. Have mercy, Lord God the Father, my glory, my life, my salvation and my strength. Have mercy, Holy Spirit, my comfort and illumination. Have mercy, have mercy, Trinity and Unity.

I praise you, I adore you, I confess you: my peace, my hope, my praise, my life, my beauty and my blessedness, my confidence and trust, remission of my crimes and offenses; my love and support, my God, my refuge, deliverer, [protector], and receiver; my teacher, physician, governor, and redeemer; my rest, health, and delight; my witness and judge, holy Trinity, inseparable Unity.

Almighty God, deign to free me from every evil and bless me with your everlasting blessing, you who are the blessed, ineffable, and incorruptible God for ever and ever. Amen.

### IX. Confession of sins.

Prepare yourself manfully for your future confession, and strengthen yourself in the Lord. Do not be ashamed, because pardon comes from this: when you have humbly confessed your sins in hope of God’s mercy, you must abandon them; for without confession there is no pardon.

First, humbly prostrate yourself on the ground before God for prayer, and ask blessed Mary, Mother of God, to intercede for you with the Lord, together with all the holy apostles, martyrs, confessors, and virgins. Ask that almighty God may deign to give you perfect wisdom, true pardon, and steadfast strength of spirit to confess your sins truthfully from the depths of your heart. Then rise, and with confidence and true faith say to the one to whom you wish to confess your sins: “My fault, because I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word, and deed.”

#### Another.

I confess before almighty God, creator of heaven and earth, and before this holy altar and the holy relics that are in this holy place, that I have sinned exceedingly in most abominable thoughts, delighting in and consenting to them, meditating upon them, planning them in my understanding and memory and will, and considering how I might carry out in deed what I was wrongly thinking.

#### Another.

I confess that I have sinned exceedingly in vain, impure, and shameful speech, in idle and harmful words. I confess the hatreds of my heart, deceitfulness, envy, slander, impatience, insults, quarrels, judgments, blasphemies, filthy speech, buffoonery, lies, curses, perjury, wicked counsels, excuses for my sins, mockery, dissimulation, flattery, reproaches, boastfulness, disturbances, ill will, seductions, rages, indignation, ambition, desires of the flesh and of the eyes, pride, sadness, fears, weakness of spirit, many wearinesses, negligence, false security, useless vigils displeasing to God, greediness in eating, drinking, speaking, and excessive sleep, disordered carnal desires, and the wicked, bitter, and most impious tyrannies of my heart.
