#### Another.

I confess that, because of the comfort and pleasure of my body, I set aside God’s commandments. I often abandoned holy vigils and satisfied my sleepiness; full of disgust for spiritual things, I followed idleness, softness, laziness, sluggishness, and cowardice. Through pride and arrogance I transgressed God’s commandments and considered myself better than others.

In many matters I pursued carnal pleasures, impurities, pollutions, drunkenness, feasting, banquets, and gluttony, openly and secretly, wrongly [F.: “I perpetrated”], and, delighting in all these things with all my senses as though they were luxuries, I took sinful and pleasant repose.

I spent Sundays, the holy solemnities of God, and the feasts of the saints unworthily and without fear of God. I meditated on nothing spiritual during them, but did everything carnally, intent on filling my belly, dissolving into laughter, and pursuing vain jokes and diversions. I did not reverently preserve my religious state with the fear of God as I ought.

In the holy church, when I went to and attended the work of God, I thought, perpetrated, and spoke many vain and evil things. Often weighed down by excessive sleep, I lost many prayers, readings, and psalmody together with the offices. Even when awake, my inner sight frequently wandered with distracted memory through many arrangements of earthly things, through unlawful pleasures, vain and shameful meditations, and various errors; thus my occupied understanding became fruitless in spiritual matters.

#### Another confession.

I, unworthy and polluted, touched the consecrated ministries of God, the holy relics, the holy books, and the sacred vessels, and handled them sordidly and negligently. With polluted heart and body, without confession or repentance, knowingly and unworthily I received the body and blood of the Lord; nor did I fear in terror, as I ought to have feared, the judgment of God that was to come upon me.

I negligently and irreverently poured out the canonical offices, prayers, psalmody, and readings in the sight of God, and omitted many things that I did not make up. I did not love my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, all my relatives and Christians for God’s sake as God commanded, nor did I offer them the service of honor; rather, I always wished to please everyone carnally, because I sought what was mine rather than what was God’s.

I did not love or patiently endure those who opposed and slandered me, as God’s commandment requires; instead, I repaid them by increasing evil for evil, and often strove to return evil for good. I did not love or honor bishops, presbyters, abbots, monks, canons, and all the clergy of God’s Church, nor my superiors or those placed in high positions, nor did I offer them the service of honor as God commanded. On the contrary, I censured, slandered, and judged them.

I did not give tithes or firstfruits of my goods. I did not love hospitality. I did not preserve true brotherhood with a pure heart. I concealed and consumed robbery and theft, and consented to those who robbed and concealed stolen goods.

I did not visit the sick or those in prison, nor clothe the naked as I ought. I did not receive guests and pilgrims for God’s sake. I did not feed the hungry or give drink to the thirsty. I did not comfort those who were grieving and weeping. I provoked those who were at odds with one another more toward anger than peace.

I preferred to believe and hear evil rather than good, and falsehood before truth. I did not believe what I especially ought to have believed, and I believed what I ought not to have believed. I often consented to evil and willingly listened to slanderers. Through carnal desires, evil thoughts and wills, and evil deeds, I polluted and destroyed myself; I harmed anyone whom I was able to harm; I consented to the devil and, by sinning, subjected myself to his pleasure.

I confess that I have sinned greatly in sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch; in my feet and hands, in my tongue, in my genital members, and in all my senses I have perpetrated many evils.

Filled with every iniquity, malice, and wickedness, I committed sacrilege, homicide, adultery, false witness, theft, robbery, and perjury. I held usury for a long time. I returned evil for good. And not only these things, but I also committed many other evils and consented to those who committed them.

I, wretched man, have sinned exceedingly, because I wrongly spent the alms, firstfruits, and tithes that I received under the pretext of priesthood, consuming them for my own uses, and I did not do what I ought to have done with them.

I sinned because I was negligent concerning my course, which I ought to have completed through the canonical hours; concerning my psalmody and prayers; and concerning my ministry, which I did not keep according to order.

I sinned concerning those penitents who came to me for confession, whom I neither judged according to canonical judgment nor attended to as I ought. I sinned against those subject to me, because I did not maintain zeal for righteousness toward the negligent with the just measure I ought to have used; and often, through useless leniency, I accommodated myself to them when I ought not to have done so.

I sinned after confessing the crimes I had committed. I sinned in desiring the property of others. Through curiosity I saw many things with my eyes and heard many things with my ears that I ought neither to have seen nor heard. I often wished to disgrace publicly through rebuke someone who did not please me, to wound my neighbor’s reputation with malicious speech, and to disparage him openly. I often judged wrongly the secrets of another’s heart.

I sinned because I retained in my mind injuries done to me, and did not forgive those who sinned against me with a pure heart. Now I forgive from my whole heart all who have sinned against me.

I sinned because I rightly judged and condemned the very iniquities that I committed against others, judging myself one way and others another. I said many things I ought not to have said. I thought many things I ought not to have thought, and did not think many good things that I ought to have thought.

I gave unlawful kisses and shameful embraces. I often touched what I ought not to have touched; I often consented to what I ought not to have consented to. I abandoned good works that I ought not to have abandoned, and did evil things that I ought not to have done. I abhorred what I ought to have loved, and loved what I ought not to have loved.

For all these and my countless other crimes, which I committed against God’s law, so that I might find pardon with God, I sought a monastery and undertook the monastic life. But I, wretched man, am often entangled in various ways in frivolity, vanity, negligence, restlessness of spirit, bitterness, and the goads of evil thoughts; in obstinate rebellion, negligence concerning good works, transgression of religion, talkativeness, buffoonery, hardness of heart, accidie, indignation, disobedience, judgment, murmuring and slander, pride, and resentment of spirit.

All these evils I confess before almighty God, this holy altar, and the holy relics that are in this place, with a pure and true confession; and, with good will, I resolve [supplied: “I propose,” or something similar] to amend them, insofar as God’s mercy deigns to help me.

For almighty God himself, who said through the prophet, “I do not desire the death of a sinner, but that he should turn and live” (Ezek. 33:11), and again, “On whatever day you groan, you will be saved” (ibid., v. 12), and who has mercifully deigned to draw me to confess my sins, may grant me the strength to restrain myself from evil deeds [supplied: “may grant,” or something similar], may have mercy on my soul, pardon, forgive, and blot out all my past, present, and future sins, and lead and bring me into eternal life. Amen.

#### Another confession.

Receive my confession, Lord God, my one hope of salvation. I am utterly ruined by gluttony, drunkenness, fornication, lust, sadness, accidie, sleepiness, negligence, anger, greed, envy, hatred, slander, perjury, falsehood, lying, vainglory, frivolity, and pride. In thought, speech, action, and all my senses I have carried these things out. But you, who justify the ungodly and make the dead alive, make me alive and justify me, Lord my God. Amen.

### X. Another confession [Note: Namely, of faith, not of sins.]

Lord God, I believe that you are almighty, invisible, uncircumscribed, governing and containing all things, creator of all, Trinity, and Unity. I believe that you sent your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, into the world for the salvation of the human race. This is the faith by which I believe in you. If I believe rightly, good; but if I believe less than I ought, I beseech you not to look at the words I have spoken, but at what I intended.

Lord Jesus Christ, I believe that you were announced by the angel to the Virgin Mary. I believe that you were born according to the flesh and shown to the shepherds. I believe that you were circumcised on the eighth day, adored by the Magi, baptized by John in the Jordan, and presented in the temple.

I believe that you were betrayed by Judas the betrayer, spat upon, scourged, crowned with thorns, crucified, buried, and rose again on the third day; that for forty days you ate and drank with your disciples; then, on the fortieth day, while your disciples stood looking on, you ascended into heaven. From there, I believe, you will come to judge the living and the dead.

I am certain, Lord, that you said: “I do not desire the death of a sinner, but that he should turn and live” (Ezek. 33:11). And again: “There will be joy over one sinner who repents more than over ninety-nine righteous persons who have no need of repentance” (Luke 15:7).

### XI. Prayer of monks.

Lord, whatever I have sinned through error, knowingly, or contempt; whatever through deliberate will, weakness, or intention; whatever through stealth or reflection, in thought, word, or deed, secretly or openly; whatever of these things is either hidden in the mind, lies exposed, wounds the conscience, or, through false security, deceives by whatever forms of delusion—mercifully and graciously forgive it in your gratuitous compassion. Do not abandon my soul without hope of pardon; rather, in your mercy, inspire it to hasten toward the boundless clemency of your compassion, after it has committed many grave and deadly sins. [Col. 0502B] And when you permit it to fear the future torments of punishment, grant that, once its sins have been forgiven, it may always breathe freely in hope of the abiding joys of eternal life. Do not permit the conscience of my soul, cleansed from the thought of transgressions and every vice, to apostatize from you again or to be irreparably polluted.

Lord, mercifully cleanse all the folly of my heart, purify the hidden vices within me, and by your holy anointing enlarge my heart for overcoming its passions. Strengthen my senses to conquer the struggles of combat; and make me rightly angry with my vices, so that I may obtain forgiveness for all my sins.

[Col. 0502C] Lord, grant that we may unceasingly keep your fear before the eyes of our minds, so that everywhere we may think of and fear our sins and the judgment that will come because of them, while also considering and always retaining in our minds your commandments and the heavenly glory given by you to those who keep them. For you, God, who will judge us, unceasingly look down from heaven upon all our actions, thoughts, and words; and every hour the angel appointed to us in heaven announces our deeds. Therefore, fearing you, may we never depart from good meditations and actions, but always think and arrange in our hearts what pleases you.

Lord, grant us that we may take no pleasure in fulfilling our own will by any action, but may do everything according to the path of your commandments, obeying you and our superiors.

[Col. 0502D] Lord, grant us that, without murmuring of mouth or heart, throughout all the days of our lives we may truly be subject and obedient to you and to our elders.

[Note: [Col. 0502D] From the Rule of Saint Benedict.]

Lord, grant us that all things hard and harsh, contrary to our will, even those imposed upon us beyond our strength and understanding, and even these same things when commanded with insults and abuse, we may simply and humbly, in hope of your mercy, receive patiently and joyfully, without any pretense, and fulfill with great desire. Even if they are impossible for us, may we humbly and patiently make our inability known to the one commanding; and if he is unwilling in any way to alter his decision, work within our hearts so that, trusting in your help, and through the strength of mind and understanding divinely given to us, we may obey devotedly out of love, because without you we can do no good.

[Col. 0503A] Give us, Lord, that we may not presume to dispute any correction, nor try by any words to prove ourselves right, nor, through shame at appearing deformed before others, wish to blame anyone; but, cast down upon the ground, may we confess ourselves guilty and liable until the agitation of the one correcting us is healed by our humility.

Lord, grant us that we may humbly confess to our abbot, and to any other spiritual brother, all our evil thoughts and evil deeds hidden from others, so that through their correction and admonition, with your help, we may escape the snares of the devil. May our heart also always be confessing everything to you, from whom nothing is hidden.

[Col. 0503B] Lord, grant us that we may always be content with the plainness of our food, drink, and clothing; whatever their plainness, provided that by these things our body can subsist for serving you, let us not concern ourselves with [48] better things, but be satisfied with these, without deceit or hypocrisy.

Lord, grant us that every lowly condition may please us, however insignificant we may be, and that we may rejoice in being last of all in sitting, standing, ascending, speaking, and in everything that can be named. Then may we truly consider ourselves mercifully regarded by you, and give you thanks in our hearts.

Lord, grant us that, in everything imposed upon us, however lowly and contemptible it may be, and however small the service, we may believe, feel in our hearts, and carry out with great devotion that we are unworthy to perform so honorable a task.

[Col. 0503C] Lord, grant us the fruit of charity, humility, obedience, and patience, together with true brotherly love.

Lord, grant us that we may always believe from the depths of our hearts that we are more contemptible and lower than everyone else; that we may desire to be regarded and placed in this position by others, and to be called so by all, even though others neither judge nor arrange nor call us so. Do not permit us to be hypocrites, so that, while we profess with our mouths that we are unworthy and ought to be more contemptible and lower than everyone else, we may not under this humble profession wish to appear and be regarded by others as righteous and religious, while inwardly desiring the exaltation, praise, and honors of this world.

Nor permit us to be among those who, if someone tells them what they themselves confess about themselves with their own mouths, or places them as low and last as they say they ought to be, immediately break out into insults or excessive anger, going so far that, at the devil’s instigation, they withdraw from the community to which they have joined themselves; or who, concealing deceit in their hearts, reserve a time for anger; or who do not cease to slander, tear apart with insults, and obstruct those who strive to live rightly.

From these blemishes [*naevis*; Quercet., *nervis*, “sinews”], Lord, and from things of this kind cleanse our hearts.

Lord, help us, free us, and guard us, so that we may do nothing presumptuously on our own, except what the holy rule commands to be done in the monastery.

[Col. 0504A] Lord, grant us the virtue of keeping silent and speaking discreetly, so that when questioned we may answer with humility and reverence; and when we ask questions, may we ask with complete submission and reverence. Let us beware of appearing to speak more, or otherwise, than is fitting for our religious profession, our matter, or our need, about which we speak. Fortify our hearts so that we may never take pleasure in empty or superfluous glory, nor think, hear, speak, or see useless things.

Lord, have mercy on us, and make us neither quick nor ready to laugh. Rather, by your gift, may there be in us salutary contrition, humility of heart, compunction, an abundance of tears, and useful sorrow. May idle laughter, carnal joy, dissipation, and amusement be driven far from us by your power.

Lord, grant us that when we speak, we may speak softly, with seriousness, using few wholesome words, without shouting or agitation.

[Col. 0504B] Lord, grant us, miserable and unworthy as we are, that in every place and at every time, whether sitting, standing, walking, or working, we may keep our [heart] heart bowed down and humbled before you; may consider ourselves guilty at every hour because of our deeds; and, filled with the spirit of your fear and love, may each of us say in the secret of our heart: “Lord, I, a sinner, am not worthy to lift my eyes to heaven. God, be merciful to me, a sinner” (Luke XVIII, 13), always, here and forever—you who live and reign unto ages of ages. Amen.

## XII. Another Prayer

[Col. 0504C] Great are you, Lord, and greatly worthy of praise; great is your power, and there is no number to your wisdom. You stir our heart to praise and glorify you, because you made us to praise you, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.

I shall seek you, Lord, calling upon you, and I shall call upon you while believing in you; for in seeking you I shall find you, and in finding you I shall praise you. My faith calls upon you, Lord—the faith you gave me, which you inspired in me through the humanity of your Son and through the ministry of your preacher. And what place is there in me into which you may come, Lord my God, so that, coming, you may find in me the God who made heaven and earth? Or can heaven and earth, which you made and in which you made me, contain you? [49] Or, since without you nothing that exists comes to be, does it follow that whatever exists can contain you?

[Col. 0504D] Since, then, I too exist, why do I ask you to come into me, when I would not exist unless you were in me? Indeed, my God, I would not exist—no, I would not exist at all—unless you were in me.

Most high, best, most powerful, most merciful and most just, most holy, most strong, stable and incomprehensible, unchanging while changing all things; never new, never old; renewing all things and bringing the proud, even unknowingly, into old age. Always active, always at rest; gathering and yet lacking nothing; carrying and filling, protecting, creating and nourishing, perfecting and seeking, although nothing is lacking to you. You love, yet are not fevered; you are jealous, yet secure. You repent, yet do not suffer; you are angry, yet remain tranquil. You change your works, yet do not change your plan. You receive what you find, though you never lost it; you are never needy, yet rejoice in gains; never greedy, yet demand interest. More is paid to you than is due, so that you become a debtor—and who possesses anything? Do you not repay debts while owing nothing, and give what is owed without losing anything?

[Col. 0505A] And what have I said [Al., “who has spoken”], my God, my life, my holy sweetness? Or what does anyone say when speaking of you? Woe to those who are silent about you, for the talkative are mute.

Who will grant me rest in you? Who will grant that you come into my heart and intoxicate it, so that I may forget my evils and embrace you, my one good? What are you to me? Have mercy, that I may speak. What am I myself to you, that you command me to love you, and, if I do not, are angry with me and threaten me with immense miseries? Is it a small misery not to love you? Woe is me!

[Col. 0505B] Tell me, Lord God, by your mercies, what you are to me. Say to my soul: “I am your salvation” (Psalm XXXIV, 3); but say it so that I may hear. Behold, the ears of my heart are before you, Lord; open them, and say to my soul: “I am your salvation.” I shall run after this voice and seize you. Do not hide your face from me, lest I die; rather, make me see it.

The house of my soul is narrow for you to enter; let it be enlarged by you. It is in ruins; restore it. It contains many impurities of sin that offend your eyes; I confess and know this. But who else will cleanse it? To whom besides you shall I cry: “Cleanse me from my hidden faults, Lord, and spare your servant from those belonging to others” (Psalm XVIII, 13)?

Have I not spoken my offenses against myself before you, my God? Then forgive, I beg you, the wickedness of my heart. [Col. 0505C] I do not contend with you in judgment, because you are truth; and I do not wish to deceive myself, lest my iniquity lie to itself. I do not contend with you in judgment, because, “if you keep account of iniquities, Lord, Lord, who will endure?” (Psalm CXXIX, 3).

Speak to me in my supplication, merciful God; speak to me in my misery: “I am your salvation.” I have sinned, Lord my God, arranger and creator of all natural things, but never the arranger of sins. Lord my God, I sinned by acting against your commandments. For I did not become disobedient by choosing better things, but through love of doing my own will and achieving proud victories.

Deliver me, Lord, now that I call upon you. Deliver also those who do not yet call upon you, so that they may call upon you and you may deliver them.

I beg you, Lord my God, cry out within my soul what it means to love you, [Col. 0505D] so that I may hear; and may your truth say to me: “I am your salvation,” and may your consolations gladden my soul. May my wicked desires not cry out against me, nor fear what ought not to be feared. Rather, may I confess to you, my God, and accept correction for my evil ways, so that I may love your good ways.

May your laws and mercies, Lord, restrain the flow of my wickedness. Mix in salutary bitterness, recalling us to you from the destructive pleasure by which we departed from you. Hear my prayer, Lord, lest my soul fail under your discipline; nor may I fail in confessing your mercies, by which you rescue me from all my worst vices, so that you may become sweeter to me than all the seductions I have followed. May I embrace your hand with all my inmost heart, so that you may rescue me from every temptation to the end and forgive me all the sins of my evil pleasures.

[Col. 0506A] Rescue me, Lord, from the most monstrous depth of unlawful pleasures, and free me as I seek you and thirst for your delights. May my heart say to you: “I have sought your face; your face, Lord, I shall seek” (Psalm XXVI, 8).

For one goes far from your face in a darkened disposition—not by feet or distances of place—and one neither departs from you nor returns to you by physical travel. Did that younger son of yours seek horses, or chariots, or ships, or fly away on a visible wing, or travel by the movement of his legs, so that, living in a distant region, he might prodigally squander what you had given him when he departed, sweet Father, and sweeter still to one returning to the kingdom [Al., *egeno*, “needy”]? [50]

[Col. 0506B] In a lustful and darkened disposition, therefore, one goes [F., *itur*, “one goes”] far from your face. For you are good, Lord, because you are our good. I sinned because I expanded my pleasures not in you but in your creatures, and therefore I fell into pains, confusion, and errors.

But you, Lord, who always are and do not change, who always live and in whom nothing dies, say to me, your miserable servant: “I am your salvation.”

Thanks be to you, my sweetness, my honor, and my confidence, my God. Thanks be to you for all your gifts, which you have bestowed upon me; but preserve them for me. For by preserving them you will preserve me, and what you have given me will increase and be perfected. I shall be with you if you preserve me and your gifts, which you gave me, because you gave me [also] that I might exist—you who live and reign unto ages of ages. [Col. 0506C] Amen.

## XIII. Prayer at the Cross

Christ, who for us endured the cross and the gibbet of death, so that you might drive from us the power of death and free us at the price of your blood, have mercy on me, your most humble servant. Grant me forgiveness for all my sins, and, as I lie prostrate before your worshipful cross, rescue me from every evil and mercifully restore me with your good gifts.

### Another Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who are and who were, begotten with the Father before the ages, God from true God, conceived from the Holy Spirit and born as man at the end of the ages [Col. 0506D] from Mary, ever a virgin; who, obedient to the Father unto death, and death on a cross, freed us by your holy and precious blood, destroyed the dominion of death, and opened the way to heavenly glory for all who believe in you: I humbly beseech you, true God and our Lord, seated at the right hand of God the almighty Father.

I implore your infinite and ineffable mercy: by the power of this saving sign of your cross and redemption, redeem me, wretched and death-deserving sinner, from all my crimes and misdeeds; free me from all past, present, and future evils; put to death within me every vice of spiritual and bodily wickedness; make me rise with you in the power [Col. 0507A] of your glory; make me desire and seek the things above, the heavenly things; and bring me happily to the glory of eternal blessedness.

May your boundless clemency grant this, Lord Jesus Christ, God and our Lord, who with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, in the unity of the essence of the Godhead, rule all things by creating them, give them life, and govern them, through immortal ages of ages. Amen.

## XIV. This Prayer Is to Be Said at the First Hour

[Note: [Col. 0507D] The following is also found in the booklet of Charles the Bald.]

Lord God, who have brought us to the beginning of this day, preserve us by your power, so that on this day we may incline toward no sin; but may our words always proceed toward the doing of your justice. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

### Prayer at the Second Hour

[Col. 0507B]

Almighty Lord God, who have brought us to this second hour after the darkness of night, preserve us today through the span and every moment of each hour, and by your perpetual mercy [Al., “through your . . . mercy”] always make us remain unharmed. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

### Prayer at Terce

Lord God, Jesus Christ, who at the third hour of the day were led to the punishment of the cross for the salvation of the world, we humbly beseech you to blot out our sins, so that for our past evils we may always find forgiveness with you, and for the future continually have protection. You who live and reign through all ages of ages. [Col. 0507C] Amen.

### Prayer at Sext

Lord Jesus Christ, when at the sixth hour you climbed the wood of the cross for the redemption of the world, the whole world was turned in darkness [Al., Latin *in tenebris*, rather than *in tenebras*, “into darkness”]. Grant us [51] always that light in soul and body by which we may deserve to reach eternal life. You who reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit unto eternal ages.

### Prayer at None

Lord Jesus Christ, who at the ninth hour on the gibbet of the cross commanded the confessing thief to enter within the walls of paradise, we humbly beseech you [“confessing our sins”] to grant that after our death we may joyfully enter the joys of paradise. You who live and reign [Col. 0507D] through all ages of ages. Amen.

### Prayer at Vespers

We give you thanks, almighty Lord God, who have granted that through the course of this day we have reached this evening hour. We humbly beseech you that the lifting of our hands to you may be an acceptable evening sacrifice in your sight. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

### Prayer at the Twelfth Hour

[Note: [Col. 0508D] That is, of the natural day.]

Lord God, ruler and protector of all, who separated light from darkness, we earnestly implore you in our prayers that through the darkness of the coming night your right hand may protect us, so that at the dawn of light we may all rise rejoicing. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

### Prayer at Compline

Give us your peace from heaven, Lord, and may your peace, Christ, always remain in our inmost being, so that we may not fear the terror of night.

### Another

Give us your peace from heaven, Lord, and may your peace, Christ, always remain in our inmost being, so that we may sleep in peace and keep watch with Christ, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit reigns unto eternal ages.

## XV. Prayer before Communion

[Col. 0508B]

Lord Jesus Christ, only-begotten Son of God, who are and who were with the Father and the Holy Spirit, God of one essence; in whom alone is the true forgiveness of all sins, and through whom eternal life and salvation are granted; who justified the tax collector confessing his sins, heard the humble Canaanite woman calling upon you, looked upon Peter when he denied you and received him when he wept bitterly, and granted the thief who confessed you on the cross forgiveness together with the glory of paradise:

Grant me, most wretched and unhappy sinner, who confess my sins with fear and trembling, forgiveness and pardon for my crimes, so that you may grant me communion of your most holy body and blood not for judgment and condemnation, but as a remedy bringing me everlasting salvation. [Col. 0508C] Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

### Another Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who by the will of the Father and with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit gave life to the world through your death, free me through this sacred body and blood of yours from all iniquities, evil and faithless thoughts, and every evil. Make me obey your commandments, and permit me never and forever to be separated from you. Through the Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, creator and restorer of the human race, who by the will of the eternal Father, with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, deigned both to assume our flesh and to undergo death for us; who are continually sacrificed for our salvation and remain whole and entire: I glorify and exalt you, most merciful one; I sing a hymn of glory to you, who have deigned to call me, wretched and entangled in so many crimes, among the number of your servants, and have granted me to become a participant in your sacred body and blood.

I ask your eternal mercy, Lord my God, that through receiving your sacraments you may cleanse me from the filth of sins, guard me from every vice and the snares of the enemy, teach me to do your will, and lead me to the joys of the heavenly homeland. Thanks be to God. Amen.

[Col. 0509]

# 52 THIRD BOOKLET. OFFICES FOR THE WEEKDAYS, OR PSALMS ARRANGED ACCORDING TO THE INDIVIDUAL DAYS OF THE WEEK ON WHICH THEY ARE SUNG IN CHURCH, WITH PRAYERS, HYMNS, CONFESSIONS, AND LITANIES. (C,G)*

## IN THE NAME OF THE MOST HIGH GOD BEGINS THE WRITING OF ALBINUS THE TEACHER TO CHARLES THE EMPEROR

[Note: [Col. 0509D] From the royal codex of Paris and the prayer book of Charles the Bald.]

[Col. 0509A]

Blessed, therefore, was the great King David, servant of the Most High God, who gave us the rule for psalmody, teaching how every person ought to pour out prayers to God at the appointed hours, saying: “Seven times a day I praise you” (Psalm CXVIII, 164). These are the first, second, third, sixth, and ninth hours, the evening hour, and the twelfth.

At these seven hours, therefore, King David praised God. The holy prophet Daniel also, ascending to his upper room at the third, sixth, and ninth hours of the day to beseech the Lord, prayed to God for himself and for the people of Israel with his hands extended toward heaven.

The same King David also said: “And I will add to all your praise” (Psalm LXX, 14). Again he says: “At midnight I rose to confess you” (Psalm CXVIII, 62), that is, at the nocturnal hour. And again: “I remembered your name in the night, Lord” (ibid., verse 55), which is the time of cockcrow. “Thus I remembered you upon my bed; in the morning watches I will meditate on you” (Psalm LXII, 7).

These are the three courses of the office by night and the seven by day; fitted [F., *junctis*, “joined”] together, they make ten, which we sing as followers of the ten words of the law of Moses.

[Note: [Col. 0509D] Up to this point in the prayer book of Charles the Bald.]

But since you have asked us to write for you a brief guide in straightforward language, explaining how a layman who still remains in the active life ought to pray to God at these appointed hours—and although you, who live according to Christian discipline and desire to perform Christian works, are not ignorant of how one should pray to the Lord—since you have nevertheless asked, we shall briefly say what we think.

When you have risen from your bed, you should say this. First say: “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, in your name I will lift up my hands.” Say “[God,] come to my assistance” [F., *Deus*, “God”] three times [the manuscript has “three times”], with the psalm “Give ear to my words,” up to “In the morning I will stand before you.”

Then say the Lord’s Prayer and the prayers: “Deign, Lord, on this day”; “Make my steps firm”; “Blessed is the Lord day by day”; “Deign to direct and sanctify”; “Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us.”

Then, rising, let him begin the verse: “Lord, open my lips.” When it has been completed, with the Gloria, let him begin the psalm: “Lord, how they have multiplied.” Then follows: “Have mercy on me, God.” Then: “Come, let us rejoice in the Lord.” Then as many psalms as he wishes.

## MONDAY

*(Something appears to be missing.)*

### PSALM

*(Psalm CIV.)* [Note: [Col. 0510D] On the use of the psalms. For the third use above, column 466.]

Give thanks to the Lord and call upon his name; proclaim his works among the nations. Sing to him and make music to him; tell of all his wonders. Glory in his holy name; let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice. Seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek his face always. Remember his wonders that he has done, his marvels and the judgments of his mouth: the offspring of Abraham, his servant; the children of Jacob, his chosen ones.

He is the Lord our God; his judgments are throughout all the earth. He remembered his covenant forever, the word that he commanded for a thousand generations, the covenant that he made with Abraham and his oath to Isaac. He established it for Jacob as a commandment and for Israel as an everlasting covenant, saying: “To you I will give the land [53] of Canaan, the measuring-line of your inheritance.”

When they were few in number, very few, and foreigners in it, they passed from nation to nation and from one kingdom to another people. He permitted no one to harm them and rebuked kings on their behalf: “Do not touch my anointed ones, and do not act wickedly against my prophets.”

He called famine upon the land and shattered every support of bread. He sent a man before them; Joseph was sold into slavery. They humbled his feet in fetters; iron pierced his soul, until his word came to pass. The utterance of the Lord inflamed him. The king sent and released him; the ruler of peoples set him free. He appointed him lord of his house and ruler of all his possessions, to instruct his princes as himself and teach his elders wisdom.

And Israel entered Egypt, and Jacob became a sojourner in the land of Ham. He greatly increased his people and made them stronger than their enemies. He turned their hearts so that they hated his people and dealt deceitfully with his servants. He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen. He placed among them the words of his signs and wonders in the land of Ham.

He sent darkness and made it dark; and he did not embitter his words. He changed their waters into blood and killed their fish. Their land brought forth frogs, in the inner chambers of their kings. He spoke, and there came flies and gnats throughout all their borders. He made their rains hail, with fire consuming their land. He struck their vines and fig trees and shattered the trees within their borders.

He spoke, and locusts and caterpillars came, beyond number. They consumed all the grass in their land and devoured all the fruit of their soil. He struck every firstborn in their land, the firstfruits of all their labor. He brought them out with silver and gold, and there was no feeble one among their tribes.

Egypt rejoiced at their departure, because fear of them had fallen upon the Egyptians. He spread a cloud for their protection and fire to give them light by night. They asked, and quail came; and he satisfied them with the bread of heaven. He split the rock, and waters flowed; rivers ran through dry places.

For he remembered his holy word, which he had spoken to Abraham his servant. He brought out his people with rejoicing and his chosen ones with gladness. He gave them the regions of the nations, and they possessed the labor of peoples, so that they might keep his statutes and seek his law.

As above: “Lord, your mercy is in heaven, and your truth reaches to the clouds.” Deign to hear us who call upon your name, Lord.

### Prayer

We beseech you, Lord, hear us who call upon your name: just as, with the power of your name going before them, you refreshed our fathers with angelic food, so may you also nourish and renew us with mystical fare. Through him.

### PSALM

*(Psalm CV.)*

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy is forever. Who can speak of the mighty deeds of the Lord or make all his praises heard? Blessed are those who keep judgment and practice justice at all times.

Remember us, Lord, in the goodwill of your people; visit us with your salvation, so that we may see the prosperity of your chosen ones, rejoice in the joy of your nation, and that you may be praised with your inheritance.

We have sinned with our fathers; we have acted unjustly and committed iniquity. Our fathers in Egypt did not understand your wonders; they did not remember the multitude of your mercies. They provoked you as they went up to the sea, the Red Sea. Yet he saved them for the sake of his name, to make his power known. He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up; he led them through the depths as through a desert. He saved them from the hand of those who hated them and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy. The water covered their oppressors; not one of them remained. They believed his words and sang his praise.

They quickly forgot his works and did not wait for his counsel. They desired desire in the desert and tempted God in the waterless place. He gave them what they asked for and sent abundance into their souls. They provoked [54] Moses in the camp, Aaron, the holy one of the Lord. The earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered the assembly of Abiron. Fire blazed in their assembly; flame consumed the sinners.

They made a calf at Horeb and worshiped a cast image. They exchanged their glory for the likeness of a calf that eats grass. They forgot God, who saved them, who had done great things in Egypt, wonders in the land of Ham, and terrible deeds at the Red Sea.

He said that he would destroy them, had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him to turn away his anger, lest he destroy them. They considered the desirable land worthless; they did not believe his word and murmured in their tents; they did not hear the voice of the Lord.

He lifted his hand against them, to overthrow them in the desert, to cast down their offspring among the nations, and to scatter them throughout the lands. They were initiated into Beelphegor and ate the sacrifices of the dead. They provoked him by their inventions, and destruction multiplied among them.

Then Phinehas stood up and made atonement, and the plague ceased. It was counted to him as righteousness from generation to generation, forever.

They provoked him at the waters of contradiction, and Moses was afflicted because of them, because they embittered his spirit. He spoke rashly with his lips. They did not destroy the nations of which the Lord had spoken to them. They mingled among the nations and learned their works. They served their cast images, and these became a stumbling block to them.

They sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons. They shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters, whom they sacrificed to the cast images of Canaan. The land was defiled with blood, polluted by their works, and they fornicated in their inventions.

The Lord was enraged with fury against his people and abhorred his inheritance. He delivered them into the hands of the nations, and those who hated them ruled over them. Their enemies oppressed them, and they were humbled under their hands. Often he delivered them, but they provoked him by their counsel and were humbled by their iniquities.

He saw when they were in distress and heard their prayer. He remembered his covenant and relented according to the multitude of his mercies. He made them objects of compassion in the sight of all those who had taken them captive.

Save us, Lord our God, and gather us from among the nations, so that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise. Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, from age to age; and all the people shall say: “Amen, amen.”

As above: “God, your way is in the holy place; what god is great like our God? You are the God who works wonders.”

### Prayer

Remember us, Lord, in the goodwill of your people, and, having shaken us free from the slavery of sin, save us through the visitation of your salvation. Through the Lord.

### PSALM
### (Psalm 106)

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever. Let those [Col. 0513A] redeemed by the Lord say so, those whom he redeemed from the hand of the enemy and gathered from the regions—from the rising and the setting of the sun, from the north and from the sea.

They wandered in the wilderness, in a waterless region; they did not find the way to an inhabited city. Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted within them. And they cried to the Lord in their distress, and he delivered them from their necessities. And he led them by a straight way, so that they might go to an inhabited city.

Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies, and for his wonders to the children of men. For he satisfied the empty soul, and filled the hungry soul with good things.

Those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, bound in poverty and iron, because they had provoked the words of God and defied the counsel of the Most High: their heart was humbled by labors; they were weakened, [Col. 0513B] and there was no one to help. And they cried to the Lord in their distress, and he delivered them from their necessities. And he led them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and broke their bonds.

Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies, **55** and for his wonders to the children of men. For he shattered bronze gates and broke iron bars.

He took them from the way of their iniquity, for they had been humbled because of their injustices. Their soul abhorred every kind of food, and they drew near to the gates of death. And they cried to the Lord in their distress, and he delivered them from their necessities. He sent his word and healed them, and rescued them from their destructions.

Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies, and for his wonders to the children of men. And let them offer a sacrifice of praise [Col. 0513C] and proclaim his works with rejoicing.

Those who go down to the sea in ships, doing their work upon the great waters: they have seen the works of the Lord and his wonders in the deep. He spoke, and the spirit of the storm arose, and its waves were lifted up. They rose to the heavens and descended to the depths; their soul wasted away in calamities. They were troubled and shaken like a drunken man, and all their wisdom was swallowed up. And they cried to the Lord in their distress, and he brought them out of their necessities. He turned his storm into a breeze, and its waves were silent. And they rejoiced because they were silent, and he led them into the harbor of their desire.

Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies, and for his wonders to the children of men. And let them exalt him in [Col. 0513D] the assembly of the people, and praise him in the seat of the elders.

He made rivers into wilderness and springs of water into thirst; a fruitful land into salt because of the wickedness of its inhabitants. He made the wilderness into pools of water and a waterless land into springs of water. And he settled the hungry there, and they established an inhabited city. They sowed fields and planted vineyards, and they produced the fruit of the harvest. And he blessed them, and they multiplied greatly, and he did not diminish their livestock.

Then they became few and were afflicted by the trouble of evils and by sorrow. Contention was poured out upon princes, and he made them wander in a trackless place and not on a road. And he helped the poor in their want, and made families like sheep.

The upright will see this and rejoice, and every iniquity will shut its mouth. Who is wise and will keep these things, and will understand the mercies of the Lord?

As above: “I will sing of the mercies of the Lord forever; from generation to generation I will proclaim your truth with my mouth.”

**Prayer.** We confess, Lord, your mercies, which you continually exercise toward our necessities; and we ask that you, who exalted sit in the churches [F., in the heights] at the right hand of the Father upon the throne, grant us both to understand and to keep the mystery of such great compassion. Through him.

**PSALM.**

[Col. 0514A]

### (Psalm 110)

I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart, in the council of the upright and in the assembly. Great are the works of the Lord, sought out according to all his purposes. [Col. 0514B] His work is confession and majesty, and his righteousness endures forever and ever. He has made his wonders memorable; the Lord is merciful and compassionate. He has given food to those who fear him.

He will remember his covenant forever; he will proclaim the power of his works to his people, so as to give them the inheritance of the nations. The works of his hands are truth and judgment. All his commandments are faithful, established forever and ever, made in truth and equity.

He sent redemption to his people; he commanded his covenant forever. Holy and terrible is his name. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. Good understanding belongs to all who practice it; his praise endures forever and ever.

As above: “I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart; I will recount all your wonders.” [Col. 0514C]

**Prayer.** O God, glorious praise of all the saints, grant us fear of your name, which you declared to be the beginning of wisdom, so that, entrusted to the councils of your mercy, we may be nourished with your provisions. Through him.

**56 PSALM.**

### (Psalm 111)

Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he takes great delight in his commandments. His offspring will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed. Glory and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever and ever.

Light has risen in the darkness for the upright: he is merciful, compassionate, and righteous. The good man shows mercy and lends; he orders his words with judgment, for he will never be shaken. The righteous will be remembered forever; he will not fear an evil report. [Col. 0514D]

His heart is ready to hope in the Lord; his heart is strengthened, and he will not be shaken until he looks down upon his enemies. He has distributed and given to the poor; his righteousness endures forever and ever, and his horn will be exalted in glory.

The sinner will see and be angry; he will gnash his teeth and waste away. The desire of sinners will perish.

As above: “The heavens will proclaim your wonders, Lord, and indeed your truth in the assembly of the saints.”

**Prayer.** O God, everlasting light of upright hearts, grant us to love you, to rejoice in your glory, and so to despise this present age that we may avoid a harsh hearing in the future. Through him.

**PSALM.**

[Col. 0515A]

### (Psalm 112)

Praise the Lord, servants; praise the name of the Lord. May the name of the Lord be blessed, from this time forth and forever. From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

The Lord is exalted above all nations, and his glory is above the heavens. Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high and looks upon the lowly in heaven and on earth? He raises the needy from the earth and lifts the poor from the dungheap, to place him with princes, with the princes of his people. He makes the barren woman dwell in a house as a joyful mother of children.

As above: “May his name be blessed forever; may his name endure before the sun. And blessed be the name of his majesty forever, and may all the earth be filled with his majesty. Amen, amen.” [Col. 0515B]

**Prayer.** O almighty God, as we praise your blessed name, we ask that, having been placed in the bosom of Mother Church, you may join us firmly to the stability of your charity. Through him.

**PSALM.**

### (Psalm 113)

When Israel went out from Egypt, the house of Jacob from a barbarous people, Judah became his sanctification, Israel his dominion. The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back. The mountains leaped like rams, and the hills like lambs of the flock.

What is wrong with you, sea, that you fled? And you, Jordan, that you turned back? Mountains, why did you leap like rams, and hills like lambs of the flock? At the presence of the Lord [Col. 0515C] the earth was moved, at the presence of the God of Jacob, who turned the rock into pools of water and the cliff into springs of water.

Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, because of your mercy and your truth. Let the nations never say, “Where is their God?” But our God is in heaven; he has done whatever he wished.

The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the works of human hands. They have mouths, but they will not speak; they have eyes, but they will not see. They have ears, but they will not hear; they have nostrils, but they will not smell. They have hands, but they will not touch; they have feet, but they will not walk; they will not cry out through their throat.

Let those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them.

The house of Israel has hoped in the Lord; he is their helper and protector. [Col. 0515D] The house of Aaron has hoped in the Lord; he is their helper and protector. Those who fear the Lord have hoped in the Lord; he is their helper and protector.

The Lord has remembered us and has blessed us. He has blessed the house of Israel; he has blessed the house of Aaron. He has blessed all who fear the Lord, small and great alike.

**57** May the Lord add to you—to you and to your children. Blessed are you by the Lord, who made heaven and earth. The heaven of heavens belongs to the Lord, but he gave the earth to the children of men.

The dead will not praise you, Lord, nor all who descend into the underworld. But we who live bless the Lord, from this time forth and forever.

As above: “Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.”

[Col. 0516A] **Prayer.** O God, ineffable name of the Trinity, who by the sight of your light terrified the streams of the Jordan, grant that those whom you renewed after washing them in holy baptism may never be defiled by forbidden idols of images. Through him.

**PSALM.**

### (Psalm 114)

I have loved, because the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer. For he has inclined his ear to me; I will call upon him throughout my days. The pains of death surrounded me, and the dangers of the underworld found me. I found tribulation and sorrow, and I called upon the name of the Lord.

O Lord, deliver my soul. The Lord is merciful and just, and our God has mercy. The Lord preserves the little ones; I was humbled, and he delivered me. Return, my soul, to your rest, [Col. 0516B] for the Lord has dealt kindly with you. For he has rescued my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from falling. I will please the Lord in the land of the living.

As above: “My vows are upon me, O God; I will repay them with praises to you. For you have rescued my soul from death and my feet from falling, so that I may please God in the light of the living.”

**Prayer.** O Lord, cleanser of sins, who swiftly console the soul that faithfully calls upon you, we ask that, having rescued us from the dangers of the underworld in the land of the living, you may restore us, with the death of sin removed. Through him.

**PSALM.**

### (Psalm 115)

I believed, therefore I spoke; [Col. 0516C] but I was greatly humbled. I said in my alarm, “Every human being is a liar.” What shall I repay the Lord for all that he has repaid me? I will take up the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord. I will fulfill my vows to the Lord in the presence of all his people.

Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints. O Lord, for I am your servant; I am your servant and the son of your handmaid. You have broken my bonds; I will sacrifice to you a sacrifice of praise and call upon the name of the Lord. I will fulfill my vows to the Lord in the presence of all his people, in the courts of the house of the Lord, in your midst, Jerusalem.

As above: “Rejoice in the Lord and confess the memory of his sanctification.”

[Col. 0516D] **Prayer.** May the life of your suppliants, we ask, O Lord, be such as the precious death of the saints is in your sight, so that, freed from the bonds of sin, we may be worthy to taste beforehand the joys of the Jerusalem to come. Through the Lord.

**PSALM.**

### (Psalm 116)

Praise the Lord, all nations; praise him, all peoples. For his mercy has been confirmed upon us, and the truth of the Lord endures forever.

As above: “Let all the earth adore you, O God, and sing psalms to you; I will sing a psalm to your name.”

**Prayer.** Most almighty ruler, praised by the mouths of all nations, we ask that you spread your truth in our minds and confirm your mercy upon us. Through him.

**58 PSALM.**

[Col. 0517A]

### (Psalm 117)

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever. Let Israel now say that he is good, for his mercy endures forever. Let the house of Aaron now say, for his mercy endures forever. Let those who fear the Lord now say, for his mercy endures forever.

I called upon the Lord in my distress, and the Lord heard me and brought me into a broad place. The Lord is my helper; I will not fear what man can do to me. The Lord is my helper, and I will look down upon my enemies.

It is better to trust in the Lord than to trust in man. It is better to hope in the Lord than to hope in princes.

All nations surrounded me, [Col. 0517B] and in the name of the Lord I took vengeance upon them. They surrounded me on every side, and in the name of the Lord I took vengeance upon them. They surrounded me like bees and burned like fire among thorns, and in the name of the Lord I took vengeance upon them.

I was pushed and overturned so that I might fall, but the Lord received me. The Lord is my strength and my praise, and he has become my salvation. The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous. The right hand of the Lord has shown strength; the right hand of the Lord has exalted me; the right hand of the Lord has shown strength.

I shall not die, but live, and I shall recount the works of the Lord. The Lord chastising has chastised me, but he has not delivered me to death.

Open to me the gates of righteousness; entering through them, I will give thanks to the Lord. This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it. I will give thanks to you, for you [Col. 0517C] have heard me and have become my salvation.

The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This was done by the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes. This is the day which the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.

O Lord, save me; O Lord, grant prosperity. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. We have blessed you from the house of the Lord. God is the Lord, and he has shone upon us. Appoint a solemn day amid the thick branches, up to the horns of the altar.

You are my God, and I will give thanks to you; you are my God, and I will exalt you. I will give thanks to you, for you have heard me and have become my salvation.

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.

As above: “Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.” [Col. 0517D]

**Prayer.** O most merciful Lord, consolation of our tribulations, who fills the tents of the righteous with joy and rejoicing, exalt your Church by the strength of your powerful right hand, so that it may become the gate of righteousness; and let it so join itself by the stability of the cornerstone that, glorified by your resurrection, it may shine. Through him.

**PSALM.**

### (Psalm 134)

Praise the name of the Lord; praise the Lord, servants. You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God, praise the Lord, for the Lord is good; sing psalms to his name, for it is sweet.

For the Lord chose Jacob for himself, Israel as his possession. For I have known that the Lord is great [Col. 0518A] and that our God is above all gods. Whatever the Lord wished, he did in heaven and on earth, in the sea and in all the depths.

He brings clouds from the end of the earth; he makes lightning into rain. He brings forth winds from his treasuries. He struck the firstborn of Egypt, from man to beast. He sent signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants. He struck many nations and killed mighty kings: Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan. And he gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance for Israel his people.

Lord, your name endures forever; Lord, your memorial from generation to generation. For the Lord will judge his people, and he will have compassion on his servants.

The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the works of human hands. They have mouths, but they will not speak; they have eyes, but they will not see. They have ears, but they will not hear, for there is no breath in their mouths. Let those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them.

House of Israel, bless the Lord; house of Aaron, bless the Lord. [Col. 0518B] House of Levi, bless the Lord; you who fear the Lord, bless the Lord. Blessed is the Lord from Zion, who dwells in Jerusalem.

As above: “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, from age to age and forever, and let all the people say: Amen, amen.”

**Prayer.** O God of extraordinary sweetness, whom the whole earth praises for the sweetness of your kindness, we ask that, having removed from us the error of vain superstition, we may be joined to your will. Through him.

**PSALM.**

[Col. 0518C]

### (Psalm 135)

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy is everlasting. Give thanks to the God of gods, for his mercy is everlasting. Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his mercy is everlasting.

He alone does great wonders, for his mercy is everlasting. He made the heavens with understanding, for his mercy is everlasting. He established the earth upon the waters, for his mercy is everlasting. He made the great lights, for his mercy is everlasting: the sun to rule the day, for his mercy is [Col. 0518D] everlasting; the moon and stars to rule the night, for his mercy is everlasting.

He struck Egypt together with its firstborn, for his mercy is everlasting. He brought Israel out from their midst, for his mercy is everlasting, with a powerful hand and an outstretched arm, for his mercy is everlasting. He divided the Red Sea into sections, for his mercy is everlasting, and led Israel through its midst, for his mercy is everlasting. He shook off Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea, for his mercy is everlasting.

He led his people through the wilderness, for his mercy endures forever. He struck great kings, for his mercy is everlasting, and killed [Col. 0519A] mighty kings, for his mercy is everlasting: Sihon king of the Amorites, for his mercy is everlasting, and Og king of Bashan, for his mercy is everlasting.

He gave their land as an inheritance, for his mercy is everlasting, an inheritance for Israel his servant, for his mercy is everlasting. He remembered us in our humiliation, for his mercy is everlasting, and redeemed us from our enemies, for his mercy is everlasting. He gives food to all flesh, for his mercy is everlasting.

Give thanks to the God of heaven, for his mercy is everlasting. Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his mercy is everlasting.

As above: “Lord, you have become our refuge from generation to generation.” [Col. 0519B]

**Prayer.** Remembering our lowliness, have mercy on us, almighty God; and as you once gave the land of our enemies to our fathers as an inheritance, so establish us, freed from the stain of sin, in your inheritance. Through him.

**PSALM.**

### (Psalm 145)

Praise the Lord, my soul; I will praise the Lord during my life; I will sing psalms to my God as long as I exist. Do not trust in princes, in human beings, in whom there is no salvation. His spirit will go forth, and he will return to his earth; on that day all their thoughts will perish.

Blessed is he whose helper is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God, [Col. 0519C] who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them. He keeps truth forever, executes justice for those who suffer wrong, and gives food to the hungry.

The Lord frees those in chains; the Lord gives sight to the blind. The Lord raises up those who are bowed down; the Lord loves the righteous. The Lord protects the strangers; he will receive the orphan and the widow, and he will destroy the ways of sinners. The Lord will reign forever, your God, Zion, from generation to generation.

**60 As above:** “Exalt our Lord and adore him on his holy mountain, for the Lord our God is holy.” [Col. 0519D]

**Prayer.** Glorious almighty God, in whom the souls of the blessed place the whole confidence of their hope, grant us that, enlightened by your help, we may continually love you with a pure mind. Through him.

**PSALM.**

### (Psalm 146)

Praise the Lord, for the psalm is good; let praise of our God be joyful and fitting. The Lord builds Jerusalem; he will gather the dispersed of Israel. He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds. He counts the multitude of the stars and calls them all by name.

Great is our Lord, and great is his power; his wisdom is without measure. The Lord lifts up the meek, but humbles sinners to the ground. Sing beforehand to the Lord with confession; sing psalms to our God on the lyre.

He covers the heavens with clouds and prepares rain for the earth. He makes grass grow on the mountains [Col. 0520A] and plants for the service of human beings. He gives their food to the animals and to the young ravens that call upon him.

He will not take pleasure in the strength of a horse, nor will the legs of a man please him. The Lord’s pleasure is in those who fear him and in those who hope in his mercy.

As above: “Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us, just as we have hoped in you.”

**Prayer.** O God, builder of the heavenly Jerusalem, who both enclose the multitude of the stars within a number and call each one by name, heal, we ask, the brokenhearted; gather the dispersed; and enrich us in your immeasurable wisdom. Through him.

**PSALM.**

[Col. 0520B]

### (Psalm 147)

Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion. For he has strengthened the bars of your gates; he has blessed your children within you. He has established peace within your borders and satisfies you with the fat of wheat.

He sends forth his word to the earth; his message runs swiftly. He gives snow like wool and scatters mist like ashes. He sends his ice like morsels; who can withstand the face of his cold? He will send his word and melt them; his spirit will blow, and the waters will flow.

He announces his word to Jacob, his statutes and judgments to Israel. He has not dealt thus with every nation, and he has not revealed his judgments to them.

As above: “I will give thanks to the Lord according to his righteousness, and I will sing psalms to the name of the Lord Most High.”

[Col. 0520C] **Prayer.** Strengthen, Lord, the gates of your Church, and establish peace within her boundaries; graciously grant her the richness of spiritual wheat. Through him.

**PSALM.**

### (Psalm 148)

Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the heights. Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his powers. Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, all stars and light. Praise him, heavens of heavens, and let the waters that are above the heavens praise the name of the Lord.

For he spoke, and they were made; he commanded, and they were created. He established them forever and ever; he gave a command, and it will not pass away.

Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all abysses. Fire, hail, snow, ice, [Col. 0520D] and storm winds, which do his word; mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars; beasts and all cattle, creeping things and winged birds; kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all judges of the earth; young men and maidens, old men **61** together with the young—let them praise the name of the Lord, for his name alone is exalted.

His praise is above heaven and earth, and he has exalted the horn of his people. A hymn belongs to all his saints, to the children of Israel, the people who draw near to him.

As above: “Wonderful is God in his saints; the God of Israel himself will give strength and power to his people. Blessed be God.”

**Prayer.** O God, supreme and exalted power of the lofty thrones, grant your servants that, [Col. 0521A] just as all that we see was created at your command, so what you have commanded may be preserved under your protection. Through him.

**PSALM.**

### (Psalm 149)

Sing to the Lord a new song; his praise is in the assembly of the saints. Let Israel rejoice in him who made him, and let the daughters of Zion exult in their king. Let them praise his name in the chorus; let them sing psalms to him with tambourine and lyre.

For the Lord takes pleasure in his people, and he has exalted the meek for salvation. The saints will exult in glory; they will rejoice in their resting places. The exaltations of God are in their throats, and two-edged swords are in their hands, to execute vengeance upon the nations and rebukes upon the peoples; to bind their kings in fetters and their nobles [Col. 0521B] in iron chains; to execute upon them the judgment that has been written. This glory belongs to all his saints.

As above: “It is good to give thanks to the Lord and sing psalms to your name, Most High; to proclaim your mercy in the morning and your truth through the night.”

**Prayer.** O God, author of all goodness, who exalts every meek person who humbly confesses you, grant that, just as you make your saints exult in glory, so you may graciously guard the present Church forever undefiled by the pleasures of this age. Through the Lord.

**PSALM.**

### (Psalm 150)

Praise the Lord in his saints; praise him in the firmament of his power. Praise him in his powers; praise him according to the multitude [Col. 0521C] of his greatness. Praise him with the sound of the trumpet; praise him with lyre and harp. Praise him with tambourine and chorus; praise him with strings and organ. Praise him with well-sounding cymbals; praise him with cymbals of jubilation. Let every spirit praise the Lord.

As above: “Praise his name, for the Lord is sweet; his mercy is everlasting, and his truth endures from generation to generation.”

Thus I will sing a psalm to your name forever and ever, that I may fulfill my vows from day to day.

**Prayer.** O God, sweetest melody of our harmony, who commands the melodies of our breast to be exercised now with breath, now with tears, grant that, while we sing them with spiritual affection, we may be inserted into everlasting choirs [Col. 0521D] and praise you with all the saints. Through him.

## HYMN OF THE THREE YOUNG MEN

### (Daniel 3)

Bless all the works of the Lord, Lord; praise and exalt him above all forever. Bless the angels of the Lord, Lord; bless the heavens, Lord. Bless all waters that are above the heavens, Lord; bless all the powers of the Lord, Lord. Bless the sun and moon, Lord; bless the stars of heaven, Lord. Bless rain and dew, Lord; bless every spirit of God, Lord. Bless fire and heat, Lord; bless cold and heat, Lord. Bless dews and frost, Lord; bless ice and cold, Lord. Bless ice [62] and snow, Lord; bless nights and days, Lord. [Col. 0522A]

Bless light and darkness, Lord; bless lightning and clouds, Lord. Let the earth bless the Lord; let it praise and exalt him forever. Bless mountains and hills, Lord; bless all things that grow upon the earth, Lord. Bless springs, Lord; bless seas and rivers, Lord. Bless whales and all that move in the waters, Lord. Bless all birds of the heavens, Lord. Bless all beasts and cattle, Lord; bless the children of men, Lord.

Let Israel bless the Lord; let it praise and exalt him forever. Bless the priests of the Lord, Lord; bless the servants of the Lord, Lord. Bless spirits and souls of the righteous, Lord; bless saints and the humble of heart, Lord. Bless Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, Lord; [Col. 0522B] praise and exalt him forever. Let us bless the Father and the Son with the Holy Spirit; let us praise and exalt him forever.

Blessed are you, Lord, in the firmament of heaven; worthy of praise, glorious, and exalted forever.

**Prayer.** O God, through whom faith does not feel the fire, while unbelief is burned without fire; you caused the most blessed three young men, armed with faith and cast into the furnace of fire, to sing a hymn to you with joyful faces, unharmed in every respect. We beseech you to deign likewise to arm us with faith and devotion and fill us with the strength of your fear, so that, freed from the furnace of vices, we may deserve to sing a hymn and exalt your name forever.

## LITANY

Spare, Lord, spare your people, whom you redeemed, [Col. 0522C] Christ, with your blood; do not be angry with us forever.

Christ, hear us. Grant me, O God, first to ask you rightly; then make me worthy to be heard; then hear me.

Holy Mary, pray for us. Holy Mary, intercede for me, a sinner. Holy Mary, help me on the day of my departure from this present life.

Holy John, pray for us. Holy Peter, pray for us. Holy Paul, pray for us. Holy Andrew, pray for us. Holy James, pray for us. [Col. 0522D] Holy John, pray for us. Holy Thomas, pray for us. Holy James, pray for us. Holy Philip, pray for us. Holy Bartholomew, pray for us. Holy Matthew, pray for us. Holy Thaddeus, pray for us. All holy apostles, pray for us.

Holy Stephen, pray for us. Holy Linus, pray for us. Holy Cletus, pray for us. Holy Clement, pray for us. Holy Sixtus, pray for us. Holy Cornelius, pray for us. [Col. 0523A] Holy Cyprian, pray for us. Holy Dionysius, with your companions, pray for us. Holy Lawrence, pray for us. Holy Maurice, with your companions, pray for us. Holy Cosmas, pray for us. Holy Damian, pray for us. All holy martyrs, pray for us.

Holy Hilary, pray for us. Holy Martin, pray for us. Holy Sylvester, pray for us. Holy Leo, pray for us. Holy Ambrose, pray for us. Holy Gregory, pray for us. Holy Germanus, pray for us. Holy Remigius, pray for us. [Col. 0523B] Holy Amandus, pray for us. Holy Chrodobert, pray for us. Holy Jerome, pray for us. Holy Benedict, pray for us. Holy Maurus, pray for us. Holy Babolene, pray for us. All holy confessors, pray for us.

Holy Felicity, pray for us. Holy Perpetua, pray for us. Holy Agatha, pray for us. Holy Lucy, pray for us. Holy Cecilia, pray for us. Holy Agnes, pray for us. Holy Anastasia, pray for us. Holy Euphemia, pray for us. [Col. 0523C] Holy Petronilla, pray for us. Holy Susanna, pray for us. Holy Brigid, pray for us. **63** All holy virgins, pray for us.

Be favorable, spare us, Lord. Be favorable, deliver us, Lord. From every evil, deliver us, Lord. From every temptation, deliver us, Lord. From every evil thought, deliver us, Lord. From every iniquity, deliver us, Lord. From every impurity of heart and body, deliver us, Lord. By your cross, deliver us, Lord.

We sinners ask you: hear us. That you may deign to grant us peace, Lord Jesus, we ask you: hear us. That you may deign to grant us forgiveness of our offenses, Lord Jesus, we ask you: hear us. That you may deign to grant us remission of our sins, Lord Jesus, we ask you: hear us. That you may graciously pour the grace of the Holy Spirit into our hearts, Lord Jesus, we ask you: hear us. That you may deign to grant us the intercession of your saints, Lord Jesus, we ask you: hear us. [Col. 0524A]

That you may deign to grant us your holy charity, Lord Jesus, we ask you: hear us. That you may deign to grant us right faith, Lord Jesus, we ask you: hear us. That you may deign to grant us firm hope in your goodness, Lord Jesus, we ask you: hear us. That you may deign to grant us eternal life, Lord Jesus, we ask you: hear us. That you may deign to grant us praise of your holy name, Lord Jesus, we ask you: hear us.

Son of God, we ask you: hear us. Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us. [Col. 0524B] Christ, hear us. Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy. Our Father.

Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, for my soul trusts in you. Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and your glory over all the earth, so that your beloved may be delivered. I will sing psalms to you, my helper, because you are my God, my protector; my God, my mercy. I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth. Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.

**Prayer.** O God, sweetest melody of our harmony, who commands the melodies of our breast to be exercised now with torches [Al., breaths], now with tears, grant, we ask, Lord, that we who sing them with spiritual [affection], inserted into everlasting choirs, [Col. 0524C] may deserve to rejoice with all the saints. Through him.

## MONDAY. PURE CONFESSION OF SINS BY ALCUIN

[Note: [Col. 0523D] It appears in the little book of prayers of Charles the Bald, p. 11, under this title: “The confession which Alcuin composed for the emperor Charles.” In Martene, *On the Ancient Discipline of the Church*, [Col. 0524D] p. 647.]

[Note: [Col. 0524D] For the first use, above, col. 466.]

O immeasurable God of mercy, God of boundless compassion, God, creator and restorer of the human race, who purify the hearts of those who confess to you and absolve those who accuse themselves before the sight of your divine clemency from every bond of iniquity: with all my groans I beseech your power to grant me, according to the multitude of your mercies, a pure confession before you concerning all my sins of which my conscience accuses me; and to grant me true and worthy repentance for all these things: whatever I have sinned in wicked thoughts, perverse meditations, evil consent, iniquitous counsel, lust and unclean pleasure, idle words, malicious deeds, sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch.

For you, merciful God, gave me each of my limbs, fitted for human use, so that I might work out the salvation of my soul; but I, most wretched and sinful of all, despised you, the author of eternal salvation, and, at the urging of the enemy who was preparing eternal fires for me, consented [Cod. Reg.: “and I consented to the one who prepared eternal fires for me”]. I fell into sins; I collapsed into pleasures [Alt.: offenses]. [Col. 0525A] In each of my limbs I exceeded nature’s proper measure and made myself liable to impious labors.

My feet were exceedingly swift in running toward evil and following lust, but feeble in obeying your commandments. My legs were strong for sustaining me in evil [Cod. Reg.: “strong”]. I bent my knees more readily to fornication than to prayer. In my thighs and genitals I did not fear defiling myself beyond measure with every impurity [Cod. Reg.: “being defiled with every impurity”], and I made myself guilty every hour.

My belly and all my inward parts are continually distended with gluttony and drunkenness. In my kidneys and loins I burn with a most shameful desire, through diabolical deception and the flame of lust. For my sides do not fear committing the wickedness of wantonness [Cod. Reg.: “the wantonness of wickedness”]. [Col. 0525B] I strengthened my back for wicked deeds and raised my neck in carnal pride. My shoulders [“as newly said”] I subjected to carrying the burdens of wickedness, and I continually offered my arms for seductive embraces.

My hands are full of blood and polluted with every filth; ready for every evil work, sluggish for doing anything good. My mouth has been polluted by a foul kiss and stained by wicked desire; with luxurious words, idle tales, and lies I have defiled myself beyond measure. Ever devoted to gluttony and drunkenness, I have never been satisfied with carnal desires. My tongue too has been profaned by every deceit. My throat continually burns with insatiable greed.

My ears are dulled by deceitful speech [Alt.: “blunted”], ready for every evil, deaf to every good. In my nostrils I have often taken pleasure in wicked odors, in which I did not at all shrink from the stench of sins. What, then, shall I say of my eyes, which have made me liable to everything and turned away every sense of my heart, with which I consented to every lust? They also perverted me by their wicked gaze when, though rarely, I adored you, Lord, in your sanctuary, and they dragged every movement of my body toward unclean desires.

But my head, rising above all the other limbs, I scarcely ever bowed to you, God my creator; rather, I made it agree with my other limbs [The word “limbs” is omitted in Cod. Reg.] in every wickedness. My heart, full of deceit and evil, I have never cleansed with pure repentance; I have always been polluted by diabolical deception and never washed clean by true confession.

For in recounting these things I do not blaspheme your creature in me, Lord; rather, I ask you, most loving God, for healing from you, since I recognize myself guilty beyond measure in all my limbs: for I know that my offenses are as innumerable as the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea.

Moreover, I confess that I am subject to anger, sadness, spiritual sloth, boastfulness, laziness, and all eight principal vices. But you, Lord, knower of hidden things, who said that you prefer the repentance of sinners to their death, to you I shall reveal all the secrets of my heart.
