In everlasting remembrance. Eternal rest. May they rest in peace.

## Thursday: Confession of Sins after Receiving Rest

### [Col. 0553A]

[Note: [Col. 0553] Beginning in the booklet of Charles the Bald, p. 113. For the seventh use, above, col. 467.]

I confess to you, Lord, all my sins, whatever I have done, committed, and perpetrated throughout all the days of my life. God, who created all things, you know my sins; forgive and have mercy on me, because I have sinned against you exceedingly. Lord, have mercy on me. Through the intercession of all angels and archangels, have mercy on me. Through the intercession of patriarchs and prophets, have mercy on me. Through the intercession of apostles, martyrs, confessors, and virgins, I beseech you, have mercy on me.

Lord, even if I have sinned against you, nevertheless I have not abandoned you; I have not worshiped foreign gods. Have mercy on me, Lord. I ask forgiveness from you for all my faults. Merciful God, I confess my sins to you, because I acknowledge crimes in myself. Be favorable to me, God, your sinful servant; do not desert me, do not abandon me, my God.

Merciful God, holy and mighty, holy and immortal, most merciful and compassionate God, help me, your sinful servant. Give me a heart that fears you, understanding that comprehends you, eyes that see you, ears that hear you, and nostrils that receive your fragrance. Lord, soften my hard and stony heart, for I am dead ashes. Save me, Lord, while I am awake; guard me while I sleep, so that I may sleep in peace and keep watch in Christ. Amen.

I beseech you, Lord, that you repay eternally all who wish or do good to me; and if there are any who wish or do evil to me, grant them forgiveness. Merciful God, grant me, your servant, remission of sins and a perfect end; lead me onto the way of salvation.

## Another Prayer

Grant me, I ask, Lord, firm faith in my heart, the helmet of salvation on my head, the sign of Christ on my forehead, the word of truth in my mouth, good will in my mind, love of God in my breast, a girding of chastity around me, honesty in action, sobriety in conscience, humility in prosperity, patience in tribulation, hope in the Creator, perseverance to the end, and love of eternal life. By the favor of the Lord.

## Prayer of Saint Benedict

Deign to grant me, merciful and holy Father, understanding that understands you, perception that senses you, a mind that savors you, diligence that seeks you, wisdom that finds you, a mind that knows you, inward affections that love you, a heart that thinks of you, an act that increases you, hearing that hears you, eyes that see you, a tongue that proclaims you, conduct that pleases you, patience that endures you, perseverance that awaits you, a perfect end, your holy presence, a good resurrection, recompense, and eternal life. Amen.

## Psalm

### (Psalm 33)

I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth. In the Lord my soul will be praised; let the meek hear and rejoice. Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together. I sought the Lord, and he heard me; and he delivered me from all my tribulations.

Approach him and be enlightened, and your faces will not be confounded. This poor man cried out, and the Lord heard him; and he saved him from all his tribulations. The angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear him, and he will deliver them. Taste and see that the Lord is sweet; blessed is the man who hopes in him.

Fear the Lord, all his saints, for there is no want for those who fear him. The rich have become needy and hungry, but those who seek the Lord will not be deprived of any good. Come, children, hear me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord. Who is the person who desires life and loves to see good days? Restrain your tongue from evil, and do not let your lips speak deceit. Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.

The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears are toward their prayers. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to destroy their memory from the earth. The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them; and he delivered them from all their tribulations. The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and he will save the humble in spirit.

Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and the Lord delivered them from all of them. The Lord guards all their bones; not one of them will be broken. The death of sinners is most grievous, and those who dare to assail the righteous will offend. The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants, and all who hope in him will not offend.

As above. You have protected me from the assembly of the wicked.

## Prayer

God, dispenser of angels and of all creation, send your angel around us. Fortified by his protection, may we deserve to be delivered from the most grievous death of sins. Through the Lord.

## Another Prayer

Mercifully hear those who seek you, Lord, and graciously grant that we may be blessed both in adversity and in prosperity. And, so that our soul may praise you, mercifully bestow your favor. And because you are near to those who are troubled in heart, open your ear to the spirit of our contrition; and grant your peace, which surpasses all understanding [Add.: “grant,” or something similar], to purify our bodies and hearts. Through.

## Psalm

### (Psalm 144)

I will exalt you, my God and king, and I will bless your name forever and for ages of ages. Every day I will bless you, and I will praise your name forever and for ages of ages. Great is the Lord and exceedingly worthy of praise, and there is no end to his greatness. Generation after generation will praise your works and proclaim your power.

They will speak of the magnificence of the glory of your holiness and recount your wonders. They will speak of the power of your terrible deeds and declare your greatness. They will pour forth the memory of the abundance of your sweetness and exult in your righteousness. The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and greatly merciful. The Lord is sweet to all, and his mercies are over all his works.

Let all your works confess to you, Lord, and let your saints bless you. They will speak of the glory of your kingdom and proclaim your power, making your power known to the children of humanity and the glory of the magnificence of your kingdom. Your kingdom is a kingdom of all ages, and your dominion is through every generation and generation.

The Lord is faithful in all his words and holy in all his works. The Lord raises up all who fall and lifts up all who are crushed. The eyes of all hope in you, Lord, and you give them food at the proper time. You open your hand and fill every living creature with blessing.

The Lord is righteous in all his ways and holy in all his works. The Lord is near to all who call upon him, to all who call upon him in truth. He will do the will of those who fear him, and he will hear their supplication; he will save them. The Lord guards all who love him, and he will destroy all sinners. My mouth will speak the praise of the Lord, and let all flesh bless his holy name forever and for ages of ages.

As above. He sent from on high and received me; he took me up from many waters. He delivered me from my strongest enemies and from those who hated me, because they had grown stronger than I. They confronted me on the day of my affliction, and the Lord became my protector.

## Prayer

Lord, ruler of all ages, who provide spiritual food to every soul at the appropriate time, grant us to bless you perpetually and to exalt your power confidently with your elect. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## Reading

You have delivered us, Lord, from those afflicting us, and you have put to shame those who hated us. Praise to you, Lord, King of eternal glory.

## Thanksgiving

I offer you praise and thanks, my God, my mercy, who have deigned to lead me to knowledge of you and, through the washing of holy baptism, to gather me among the children of your adoption. I offer you praise and thanks, who, from the very beginnings of infancy until this hour, while I have flowed into many vices, patiently await my amendment through your immense goodness.

I praise and glorify you, who have so often delivered me from many tribulations and afflictions, calamities and miseries, and who have thus far rescued me from eternal punishments and from the torments of this body. I praise and glorify you, who have deigned to confer upon me soundness of limbs, tranquility of times, honor, affection, and love—and whatever gifts of your mercy may also be in me.

I ask, Lord God, for the immeasurable gentleness of your sweetness, so that you may perfect the good things begun in me. Whatever in me displeases you, drive away; rescue me from all the tribulations, iniquities, and various evils that remain. Direct my thoughts, words, and actions alike according to your will; and do not take my soul from this world before it strives to be amended in your will.

Guard me always and everywhere as I walk amid adversity and prosperity, and at last lead me to the repeated joys of the vision of you. Amen.

## Prayer of Isidore for All Christians

Most merciful Lord, readily hearing God, Jesus Christ our God, with every supplication we earnestly ask your clemency: through the intercession and merit of the blessed and glorious ever-virgin Mary and of all the holy angels, archangels, patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs, virgins, confessors, monks, and all the citizens of heaven, increase the faith of your holy catholic Church; grant peace to our rulers and grant us indulgence and remission of sins; grant health to the sick, restoration to the fallen, favorable weather, and to faithful sailors and travelers a prosperous journey and a safe harbor; joy to those in tribulation [L., “to the afflicted”], relief to the oppressed; to captives, prisoners, and exiles forgiveness, absolution, and return to their homeland; mutual charity to those in discord; true faith to unbelievers; and rest to the faithful departed.

Mercifully deign to grant us your holy angel here and everywhere as guardian and defender. You live and reign as God with the Father and the Holy Spirit through all ages of ages. Amen.

## Hymn of Saint Ambrose for the Sick

### [Col. 0556C]

[Note: [Col. 0555D] Marten, cited passage, p. 624.]

Christ, heavenly medicine of the Father,

true physician of human salvation:

for the provident people, powerfully

open favor through prayers.

Behold, for the sick we beseech your [Marten: “you”],

those whom harmful disease afflicts:

as the merciful one, relieve the illness

of those lying in suffering.

You who, manifest in power,

immediately save Peter’s mother-in-law

lying in fever, the child of the ruler,

and the servant-boy of the centurion.

Bring strength [Marten: “festival”] to the languishing people;

pour out abundant salvation upon the people,

restoring the sick, as is your custom,

to their former strength.

Heal the diseases of bodies and the mind [Marten: “of souls”].

Apply a remedy to the causes of wounds,

lest suffering burn our bodies

without fruit.

Let every deadly assault withdraw;

let every torturing attack melt away;

let the strength of desired salvation

cherish the suffering limbs.

Now, our God, have mercy on our tears,

and so heal those for whom

we now seek you, that every sick person lying down

may feel your healing.

So that, while the evils inflicted are worn away,

they may enter the kingdoms of heaven,

honored among the number of the learned,

having obtained their share with their companions.

Glory to the Father and to the begotten Son,

and to you, gracious Spirit, ever equal to them both,

one God

through every age of the world.

Let the choir sing glory and resound;

let it speak glory, sing it, and pour it forth [Marten: “fly back”],

life-giving Spirit, one God

through every age of the world.

## Prayer for Relatives

Deliver us, we beseech you, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, from all vices and from the snares of the enemy. Protect us from every tribulation and evil power, so that your name and your majesty may be magnified, lest the nations say, “Where is their God?” But our God is in heaven; he has done everything that he willed.

Guard us, Lord, as the apple of the eye; protect us under the shadow of your wings, lest any evil human power be able to harm us in soul, body, mind, while walking, sleeping, standing, sitting, seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, tasting, drinking, using, walking, reading, praying, perceiving, speaking, thinking, separating, gathering, traveling, or sailing.

Deliver us, merciful Trinity, from every past, present, and future evil, just as from the beginning of the world you delivered your servants: Noah from the flood; Abraham from Ur of the Chaldeans; Lot from the city of the Sodomites; Moses and the people of Israel from the Red Sea and from the hands of Pharaoh; David from the hand of Saul and from Goliath; Elijah and Enoch from this world; Tobit from the pain of his eyes; the three young men from the furnace of blazing fire; Susanna from the hand of the rulers; Daniel from the lions’ den; Jonah from the belly of the whale; Hezekiah from illness; Naaman the Syrian from disease; and Joshua son of Nun from the battles of the Canaanites; Nineveh from impending death; Isaac from the sword of his father; Job from his tribulations; Gideon from the barbarians; Peter from the waves of the sea and from prison; Paul from many tribulations and dangers.

So may you, holy Trinity, eternal God, deign to deliver us, your servants, from all the snares of the devil in this world and preserve us unharmed in your holy service, so that in the future we may deserve to obtain eternal rewards with you, who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

## Psalm

### (Psalm 19)

May the Lord hear you on the day of tribulation; may the name of the God of Jacob protect you. May he send you help from the sanctuary, and may he guard you from Zion. May he remember all your sacrifice, and may your burnt offering become rich. May he grant you according to your heart and confirm all your plans.

We will rejoice in your salvation, and in the name of our God we will be magnified. May the Lord fulfill all your petitions. Now I know that the Lord has saved his anointed; he will hear him from his holy heaven, with the saving power of his right hand.

Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will call upon the name of the Lord our God. They are bound and have fallen, but we have risen and stand upright. Lord, save the king, and hear us on the day we call upon you.

As above. Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us.

## Prayer

Fulfill our petitions, Lord, and receive us as a most richly fattened burnt offering, so that, with the chariots of our enemies bound, we may rejoice in the help of your salvation. Through.

## Another Prayer

Fulfill our petitions, Lord, and send us help from the sanctuary. Remember our sacrifice, which is offered to you not only through offering and prayer; and graciously deign to hear our petitions, which on whatever day we offer to you with the hand of the tongue and the knee of the heart. Through.

## Psalm

### (Psalm 40)

Blessed is the one who understands concerning the needy and poor; on the evil day the Lord will deliver him. May the Lord preserve him, give him life, and make him blessed on the earth; and may he not hand him over to the desire of his enemies.

May the Lord bring him help upon the bed of his pain; you have turned his entire bed in his illness. I said, “Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, because I have sinned against you.” My enemies spoke evil against me: “When will he die and his name perish?” And if he entered in order to see, he spoke vainly; his heart gathered iniquity for itself. He went out and spoke together with others.

All my enemies whispered against me; they devised evil against me. They established an evil word against me: “Will the one who sleeps not rise again?” Indeed, the man of my peace, in whom I hoped, who ate my bread, magnified treachery against me.

But you, Lord, have mercy on me and raise me up, and I will repay them. By this I know that you have desired me, because my enemy will not rejoice over me. But you received me because of my innocence and established me in your presence forever.

Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from age to age and forever. So be it, so be it.

As above. He scattered and gave to the poor.

## Prayer

Eternal God, gentle forgiver of our sins, who grant escape from the evil day when mercy follows the needy: we beseech you, bring aid to our pains, so that, while you mercifully rebuke carnal offenses, you may graciously bestow the medicine of the soul. Through the Lord.

## Another

Establish us in your presence, Lord, forever, so that our fixed path may not be troubled by any alien gaze. Through.

## Psalm

### (Psalm 66)

May God have mercy on us and bless us; may he make his face shine upon us and have mercy on us, so that we may know your way on earth, your salvation among all nations. Let the peoples confess to you, God; let all the peoples confess to you. Let the nations rejoice and exult, for you judge the peoples with equity and direct the nations on earth.

Let the peoples confess to you, God; let all the peoples confess to you. The earth has given its fruit. May God, our God, bless us; may God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth fear him.

As above. Our help is in the name of the Lord.

## Prayer

Shine your face upon us, Lord, and grant us abundant mercy and blessing. Through.

## Another Prayer

Knowing your way on earth, Lord, your salvation among all nations, we confess that Christ the Lord is both the way and the homeland. Through him we walk on the straight path and reach the fullest perfection. Through.

## Psalm
(PSALM 131.) Remember, O Lord, David and all his meekness. As he swore to the Lord, he vowed a vow to the God of Jacob: “If I enter the tent of my house, if I climb upon the bed of my couch; if I give sleep to my eyes and slumber to my eyelids, and rest to my temples, until I find a place for the Lord, a dwelling for the God of Jacob.” Behold, we heard of it in Ephrata; we found it in the fields of the forest. We shall enter his dwelling; we shall adore in the place where his feet have stood. Arise, O Lord, into your rest, you and the ark of your sanctification. Let your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let your holy ones exult. For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed. The Lord swore truth to David, and he will not frustrate it: “From the fruit of your womb I will set upon your throne. If your sons keep my covenant and these testimonies of mine that I shall teach them, their sons also shall sit upon your throne forever.” For the Lord chose Zion; he chose it as a dwelling for himself. “This is my rest forever and ever; here I shall dwell, for I have chosen it.” 89 “Blessing I will bless her widow; I will satisfy her poor with bread. I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her holy ones shall exult with exultation. There I shall bring forth the horn of David; I have prepared a lamp for my anointed. I will clothe his enemies with shame, but upon him my sanctification shall flourish.”

As above. Save us, O Lord our God.

Prayer. In all our coming in, remember us, almighty and eternal God; clothe us with priestly righteousness, so that we may be deemed worthy to be brought into everlasting dwellings. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another. Arise, O Lord, and let our hearts be prepared for you in your rest; and let there be in each one the sanctification of your ark and meditation upon holiness, and let Christ our Lord be the lamp of our works, so that, with him preparing these things, we may be filled with the fruit of righteousness for grace and be held fast by the word of life for glory. Through [Christ our Lord].

PSALM.

(PSALM 132.) Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together as one. It is like ointment upon the head, which descends upon the beard, the beard of Aaron; which descends upon the edge of his garment. It is like the dew of Hermon, which descends upon Mount Zion. For there the Lord commanded blessing, and life forever.

As above. The dead shall not praise you, O Lord.

Prayer. Pour into your Church, O Lord, the love of brotherhood and peace, so that, sprinkled with the dew of spiritual ointment, we may rejoice in the grace of your blessing. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another. Christ the Lord, whose holy name compared the fragrance of wisdom to poured-out ointment: grant, we ask, that the ointment of your crown may descend, as you pour it forth, upon the beard of your beautiful people, and reach the very edge of the garment with which the present life is clothed. Through the Lord.

PSALM.

(PSALM 133.) Behold now, bless the Lord, all servants of the Lord, who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands toward the sanctuary and bless the Lord. May the Lord bless you from Zion, he who made heaven and earth.

As above. For the sake of my brothers and my neighbors.

Prayer. As all your servants bless you, O Lord, we beseech you to illumine us, covered by the night of this world, so that, while we raise our hands in good works, we may obtain from you the most abundant blessing. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another Prayer. Grant, O Lord, that, having ascended all the steps of perfection and reached the summit of the virtues, we may praise you; and that, standing in your house and in your courts, we may stretch out our hands to bless you by day and by night, having received a blessing from you, the Lord and Savior of heaven and earth.

SUPPLICATION, which Pope Gelasius established should be sung for the universal Church.

Let us all say: “O Lord, hear and have mercy.”

We invoke in faithful hearts the Father of the Only-Begotten, the Son of the unbegotten Begetter, and the holy God, the Spirit.

For the spotless Church of the living God, and for its priests and ministers, we beseech the abundant riches of divine goodness.

For the holy priests and ministers of the great God, and for all peoples who worship the true God, we entreat Christ the Lord.

For all who rightly handle the word of truth, we especially beseech the manifold wisdom of the Word of God.

For those who sanctify themselves in mind and body for the sake of the kingdom of heaven, and who labor strenuously in spiritual things, we beseech the giver of spiritual gifts.

For religious rulers and all their army, who love judgment and justice, we beseech the power of the Lord.

For pleasantness and calm in the rain, for the refreshing breezes that give life, and for the prosperous course of various undertakings, we beseech the Lord, ruler of the world.

For those whom the first recognition of the Christian name initiated, and whom desire for heavenly grace now inflames, we beseech the mercy of almighty God.

For those whom the frailty of human weakness, the envy of spiritual wickedness, or the various terror of the world has enveloped, we implore the mercy of our Redeemer.

For those whom the necessity of exile, the impiety of an unjust power, or hostile distress afflicts, we beseech the Lord Savior.

For those deceived by Jewish falsehood, heretical perversity, or steeped in the superstition of the pagans, we beseech the Lord of truth.

For those who perform works of piety, and for those who, in fraternal charity, assist people in need, we beseech the Lord’s mercy.

For all who enter the courts of this holy house of God with religious hearts and fitting humble devotion, we beseech the Lord of glory.

For the cleansing of all our souls and bodies, and for the forgiveness of sins, we beseech the most merciful Lord.

For the refreshment of the souls of the faithful, especially of the holy priests of the Lord who presided over this Catholic Church, we beseech the Lord of spirits and judge of all flesh.

Grant, O Lord, a flesh mortified by vices and a soul alive through faith. Grant, O Lord, grant.

Grant chaste fear and true love. Grant, O Lord, grant.

Grant a commendable ordering of life and an approved end. Grant, O Lord, grant.

Grant the angel of peace and the consolations of the holy ones. Grant, O Lord, grant.

We entrust ourselves and all that is ours—which, having arisen and been accomplished, we have received through the Lord as its author, retain through him as its guardian, and commend to his mercy and the decision of his providence. Lord, have mercy.

DAILY [PRAYER] FOR FAMILIARS.

Let us all say: “O Lord, hear and have mercy.” Lord, have mercy.

Most merciful Father, may you deem worthy to hear with the ears of your compassion this prayer of ours, which, urged on by the affection of fraternal charity, we pour forth in a suppliant voice to you for our brothers and sisters, who, striving daily to intercede for us with tireless prayer, have commended themselves to our prayers, and likewise for all who, by your gracious mercy, do good to us for the sake of your name. And for those who, pierced by a spiritual goad, have confessed their sins to us.

Therefore, almighty God, preserve all these, whose names are written here, unharmed in your holy service from every snare of the devil in this world, so that in the future they may be deemed worthy to obtain eternal rewards with you.

Save your servants. Send them help, O Lord, from the holy place. May the enemy accomplish nothing against them. Through the merits and prayers of all the saints, O Lord, free them, guard them, strengthen them, give them peace, purify them, forgive them their offenses, and preserve them in your name, as you will and as you know, O Lord. Blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and strength be to our God forever and ever. Amen.

FRIDAY. IN MEMORY OF THE INCARNATION, PASSION, AND RESURRECTION, OR ASCENSION, OF THE LORD.

HYMN OF FORTUNATUS [Note: [Col. 0561D] Rather, of Mamertus Claudianus. See Sirmond in the note to Sidonius’s letter 3, p. 933.] ON THE NATIVITY AND CROSS OF CHRIST.

[Note: [Col. 0562D] For the ninth use, above, col. 497.]

Tell, O tongue, of the glorious

Battle of the conflict,

And upon the trophy of the cross

Grant noble triumph;

How the Redeemer of the world,

Sacrificed, conquered.

The Maker, grieving over

The fraud of the first parent,

When, by the bite of the deadly fruit,

He fell into death,

Then himself designated the wood,

So that he might undo the damage of the wood.

This work of our salvation

The order of things had demanded,

That by the art of the many-formed destroyer

He might deceive the deceiver’s art,

And bring healing from the place

From which the enemy had wounded.

91 Therefore, when the fullness

Of sacred time had come,

The Founder of the world was sent

From the Father’s citadel and was born;

And, having become flesh

From a virgin’s womb, he came forth.

The infant wails, enclosed

Within a narrow manger;

The virgin mother binds

His limbs in swaddling clothes,

And with a tight bandage

She binds [Alternative: girds] his feet, hands, and legs.

When six periods of years had already passed,

Fulfilling the time of his body,

Of his own will, born for this,

He surrendered himself to suffering;

The Lamb is raised upon the wood

Of the cross, to be sacrificed.

Here vinegar, gall, reed,

Spittle, nails, and lance:

His gentle body is pierced,

And blood flows forth like water;

Earth, sea, stars, the world—

By this stream they are washed.

Faithful cross, among all trees

The one noble tree,

No forest produces one such as this

In leaf, flower, or shoot;

Sweet wood, bearing

A sweet nail [Alternative: sweet nails],

Bearing a sweet burden.

Bend your branches, lofty tree;

Relax your stretched fibers,

And let that rigidity grow slack

Which birth imparted,

So that you may extend upon the wood

The limbs of the heavenly King.

You alone were worthy

To bear the price of the world,

And to prepare a harbor,

As a sailor, for the shipwrecked world.

The sacred blood anointed you,

Poured from the Lamb upon the wood

[Alternative: from the Lamb’s body].

OF THE SAME AUTHOR.

[Col. 0563C]

The blessed cross shines, upon which the Lord hung in the flesh

And washed our wounds with his own blood.

Made a victim for us through gentle, devout love,

The sacred Lamb drew the sheep from the wolf’s mouth.

When, with palms transfixed, he redeemed the world from ruin

And closed the way of death with his own burial.

That was the hand pierced by bloody nails

Which rescued Paul from guilt and Peter from death.

Powerful in fruitfulness, O sweet and noble wood!

When do you bear such new fruits upon your branches?

By whose new fragrance dead corpses rise,

And those who lacked the day of life return to life.

No heat will burn beneath the leaves of this tree,

Nor the moon by night, nor the sun at midday.

[Col. 0563D] You shine, planted beside the course of waters,

And scatter fresh-blossomed adornments over your hair.

A vine is hung between your arms,

From which sweet wines flow with a blood-red hue.

PSALM OF THE INCARNATION.

(PSALM 2.) Why did the nations rage, and the peoples meditate on vain things? The kings of the earth stood forth, and the rulers gathered together as one against the Lord and against his anointed. “Let us break their bonds and cast their yoke away from us.” He who dwells in the heavens will laugh at them, and the Lord will mock them. Then he will speak to them in his anger, and in his wrath he will trouble them. “But I have been appointed king by him over Zion, his holy mountain, proclaiming his command.” The Lord said to me: “You are my Son; today I have begotten you. Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance and the ends of the earth as your possession. You shall rule them with an iron rod, and like a potter’s vessel you shall shatter them.” And now, kings, understand; be instructed, you who judge the earth. Serve the Lord in fear, and exult before him with trembling. Seize instruction, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the righteous way. When his anger has suddenly blazed forth, blessed are all who trust in him.

92 As above. A light has dawned in the darkness. We have received your mercy, O God.

Prayer. Make us, O Lord, like a most fruitful tree before your presence, so that, refreshed by your rains, we may be deemed worthy to please you with an abundance of sweet fruits. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another. Serving you, O Lord, in fear because of dread of judgment, and exulting with trembling because of confidence in hope, teach us to seize instruction, you who judge the earth, so that, with you showing favor, we may shatter the potter of the old man and trample the refuse of the earthly exterior.

PSALM OF THE LORD’S PASSION.

(PSALM 34.) Judge, O Lord, those who harm me; defeat those who attack me. Take up weapons and shield, and rise to my help. Draw out the sword and close the way against those who persecute me. Say to my soul: “I am your salvation.” Let those who seek my soul be confounded and put to shame. Let those who think evil against me be turned backward and confounded. Let them become like dust before the face of the wind, and let the angel of the Lord hem them in. Let their way be darkness and slippery ground, and let the angel of the Lord pursue them. For without cause they secretly hid the destruction of their trap for me; in vain they reproached my soul. Let the trap he does not know come upon him, and let the snare he concealed seize him; let him fall into that very trap. But my soul shall exult in the Lord and rejoice in his salvation. All my bones shall say: “O Lord, who is like you? You will rescue the needy from the hand of those stronger than he, the poor and indigent from those who plunder him.” Unjust witnesses rose up and questioned me about things I did not know. They repaid me evil for good, barrenness for my soul. But when they troubled me, I clothed myself in sackcloth. I humbled my soul with fasting, and my prayer shall return into my bosom. As for a neighbor and as for our brother, so I was pleasing; as one mourning and grieving, so I humbled myself. Yet they rejoiced against me and gathered together; scourges were assembled against me, and I did not know it. They were scattered and were not pierced with remorse; they tested me, mocked me with mockery, and gnashed their teeth against me. O Lord, when will you look upon this? Restore my soul from their malice, my only one from the lions. I will confess to you in the great Church; in a weighty people I will praise you. Let those who unjustly oppose me not rejoice over me, those who hate me without cause and wink with their eyes. For they spoke peaceably to me, but while speaking in the anger of the earth they devised deceit. And they opened their mouths wide against me; they said: “Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen it.” You have seen, O Lord; do not be silent. O Lord, do not depart from me. Arise and attend to my judgment, my God and my Lord, to my cause. Judge me according to your justice, O Lord my God, and let them not rejoice over me. Let them not say in their hearts: “Aha, aha, our desire!” Nor let them say: “We shall devour him.” Let those who rejoice at my misfortunes be ashamed and confounded together. Let those who speak evil against me be clothed with shame and reverence. Let those who desire my righteousness exult and rejoice, and let them always say: “May the Lord be magnified,” those who desire the peace of his servant. And my tongue shall meditate upon your righteousness, and all day long upon your praise.

As above. Be my helper and deliverer, O Lord; do not delay.

Prayer. Protection and salvation of our soul, cover us with the helmet of hope and the shield of unconquerable defense, so that, helped by you in the circumstances of our need, we may be deemed worthy to be flooded with joy and exultation together with those who love you. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another Prayer. O Lord, when will you look upon us and say: “I am your salvation”? And when will you mercifully turn toward our solitude and supplication? Turn toward it now, O Lord, and attend to our judgment; and, as a strong champion, yourself defeat those who judge us, so that our prayer—which now returns into our bosom because of remorse for its secret matters—may, purified before your presence, be directed with the groaning of the heart.

93 PSALM OF THE RESURRECTION.

(PSALM 3.) O Lord, why have those who afflict me become so numerous? Many rise up against me [Alternative: many arise against me]. Many say to my soul: “There is no salvation for him in his God.” But you, O Lord, are my protector, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head. With my voice I cried to the Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain. I slept and was overcome with sleep, and I arose, because the Lord received me. I will not fear thousands of people surrounding me. Arise, O Lord; save me, my God. For you struck all those who oppose me without cause; you crushed the teeth of sinners. Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people.

As above. You have held my right hand.

Prayer. Pour your blessing upon your people, O Lord, so that, strengthened by your resurrection, we may not fear being surrounded by the malice of opposing vices. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another. O Lord, come swiftly as a strong champion against the multiplication of our tribulations, and stand as a merciful defender against the multitude rising up against us. Let your blessing be upon your people, so that those who deny that the salvation of our soul is in you may recognize you as our Savior through their very defeat.

PSALM ALSO ON THE SAME SUBJECT.

[Col. 0566A]

(PSALM 29.) I will exalt you, O Lord, for you have received me, and have not allowed my enemies to rejoice over me. O Lord my God, I cried to you, and you healed me. O Lord, you brought my soul up from the underworld; you saved me from those descending into the pit. Sing psalms to the Lord, you his holy ones, and confess the memory of his holiness. For there is anger in his indignation, and life in his will. In the evening weeping will linger, and in the morning joy. But I said in my abundance: “I shall not be shaken forever.” O Lord, by your will you gave strength to my beauty. You turned your face away from me, and I became troubled. To you, O Lord, I shall cry, and to my God I shall plead. What profit is there in my blood, when I descend into corruption? Will dust confess to you, or declare your truth? The Lord heard and had mercy on me; the Lord became my helper. You turned my mourning into joy for me; you tore off my sackcloth and girded me with gladness, so that my glory might sing to you and I might not be pierced with remorse. O Lord my God, forever I shall confess to you.

As above. I slept.

Prayer. Most merciful God, protector of all, do not permit our enemies to rejoice over us; but strengthen us with your power in such a way that we may continually cultivate our mourning, turned into the joy of your holiness, in remembrance of it. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another. Hear, O Lord, and have mercy on us; and, as we confess the memory of your holiness, gird us with the joy of confession. Since our life is in your will, grant us the gift of that will, so that, while life is bestowed upon us according to your will, your will may be fulfilled through the gift of that very life. Through [Christ our Lord].

PSALM OF THE ASCENSION.

(PSALM 8.) O Lord, our Lord, how wondrous is your name in all the earth! For your magnificence has been exalted above the heavens. From the mouth of infants and sucklings you perfected praise because of your enemies, to destroy the enemy and the avenger. For I shall see your heavens, the works of your fingers; the moon and the stars, which you established. What is man, that you are mindful of him, or the son of man, that you visit him? You made him a little lower than the angels; you crowned him with glory and honor, and set him over the works of your hands. You subjected all things beneath his feet: all sheep and oxen, and also the beasts of the field; the birds of heaven and the fish of the sea, which pass along the paths of the sea. O Lord, our Lord, how wondrous is your name in all the earth!

As above. God has ascended with rejoicing. God shall reign over the nations.

94 Prayer. What is man, O Lord, that you are mindful of him? Or why are you the son of man, unless it is so that you might redeem him, lest he perish forever? Therefore give us the necessary help, you who gave precious blood for us; and grant that those whom your death redeems may glorify you by their life.

[Col. 0567A] According to your name, O God. He heard my voice from his holy temple. Sing psalms to our God, for God is king of all the earth.

Prayer. Your name is wondrous, almighty Lord. We humbly beseech you: since you have subjected every creature of the world to human use, deem us worthy to be made fit for the service of your worship. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer also. Hear, O Lord, holy Father, almighty, eternal God, our prayers, which we pour forth to your goodness in memory of the sacred incarnation, birth, passion, resurrection, and ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ. For he deigned to become incarnate, be born, die, rise again, and ascend into heaven for us, leading our captivity captive by his power. May we, by his governance, protection, and mercy, be defended from all the snares of diabolical deceit. He lives with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit forever and ever.

FRIDAY ALSO: PRAYER OF SAINT CYPRIAN THE MARTYR.

O Lord, holy Father, holy, I have lifted up my soul to you. My God, who indeed is greater than you? To you I return thanks and praise. God of Abraham, God of Isaac, God of Jacob, God of our fathers, God of the apostles, God of the prophets, God of the martyrs; you who are and who were before the foundation of the world. God of the living, who will come to judge the living and the dead; you are the true God, who sits above the cherubim and looks upon the abysses; you see all things before they are born; you have power to kill and to restore again; you have power to make the withered green. You are the God and ruler of all; free me from this world.

Hear me praying, as you heard the children of Israel from the land of Egypt, who neither believed you nor your servant Moses. Woe to my sins! When you rise to shatter the earth, beneath what fissure of the rocks shall I hide myself before your power? To what mountain shall I say, “Fall upon me,” and to what hill, “Cover me,” before the fear of the Lord, when you rise to shatter the earth? I ask you, O Lord, help me, and do not judge me according to my deeds, for I have prepared nothing in accordance with your commandments. Hear me as I plead.

As you heard Jonah from the belly of the whale, so hear me and cast me from death into life. As the Ninevites put on ashes and sackcloth and performed penance, so also may I, making confession before your presence for all my sins—you who love repentance—receive your mercy. David also says: “O Lord, for the sake of your name, blot out my sin”; and I, entreating your majesty, say: blot out all my sins.

Hear me praying, as you heard the three youths from the furnace of fire, Ananias, Azariah, and Misael, and sent your angel with a cloud of dew. Nebuchadnezzar, the ruler of the kingdom, was confounded, for you are King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule, you alone possessing immortality and dwelling in inaccessible light, whom no human being sees or can see.

Hear me praying, as you heard Daniel from the lions’ den and sent the prophet Habakkuk, who brought him food and said: “Eat the meal that the Lord has sent you.” And Daniel said: “The Lord does not forsake those who seek him.”

Hear me praying, as you heard Tobiah and Sarah while they were praying in the court of their house. Then the angel Raphael offered their prayer for them. So hear my prayers and admit my petitions to your holy court; and continually send your angel to blot out all my sins, as you blotted out the unclean spirit from Sarah, daughter of Raguel. Enlighten my heart, as you enlightened Tobiah’s eyes.

Hear me praying, as you heard Susanna and rescued her from the hands of the elders; so also rescue me from this world, because you love a pure conscience.

Hear me praying, as you heard Hezekiah, king of Judah, and removed his bodily illness; so also take away from me the infirmity of body and soul, and increase my faith, as you added fifteen years to his life. Free me from the midst of this world, as you freed Thecla from the midst of the amphitheater; so free me from every infirmity of the flesh.

I entreat you, Father, who at the end of time remembered us, sending us Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord and Savior, born of the Virgin Mary from the Holy Spirit, announced by the angel Gabriel, through whom you freed us from the danger of impending death.

And I entreat you, Son of the living God, who performed great deeds at Cana of Galilee, making wine from water for Israel; who opened the eyes of the blind, made the deaf hear, restored paralytics to their limbs, healed the tongues of those who stammered when tormented by a demon, made the lame run like deer, freed the woman from the flow of blood, raised the dead, and walked upon the water with your feet; who founded the sea and set its boundaries by your power.

I entreat you, Son of the living God, for all my sins. You are in heaven, the Son in the Father and the Father eternally in you; you sit above the cherubim and seraphim, the seat of your honor. An innumerable host of angels stands before you, fearing and trembling at your honor and power, crying out with a loud voice and saying: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth.”

You yourself made a covenant with us, and shortly afterward said: “Ask and you shall receive; seek and you shall find; knock and it shall be opened to you. Whatever you ask of my Father in my name, you shall receive.” I ask the Father, so that I may receive; I seek, so that I may find; I knock, so that it may be opened to me. In your name I ask that you ask the Father, and that forgiveness may be given to me.

I am ready, for the sake of your name, to pour out the sacrifice of blood and to endure whatever torment. You are my helper and my defender; defend my soul from the adversary. May your angel of light protect me, because you said: “Whatever believers ask for through prayer shall be given to them.”

Every human being is a liar; you alone are truthful. As you promised, you have the power to give. O Lord, reveal to me your heavenly mystery, so that I may be worthy to see the face of your holy ones. May the Holy Spirit work in me your will, which I have vowed to you all the days of my life.

You who made the good confession under Pontius Pilate; you were crucified, descended, and trampled upon the sting of death. You said: “Where are you, death, which reigned? Where are you, sting of death?” Death has been conquered; the enemy devil has been defeated. You rose from the dead and appeared to your apostles. You ascended into heaven and sit at the right hand of the Father, coming to judge the living and the dead.

You who rule over us, free me from the hand of him who seeks my soul. By your holy name I entreat you: free me from the adversary’s side, so that you may grant me help in conquering my enemy. For you are a powerful defender and advocate of prayers, and, at our petition, interceding day and night, O Lord, for my sins, may you carry my prayer to your Father.

Deign to look upon my prayers, as you looked upon the offerings of your righteous servant Abel. Deign to free me from the everlasting fire of punishments and from every torment that you have prepared for the wicked, through Jesus Christ our good and blessed Savior, through whom honor, power, and glory are yours forever and ever. Amen.

ANOTHER PRAYER.

Grant me, O Lord, purity of lips, purity and innocence of heart, and uprightness of action. Grant me humility, patience, abstinence, chastity, sobriety, prudence, justice, fortitude, or temperance. Grant me the spirit of wisdom and understanding, counsel and fortitude, knowledge and piety, and of your fear. Give me the lower watering-place and the upper watering-place. Grant me the twofold effect of charity, right faith, and unshaken hope. Give me blessing from the dew of heaven and the fatness of the earth. Make me seek your face with all my heart and all my soul. Grant me, in your presence, a contrite and humbled heart; that I may place nothing before your love, and that at some time I may be utterly extinguished to the world by love of you. Make me become a living sacrifice in your sacrifice, offering the rich marrow of holocausts to your mercy.

Highest, eternal, and ineffable Wisdom, drive away from me the darkness of blindness and ignorance. Highest eternal Power, free me. Highest eternal Strength, help me. Highest and incomprehensible Light, illumine me. Highest and boundless Mercy, have mercy on me. Amen.

96 COLLECTION OF BEDE’S PSALTER [Note: [Col. 0569] Alcuin mentions this psalter in Letter 153, to Arno.]

PSALM 1. Blessed is the man who has not gone in the counsel of the wicked, has not stood in the way of sinners, and has not sat in the seat of scoffers. But his will is in the law of the Lord, and in his law he will meditate day and night. He shall be like a tree transplanted beside channels of water, which will give its fruit in its season. Its leaf shall not fall, and everything he does shall prosper.

2. Now therefore, kings, understand; be instructed, judges of the earth. Serve the Lord in fear, and exult before him in trembling. Adore purely, lest he perhaps become angry and you perish from the way.

3. But you, O Lord, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head. Arise, O Lord; save me, my God.

4. Have mercy on me and hear my prayer.

5. Hear my words, O Lord; understand my murmuring. My king and my God, for to you I pray. O Lord, lead me in your justice because of those lying in wait for me; direct your way before my face.

6. O Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor correct me in your wrath. Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak; heal me, O Lord, for my bones are troubled. And my soul is greatly troubled; but you, O Lord—how long? Return, O Lord, and rescue my soul; save me for the sake of your mercy.

7. O Lord my God, in you I have hoped; save me from all who pursue me and deliver me, lest he seize and tear my soul like a lion, with no one to rescue me.

8. O Lord, our ruler, great is your name in all the earth.

9. I shall rejoice and exult in you; I shall sing to your name, O Most High. Arise, O Lord God; lift up your hand; do not forget the poor.

10. The Lord tests the righteous.

11. Save us, O Lord.

[Col. 0570C] 12. How long will my enemy be exalted over me? Turn and hear me, O Lord my God, lest my enemy ever say: “I have prevailed against him.”

13. Jacob shall exult, and Israel shall rejoice.

14. But he glorifies those who fear the Lord.

15. Guard me, O God, for I have hoped in you, saying to God: “You are my Lord; I have no good apart from you.”

16. Attend to my supplication; sustain my steps in your paths, and let my footsteps not slip. Incline your ear to me; hear my speech. Make your mercy wondrous, Savior of those who hope in you. Guard me like the pupil within the eye; protect me in the shadow of your wings. But I shall see your face in righteousness.

17. I shall love you, O Lord, my strength.

18. Cleanse me from my hidden faults, and also free your servant from the proud. Let the words of my mouth be pleasing, O Lord, my strength and my redeemer.

19. But we shall remember the name of the Lord.

20. Be exalted, O Lord, in your strength; we shall sing and chant your mighty deeds.

21. But you, O Lord, do not be far from me, my strength; hasten to my help. Rescue my soul from the sword; save me from the lion’s mouth.

[Col. 0571A] 22. And your kindness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life.

23. And I shall receive blessing from the Lord.

24. To you, O Lord, I lift up my soul. Show me your ways, O Lord, and teach me your paths. Lead me in your truth; teach me, for you are God my Savior. Do not remember the sins of my youth and my transgressions. According to your mercy, remember me. For the sake of your name, be gracious to my iniquity, for it is great. Look upon me and have mercy on me; lead me out of my troubles. See my affliction and bear all my sins. Guard my soul and deliver me.

97 25. O Lord, I have loved the dwelling of your house. Do not take away my soul with sinners; redeem me and have mercy on me.

26. The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? Hear, O Lord, the voice of me who calls; have mercy on me and hear me. Do not hide your face from me; do not turn away in anger from your servant. You have been my help; do not forsake me and do not abandon me, O God my Savior. Show me your way, O Lord, and lead me on the straight path because of those lying in wait for me. Do not hand me over, O Lord, to the souls of those who trouble me. But I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.

27. Hear, O Lord, my supplication when I cry to you. Do not hand me over with the wicked and with those who work iniquity.

[Col. 0571C] 28. The Lord is my strength and my shield. Adore the Lord in holy beauty.

29. Hear, O Lord, and have mercy on me. O Lord, be my helper, so that glory may praise you and not be silent. O Lord my God, forever I shall confess to you.

30. In you, O Lord, I have hoped; I shall not be confounded forever. In your justice save me. Incline your ear to me; swiftly deliver me, for you are my rock and my fortress. Into your hand I commend my spirit. In your hand are my times. Deliver me from the hand of my enemies and those who pursue me. Show your face upon your servant; save me in your mercy.

31. Blessed is he whose iniquity is forgiven and whose sin is covered. I make my sin known to you, and I do not hide my iniquity. You are my protection; you will guard me from the enemy.

32. Behold, the eye of the Lord is upon those who fear him and who await his mercy. Let your mercy, O Lord, be upon us, just as we have awaited you.

XXXIII. I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise shall always be in my mouth. Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together. I sought the Lord, and he answered me; and he delivered me from all my anxieties. Taste and see that the Lord is good; blessed is the man who hopes in him. Fear the Lord, his holy ones, for those who fear him lack nothing. But those who seek the Lord shall lack no good thing. The Lord guards all their bones; not one of them shall be broken. The Lord redeems the souls of his servants.

[Col. 0572A]

XXXIV. Judge, Lord, my adversaries; fight against those who attack me. Take up shield and spear, and rise to my aid. Say to my soul, “I am your salvation.” But my soul shall rejoice in the Lord and exult in his salvation. I will give you thanks in the great assembly, and my tongue shall meditate on your righteousness; all day long I shall praise you.

XXXV. Lord, your mercy is in heaven. How precious is your mercy, Lord! For with you is the fountain of life, and in your light we shall see light. Draw forth your mercy for those who know you, and your righteousness for the upright in heart. Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of the wicked move me.

[Col. 0572B]

XXXVI. I was young, and indeed I have grown old; yet I have not seen the righteous man abandoned. For the Lord loves judgment, and he will not forsake his holy ones. They are preserved forever, and the Lord will help them.

XXXVII. Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor chastise me in your fury. For I waited for you, Lord; you will answer me, Lord my God. Because I followed what is good, do not forsake me. Lord my God, do not withdraw far from me; hasten to my aid, Lord of my salvation.

XXXVIII. You are my expectation; free me from all my iniquities. Do not make me a reproach to the fool; take your scourges away from me.

XXXIX. I waited patiently for the Lord, and he inclined toward me. He heard my cry; Lord, hasten to help me. Let those who seek you rejoice and be glad; you are my help and my salvation, my God; do not delay.

98 XL. I said, “Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.” But you, Lord, have mercy on me.

XLI. As a prepared plot of ground for the irrigation of waters, so my soul is prepared for you, O God.

XLII. Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from an unholy nation; deliver me from the deceitful and wicked man. For you are my strength; why have you cast me away?

XLIII. Rise up and help us; redeem us for the sake of your mercy.

XLIV. Your throne, O God, is forever and ever. Therefore the peoples shall give you thanks forever and ever.

[Col. 0572D]

XLV. Merciful God, hope and strength, you have proved a powerful help in tribulations.

XLVI. A great king over all the earth. Sing to God, sing; sing to our King, sing.

XLVII. For he himself is God, our God, forever and without end. He himself shall be our guide in death.

XLVIII. Yet God will redeem my soul from the hand of the lower world, when he takes me up.

XLIX. The mighty God, the Lord, has spoken: “I will not rebuke you because of your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are always before me. I will not accept a calf from your house, nor goats from your flocks; for all the animals of the forests are mine. I know all the birds of the mountains, and every creature of the field is with me. If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and its fullness are mine. Sacrifice praise to God, and fulfill your vows to the Most High. Call upon me on the day of tribulation; I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me. Whoever sacrifices thanksgiving glorifies me; and to the one who walks rightly I shall show my salvation.”

[Col. 0573A]

L. Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy. According to the multitude of your compassions, blot out my iniquities. Wash me greatly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I acknowledge my iniquities, and my sin is always against me. Against you alone have I sinned, and I have done evil before you. Hide your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities. Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me. Do not cast me away from your presence, and do not take your Holy Spirit from me. Restore to me the joy of your Jesus, and strengthen me with a powerful spirit. Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, God of my salvation; my tongue shall praise your righteousness. Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise. A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit; a broken and humbled heart, O God, you will not despise.

[Col. 0573B]

LI. The mercy of God endures all day. But I, like a flourishing olive tree in the house of God, have hoped in God’s mercy forever and ever.

LII. Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

LIII. O God, save me by your name, and vindicate me by your strength. O God, hear my prayer; listen with your ears to the words of my mouth.

[Col. 0573C]

LIV. Hear my prayer, O God, and do not despise my supplication; attend to me and hear me. But I place my confidence in you.

LV. On whatever day I am afraid, I shall trust in you. I shall not fear what flesh can do to me; this I know, because you are my God.

LVI. Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, for my soul hopes in you. In the shadow of your wings I shall hope until the snares pass away. I shall call upon the Most High God, my avenger. He will send from heaven and save me.

LVII. Truly, God is judge on earth.

LVIII. Deliver me from my enemies, my God, and protect me from those who resist me. I shall preserve my strength for you. For you, O God, are my exaltation; the mercy of my God shall go before me. For you have become my strength and my refuge on the day of my tribulation. I shall sing to you, for you are my God, my helper, my strength, my merciful God.

[Col. 0573D]

LIX. Give us help in tribulation, for salvation from man is futile. Through God we shall act valiantly, and he himself shall trample down those who trouble us.

LX. Hear, O God, my praise; attend to my prayer. From the ends of the earth I shall cry to you when my heart is sorrowful. When the strong man rises against me, you shall be my guide. You were my hope, a most fortified tower in the face of the enemy. I shall dwell in your tabernacle; I shall continually hope in the protection of your wings. For you, O God, have heard my prayer; you have given an inheritance to those who fear your name. Mercy and truth shall preserve him.

99 LXI. For from him comes my expectation; he is my strength and my salvation, my protector; I shall not fear.

LXII. You are my strength, O God; from early dawn I shall rise to you. My soul thirsted for you; my flesh longed for you. Thus I appeared to you in the sanctuary, that I might see your strength and your glory. Your mercy is better than life; my lips shall praise you. Thus I shall bless you during my life; in your name I shall lift up my hands. For you have been my help; in the shadow of your wings I shall praise you.

LXIII. Hear, O God, my voice as I speak; preserve my life from fear of the enemy.

[Col. 0574B]

LXIV. Hear us, O God our savior.

LXV. Let all the earth worship you and sing to you; let it sing to your name. Bless our God, O peoples, and make the voice of his praise heard. He has set our soul in life. Blessed is he who has not removed my prayer or his mercy from me.

LXVI. May God have mercy on us and bless us; may he enlighten his face upon us. May God bless us, our God; may God bless us.

LXVII. Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his face. But let the righteous rejoice and exult in God’s presence; let them rejoice with gladness.

LXVIII. Hear me, Lord, for your mercy is good; according to the multitude of your compassions, look upon me. Do not hide your face from your servant, for I am afflicted; quickly hear me. Draw near to my soul and redeem it; deliver me because of my enemies. Your salvation, O God, has received me.

[Col. 0574C]

LXIX. O God, to deliver me; Lord, hasten to help me. Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you. But I am needy and poor; O God, hasten for me. You are my help and my savior, Lord; do not delay.

LXX. In you, Lord, I have hoped; I shall not be confounded forever. In your righteousness deliver me and free me. Incline your ear to me and save me. My God, save me from the hand of the wicked, from the hand of the unjust and harmful man; for you are my expectation, Lord. O God, do not withdraw far from me; my God, hasten to help me.

[Col. 0574D]

LXXI. Your name shall endure forever; beyond the sun your name shall persist.

LXXII. But for me, it is good to draw near to God; I have placed my hope in the Lord God.

LXXIII. But God is my king from the beginning. Do not hand over to beasts the soul instructed by your law; do not forget forever the lives of your poor.

LXXIV. But I shall proclaim forever; I shall sing to the God of Jacob.

LXXV. When God rises to judgment, to save all the meek of the earth.

LXXVI. With my voice I cried to the Lord; with my voice to the Lord, and he heard me. On the day of my tribulation I sought God.

[Col. 0575A]

LXXVII. But he, being merciful, is appeased toward iniquity and will not destroy.

LXXVIII. Do not remember our former iniquities. Let your mercies quickly precede us, for we have become very weak. Help us, O God our savior, for the glory of your name, and deliver us. And be propitious toward our sins for the sake of your name.

LXXIX. Stir up your strength and come, that you may save us. Lord God of hosts, turn us back, show your face, and we shall be saved.

LXXX. Praise the Lord, our strength.

LXXXI. Judge the poor and the orphan; do justice to the needy and destitute. Save the helpless, and deliver the poor from the hand of the wicked.

[Col. 0575B]

LXXXII. O God, do not be silent; do not keep silence, and do not remain inactive, O God. And they know [F.: may they know] that your name is the Lord; you alone are Most High over all the earth.

LXXXIII. Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer; Lord of hosts, blessed is the man who trusts in you.

100 LXXXIV. Turn us back, O Jesus our savior, and set aside your anger against us. Do not be angry with us forever. Show us, Lord, your mercy, and grant us your salvation.

LXXXV. Incline your ear, Lord, and hear me, for I am needy and poor. Have mercy on me, Lord, for I shall cry to you all day long. Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you I lift up my soul. For you, Lord, are good and propitious, and abundant in mercy to all who call upon you. Hear, Lord, my prayer, and listen to the voice of my supplications. On the day of my tribulation I shall call upon you, for you will hear me. Teach me, Lord, your way, that I may walk in your truth. Make my heart single, that it may fear your name. I will give you thanks, Lord my God, with my whole heart, and I will glorify your name forever. But you, Lord God, merciful and gracious, look upon me and have mercy on me; give strength to your servant, and save the daughter of your maidservant. Establish with me a sign for good, and let those who hate me hear and be confounded. For you, Lord, have helped and comforted me.

[Col. 0575C]

LXXXVI. And all my strong ones shall sing, as in choirs, in you.

LXXXVII. Let my prayer enter before you; incline your ear to my praise. But I cried to you, Lord, and in the morning my prayer shall go before you.

LXXXVIII. The heavens shall confess your wonders, Lord; mercy and truth shall go before your face.

LXXXIX. Let your work appear to your servants, and your glory upon their children. Let the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us, and strengthen the work of our hands.

XC. For you, Lord, are my hope.

XCI. For you have gladdened me, Lord, by your work.

[Col. 0576A]

XCII. Your testimonies have been made exceedingly faithful.

XCIII. Your mercy sustained me.

XCIV. Come, let us worship and bow down; let us bend our knees before the face of the Lord our maker, for he is the Lord our God.

XCV. Glory and beauty are before his face.

XCVI. You who love the Lord, hate evil. He guards the souls of his holy ones; he will deliver them from the hand of the wicked.

XCVII. He remembered his mercy. And exalt the Lord our God.

XCVIII. Serve the Lord with gladness; enter before him with praise.

XCIX. Know that the Lord himself is God; he made us, and we are his.

[Col. 0576B]

C. I shall sing mercy and judgment to you, Lord; I shall sing psalms and be instructed in the perfect way, when you come to me.

CI. Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you. Do not hide your face from me. On the day of my tribulation incline your ear to me. On whatever day I call upon you, quickly hear me.

CII. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and do not forget all his rewards. He is propitious toward all your iniquities and heals all your infirmities. He redeems your life from corruption and crowns you with mercy and compassion.

CIII. Bless the Lord, O my soul; Lord my God, you are greatly magnified. You are clothed with glory and beauty. May the glory of the Lord endure forever; the Lord shall rejoice in his works.

[Col. 0576C]

CIV. Seek the Lord and his strength; seek his face continually. Remember his wonders, which he has done.

CV. Blessed are those who keep judgment and practice justice at all times. Save us, Lord our God, that we may give thanks to your holy name and sing in praise: “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel.”

CVI. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever. Give thanks to the Lord for his mercies and his wonders toward the children of men. For he has satisfied the empty soul and filled the hungry soul with good things.

CVII. Give us help in tribulation, for salvation from man is futile. In God we shall be strong, and he himself shall trample our enemies.

[Col. 0576D]

101 CVIII. But you, O God the Lord, act for me for the sake of your name, for your mercy is good. Deliver me, for I am needy and poor; help me, Lord my God. Save me according to your mercy.

CIX. Rule in the midst of your enemies.

CX. I will give thanks to the Lord with my whole heart. Glory and beauty are his work; the work of his hands is truth and judgment.

CXI. Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he shall greatly delight in his commandments. The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance; he shall not fear evil tidings. May the name of the Lord be blessed, now and forever.

[Col. 0577A]

CXII. Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, because of your mercy and your truth.

CXIII. I beseech you, Lord, save my soul.

CXIV. And I shall call upon the name of the Lord. Glorious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his holy ones.

CXV. And the truth of the Lord endures forever.

CXVI. You are the Lord, my Lord; I shall not fear what man can do to me. The Lord is my helper, and I shall despise those who hate me. It is better to hope in the Lord than to hope in man. It is better to hope in the Lord than to hope in princes. I will give you thanks, Lord, for you have heard me and have become my salvation.

[Col. 0577B]

CXVII. I will give you thanks, Lord, with an upright heart, when I have learned the judgments of your righteousness. Do not let me stray from your commandments. Open my eyes, and I shall see wonders in your law. Take the way of falsehood away from me, and grant me your law. Incline my heart to your testimonies and not to greed. Let your mercies come to me, Lord, and your salvation according to your word. This is my consolation in my affliction, because your word has given me life. Your mercy has filled the earth; teach me your precepts. Before I heard, I was ignorant. You are good and beneficent; teach me your precepts. Let your mercy, I beseech you, be my consolation, as you spoke to your servant. According to your mercy give me life, and I shall keep the testimony of your mouth. If your law had not been my meditation, I might have perished in my distress. How sweet is your word to my throat, sweeter than honey to my mouth. Let the voluntary offerings of my mouth please you, Lord, and teach me according to your judgments. Strengthen me according to your word, and I shall live; help me, and I shall be saved. Deal with your servant according to your mercy, and teach me your precepts. Look upon me and have mercy on me, and teach me your precepts. You are righteous, Lord, and your judgment is right. Hear my voice according to your mercy, Lord; according to your judgment give me life. See my affliction and deliver me; according to your mercy give me life. There is great peace for those who love your law, and there is no stumbling-block for them. Let my praise enter before you, Lord, according to your word. Let my supplication come before your face; according to your word deliver me.

[Col. 0577C]

CXVIII. Lord, deliver my soul from lying lips and from a deceitful tongue.

CXIX. I will lift up my eyes to the mountains, from where help may come to me.

CXX. May it go well with those who love you.

CXXI. Have mercy on us, Lord; have mercy on us.

CXXII. Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

CXXIII. Deal well, Lord, with those who are good and upright in heart.

CXXIV. Turn back our captivity, Lord, like a stream in the south.

[Col. 0578A]

CXXV. Unless the Lord guards the city, the one who guards it keeps watch in vain.

CXXVI. Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways.

CXXVII. May the blessing of the Lord be upon us.

CXXVIII. Lord, hear my voice. Let your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication.

CXXIX. Lord, my heart has not been exalted, nor have my eyes been lifted up.

CXXX. This is my resting place forever.

CXXXI. For there the Lord commanded blessing and life forever.

102 CXXXII. You who stand in the house of the Lord.

CXXXIII. Praise the Lord, for he is good.

CXXXIV. Give thanks to the God of heaven, for his mercy endures forever.

[Col. 0578B]

CXXXV. Blessed is the man who loves the Lord.

CXXXVI. I will give you thanks, Lord, with my whole heart. Lord, your mercy endures forever; do not abandon the works of your hands.

CXXXVII. If I ascend into heaven, you are there; if I lie down in the underworld, you are present.

CXXXVIII. Deliver me, Lord, from the evil man; save me from unjust men.

CXXXIX. Hear my voice as I cry to you. Let my prayer be directed like incense in your sight.

CXL. Place, Lord, a guard over my mouth; preserve the poverty of my lips. Lead my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks to your name.

[Col. 0578C]

CXLI. Lord, hear my prayer; hear me in your righteousness. Do not enter into judgment with your servant, for no living person shall be justified in your sight. Make me hear your mercy in the morning, for I trust in you. Make known to me the way in which I should walk, for I lift up my soul to you. Deliver me from my enemies, Lord; I am protected by you. Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your good spirit shall lead me into a straight land. For the sake of your name, Lord, you shall give me life in your righteousness. For I am your servant.

CXLII. Blessed is the Lord, my strong one, my mercy and my strength; my helper and my savior.

[Col. 0578D]

CXLIII. Every day I shall bless you, and I shall praise your name forever and continually.

CXLIV. My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord, and all flesh shall bless his holy name forever and continually.

CXLV. Praise the Lord, O my soul; I shall praise the Lord during my life; I shall sing to my God as long as I exist.

CXLVI. Praise the Lord, for he is good; may the Lord be pleased with those who fear him and await his mercy.

CXLVII. He will blow with his spirit, and the waters will flow.

CXLVIII. Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the heights. Praise him, all his angels. Praise him, all his armies. Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, stars of light. Praise him, heavens of heavens, and let the waters that are above the heavens praise the name of the Lord. For he commanded, and they were created. Praise the Lord, kings of the earth and all peoples; princes and all judges of the earth. Let young men and virgins, old men and children, praise the name of the Lord. For his name alone is exalted; his glory is in heaven and on earth. He has exalted the horn of his people; praise belongs to all his holy ones.

[Col. 0579A]

CXLIX. Sing a new song to the Lord; his praise is in the assembly of the holy ones. He shall exalt the meek in Jesus. The holy ones shall exult in glory; they shall praise him on their couches. The praises of God shall be in their throats.

CL. Let everything that breathes praise the Lord.

LITANY AS ABOVE, AND PRAYERS.

[Col. 0579B]

My soul lives, and it shall praise you. Judge, Lord, those who do harm to me. Let my mouth be filled with praise. Lord, turn your face away from my sins. Create in me a clean heart, O God. Restore to me the joy of your salvation. Lord, do not hand me over together with sinners. Lord, do not deal with us according to our sins. Lord, do not remember our iniquities. Help us, O God our savior. Be for us, Lord, a tower of strength. Be my helper and deliverer, Lord. Blessed is the Lord day by day. Do not enter into judgment with your servant. The sins of my youth. Deliver me, Lord, from the evil man. Deliver me from my enemies, my God. Deliver me from those who work iniquity.

[Col. 0579C]

Thus I shall sing the psalm to your name forever and ever. Hear us, O God our savior. O God, attend to my help. Holy God, holy strong one. May God the Father bless us. O Lord, save me. Lord, save the king. Save your people. Save your servants. Remember your assembly. Hear my voice, Lord. Have mercy on me, O God, entirely. Lord, hear.

103 **PRAYER OF EUGENIUS, BISHOP OF TOLEDO**

[Note: [Col. 0579D] This prayer appears first among the other prayers and poems of blessed Eugenius in volume XII of the *Bibliotheca Patrum*, Lyon edition, 1677, p. 345.]

King God, by whom the structure of the immense world stands,

What I, wretched man, implore, gracious Christ, accomplish.

Let right faith be mine, confronting false sects.

Let the correction of my morals especially be present.

May I be dear, humble, truthful, prudent in due season,

Silent about what is secret, and cautious in the speech of my tongue.

[Col. 0579D]

Give me a faithful companion, always a steadfast friend.

Give me a gentle, sober, frugal, and chaste servant.

Let poverty not torment me, nor sickness cripple me.

Let kindly health and sufficient nourishment be my companions.

Let wealth, arrogance, quarrels, and disputes be absent,

Envy, luxury, and the disgraceful tax of the belly.

May I neither injure anyone by crime nor be injured by crime.

Thus may I be able to will what causes the power to do wrong to withdraw.

May I never desire, do, or speak anything shameful.

May my mind desire you, my tongue sing, and my action bring you forth.

[Col. 0580A]

Grant, thunder-bearing Father, a billowing rain of tears,

By which I may dissolve the burdens of my faults with tears.

Grant, I pray, help by which I may conquer the world,

And traverse the course of life with peaceful steps.

And when the final day of death has opened the urn,

Grant pardon to the one whose guilt removes the crown.

**SATURDAY. IF THE PRESENT LIFE IS DISPLEASING TO SOMEONE, IT IS HELPFUL FOR HIM TO CONTEMPLATE THE LIFE ABOVE. PRAYER OF SAINT AUGUSTINE.**

[Note: [Col. 0580D] For the fifth use, above, col. 467.]

God, creator of the universe, grant me first that I may ask you rightly; next, that I may conduct myself worthily of being delivered by you; finally, that you may deliver me. God, through whom all things that would not exist by themselves strive toward existence. God, who do not even permit that which destroys itself mutually to perish. God, who created this world from nothing, the most beautiful of all that eyes perceive. God, who do not make evil, yet cause it to exist so that it may not become the worst. God, who show to the few who flee toward what truly is that evil is nothing. God, through whom the universe, even with its darker part, is perfect. God, from whom there is no discord to the very end, since inferior things harmonize with better things. God, whom everything capable of loving may love, whether knowingly or unknowingly. God, in whom all things exist, yet whose whole creation possesses neither a shameful ugliness nor a harmful wickedness, nor does error err. God, who did not wish us to know you truly unless we were cleansed; God the Father of truth, Father of wisdom, Father of true and supreme life, Father of blessedness, Father of good and beautiful things, Father of intelligible light, Father of our awakening and illumination, Father of the pledge by which we are admonished to return to you—I call upon you.

[Col. 0580B]

God, truth, in whom, from whom, and through whom all things that are true are true. God, wisdom, in whom, from whom, and through whom all things that possess wisdom are wise. God, true and supreme life, in whom, from whom, and through whom all things that truly and supremely live live. God, blessedness, in whom, from whom, and through whom all things that are blessed are blessed. God, good and beautiful, in whom, from whom, and through whom all things good and beautiful are good and beautiful. God, intelligible light, in whom, from whom, and through whom all things that shine intelligibly shine. God, whose kingdom is the whole world, which the mortal sense of the body does not perceive. God, from whose kingdom the law is also inscribed in these earthly kingdoms. God, from whom to turn away is to fall; toward whom to turn is to rise again; in whom to remain is to stand firm. God, from whom to depart is to die; to return to whom is to come back to life; to dwell in whom is to live.

104 God, whom no one loses unless deceived, whom no one seeks unless admonished, whom no one finds unless purified. God, to abandon whom is the same as to perish; to attend to whom is the same as to love; to see whom is the same as to possess. God, whose faith awakens us, whose hope raises us, whose charity joins us. God, through whom we conquer the enemy, I beseech you. God, whom we have received so that we might not perish altogether. God, by whom we are admonished to keep watch.

[Col. 0581A]

God, through whom we distinguish good from evil. God, through whom we flee evils and pursue good things. God, through whom we do not yield to adversities. God, through whom we serve well and rule well. God, through whom we learn that what once seemed ours is another’s, and what we once thought another’s is ours. God, through whom we do not cling to the foods and enticements of evils. God, through whom small things do not diminish us. God, through whom our better nature is not subjected to what is worse. God, through whom death is swallowed up in victory. God, who turns us around. God, who strips us of what is not and clothes us with what is. God, who makes us worthy to be heard. God, who fortifies us. God, who leads us into all truth. God, who speaks all good things to us, neither making us insane nor allowing anyone else to do so. God, who recalls us to the way.
