God, who causes the door to be opened to those who knock. God, who leads us to the door. God, who gives us the bread of life. God, through whom we thirst for the drink that, once tasted, will never leave us thirsty. God, who convicts the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment. God, through whom those who scarcely believe do not move us. God, through whom we reject the error of those who think that the merits of souls count for nothing with you. God, through whom we do not serve weak and needy elements. God, who purify us and prepare us for divine rewards.

[Col. 0581B]

Come graciously to my aid: you, the one God, whatever has been said by me. You, you, come, come to my aid, one, eternal, true substance, where there is no discrepancy, no confusion, no change, no need, no death; where there is perfect harmony, perfect clarity, perfect constancy, perfect fullness, perfect life; where nothing is lacking, where all things overflow, where the begetter and the one begotten are one; whom all things that serve serve, whom every good soul obeys, by whose laws the heavens revolve, the stars complete their courses, the sun brings forth the day, and the moon regulates the night.

[Col. 0581C]

And the whole world, through days by the succession of light and darkness, through months by the waxing and waning of the moon, and through years by the succession of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, traverses its course. Through the perfection of the sun’s course, by the great returns of the world to the risings of the stars, it preserves the great coherence of things, insofar as sensible matter permits, through the orders and repetitions of times. By whose laws, standing forever, the unstable motion of mutable things is not allowed to become disordered; and by the reins of revolving ages it is always renewed in the likeness of stability.

[Col. 0581D]

By whose laws the soul’s free choice exists, and rewards for the good and punishments for the evil have been distributed with necessities fixed throughout. From whom all good things flow to us; from whom all evils are restrained from reaching us. Above whom there is nothing, outside whom there is nothing, without whom there is nothing; beneath whom everything is, in whom everything is, with whom everything is. You made humanity in your image and likeness; whoever knows himself recognizes this.

Hear me, hear me, hear me, my God, my Lord, my King, my Father, my cause, my hope, my possession, my honor, my home, my homeland, my salvation, my light, my life. Hear me, hear me, hear me in that manner of yours known to few. For I love you alone, follow you alone, seek you alone, and am ready to serve you alone, because you alone rule justly. I desire to belong to you; command, I beg you, and order whatever you will. But heal and open my ears, by which I may hear your voices. Heal and open my eyes, by which I may see your signs. Drive madness away from me, that I may recognize you. Tell me where I should direct my attention, so that I may look upon you; and I hope to do everything that you command.

[Col. 0582A]

Look upon your fugitive, most merciful Lord. By now I have suffered punishments enough; I have served your enemies, whom you hold beneath your feet, long enough; I have been the plaything of deceits long enough. Receive me, your servant, as I flee from those things, since they too received me as one estranged when I was fleeing from you. I perceive that I must return to you. Let your door be opened to me as I knock, but teach me how one reaches you.

I have nothing else but willingness. I know nothing else except that things fleeting and perishable must be despised, and things certain and eternal must be sought. This I do, Father, because this alone I know; but I do not know how one reaches you. Suggest it to me; show it to me; provide me with provisions for the journey. If those who flee to you find you by faith, give me faith; if by virtue, virtue; if by knowledge, knowledge. Increase hope in me. Increase charity.

O wondrous and singular goodness of yours! I hasten toward you, and I ask you again how one hastens toward you. For if you abandon me, I perish here; but you do not abandon me, because you are the highest good, which no one has rightly sought without finding it. Everyone has rightly sought whom you have caused to seek rightly. Make me such, Father; rescue me from error.

[Col. 0582C]

As I seek you, let nothing else present itself in place of you. If I desire nothing other than you, may I find you now, I beg you, Father. But if there is in me a desire for something superfluous, cleanse me yourself and make me fit to see you.

As for the well-being of this mortal body of mine, while I dwell in it, I do not know what benefit it offers me or those whom I love. I entrust it to you, wisest and best Father, and for whatever you admonish me concerning it for a time, I shall pray. I ask only this of your supreme mercy: turn me wholly toward you; do not allow anything to resist me as I strive toward you; and command that, while I inhabit and bear this very body, I be pure, magnanimous, just, and prudent, a perfect lover and apprehender of your wisdom, worthy of dwelling in your kingdom and a most blessed inhabitant of it. Amen.

O God, attend to my aid, three times.

**PSALM**

(PSALM XLI.) As the deer longs for springs of water, so my soul longs for you, O God. My soul thirsted for the strong and living God; when shall I come and appear before the face of God? My tears have been my bread day and night, while it is said to me daily, “Where is your God?” I remembered these things and poured out my soul within me, for I shall pass into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God, amid the voice of exultation and thanksgiving, the sound of one feasting. Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I shall still give him thanks: he is the salvation of my face and my God.

[Col. 0583A]

My soul within me is troubled; therefore I shall remember you from the land of the Jordan and from Hermoniim, from the little mountain. Deep calls to deep at the sound of your cataracts. All your heights and your waves have passed over me. By day the Lord commanded his mercy, and by night his song. With me is prayer to the God of my life. I shall say to God, “You are my protector.” Why have you forgotten me, and why do I walk sorrowfully while the enemy afflicts me? While my bones are crushed, those who trouble me, my enemies, reproached me. While they say to me each day, “Where is your God?” Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I shall still give him thanks: he is the salvation of my face and my God.

[Col. 0583B]

As above. I will love you, Lord, my strength. The Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my deliverer. My God is my helper, and I shall hope in him.

**Prayer.** O wondrous salvation of our face, which the souls of the faithful servants ardently thirst for, grant, we ask, that while we seek you, nourished visibly by a shower of tears, we may place you invisibly within the tabernacle of our breast. Through.

**PSALM**
## (Psalm 62)

O God, you are my God; at first light I keep watch for you. My soul thirsts for you; how greatly my flesh longs for you. In a desert land, trackless and waterless, thus have I appeared before you in the [Col. 0583C] sanctuary, that I might behold your power and your glory. For your mercy is better than lives; my lips shall praise you. Thus will I bless you in my life; and in your name I will raise my hands. May my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness; and my mouth shall praise you with lips of exultation. Thus I remembered you upon my bed; in the morning I shall meditate on you, because you have been my helper. And under the shelter of your wings I shall exult; my soul clung to you; your right hand upheld me. But they sought my soul in vain; they shall enter into the depths of the earth; they shall be handed over to the power of the sword; they shall become the portion of foxes. But the king shall rejoice in God; all who swear by him shall be praised, because the mouth of those who speak wickedness has been stopped.

[Col. 0583D] As above. Blessed is he whom you have chosen and taken up; he shall dwell in your courts.

**Prayer.** Grant everlasting light to those who keep watch for you at dawn, O author of eternal light, so that our lips may praise you, our life bless you, and our morning meditation glorify you. Through him.

## Psalm

### (Psalm 83)

How lovely are your tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! My soul longs and languishes for the courts of the Lord. My heart and my flesh have exulted in the living God. For the sparrow has found a house for itself, and the turtledove a nest for itself, where it may place its young. Your altars, O Lord of hosts, my King and my God. [Col. 0584A] Blessed are those who dwell in your house, O Lord; forever and ever they shall praise you. Blessed is the man whose help is from you; he has arranged ascents in his heart, in the valley of tears, in the place he has appointed. For the lawgiver will give a blessing; they shall go from strength to strength; the God of gods shall be seen in Zion. O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer; listen with your ears, O God of Jacob. Behold, O God our protector, and look upon the face of your anointed. For one day in your courts is better than thousands. I have chosen to be rejected in the house of my God rather than to dwell in the tents of sinners. For God loves mercy and truth; the Lord will give grace and glory. He will not deprive those who walk in innocence of good things. O Lord of hosts, blessed is the person who hopes in you.

**Litany, as above.**

[Col. 0584B]

Strengthen this, O God, which you have wrought in us; from your temple in Jerusalem kings offer gifts to you. Send forth your Spirit, and they shall be created, and you shall renew the face of the earth. May the glory of the Lord endure forever; the Lord shall rejoice in his works. May my speech be pleasing to him; but I shall delight in the Lord. Let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice, and be strengthened; seek his face always.

**Prayer.** Eternal God, founder of the heavenly tabernacles, arrange, we ask, ascents in our hearts, by which we may deserve to climb without the fall of sin to your tabernacles. Through him.

## Prayer of Saint Isidore

[Col. 0584C] “Blessed are those servants whom, when the Lord comes, he finds watching” (Luke 12:37). Blessed is the vigil by which one keeps watch for the Lord, lover of the universe. Would that you might also deign, O Lord, to awaken me, vile though I am, yet still your little servant, from the sleep of sluggishness; to kindle me with that fire of divine love by which the flame of your charity, the desire of your excessive love, might blaze from my heart above the stars, and the divine fire might always burn within me! Would that I had the wood by which that fire might continually be fed, nourished, kindled, and that flame sustained which would not know how to be extinguished but would know how to increase! Would that I were of such merit that my lamp might always burn throughout the whole night in the temple of the Lord my God, so that it might shine for all who enter the house of God!

Grant me, Lord, I beg you, in the name of [Col. 0584D] Jesus Christ, your Son, my God, that charity which does not know how to fall, so that my lamp may know how to be kindled but not how to be extinguished; may it burn for me and give light to others. May you yourself, O Christ, deign to kindle our lamps, and, most luminous Savior, so that they may shine perpetually in your temple and receive everlasting light from you, the everlasting light; so that our darkness may be illumined and the darkness of the world driven away.

Thus grant light to my lamp, I beg you, Lord Jesus, so that by the brilliance of that light those holy of holies may appear to me in such a way that they contain you, the eternal high priest of eternal things, entering the inner parts of that great temple of yours, where I may continually behold, desire, and await you alone. May I long for you, loving you so greatly. May it be yours, [Col. 0585A] I ask, most loving Savior, to reveal yourself to us when we knock, so that, understanding you more fully, we may love only you, meditate on you alone day and night, and always think of you.

Deign to breathe into us your love in the measure in which it is fitting that God be loved and cherished, so that your love may fill all our inward parts, your affection possess us wholly, and your charity fill us; so that, set aflame by your charity, we may know how to love nothing besides you, and so that such great charity may not be extinguished in us by the many waters of this air, this earth, and this sea, according to the saying: “Many waters cannot extinguish charity.” May God also bring this to fulfillment in us, even in part, through the gift of our Lord Jesus Christ.

## Another Prayer of the Same

[Col. 0585B] Be with us, we ask, Lord, that you may defend us in glory; be within us, that you may receive us; be around us, that you may preserve us; be before us, that you may lead us; be for us, that you may intercede for us; be above all things, that you may bless us and summon us to your kingdom—you who live and reign.

## Also on Saturday, in Honor of All the Saints: Prayer of Pope Saint Gregory

Almighty God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one Trinity in three persons, who are the same, who were, and who are to come: deliver me, Lord, from all my sins and from this mortality, and from the [Col. 0585C] death of punishment, from the sole of my foot to the crown of my head, within and without.

Intercede for me, holy cherubim, holy seraphim, holy thrones, holy dominions, holy principalities, holy powers, holy virtues, holy angels, holy archangels. Saint Gabriel, Saint Michael, Saint Raphael, pray for me.

Intercede for me, holy patriarchs, holy leaders, holy judges, holy priests, holy prophets, holy kings, holy Maccabees, holy Innocents. Intercede for me, Nativity of Christ, Circumcision of Christ, Baptism of Christ, work of Christ, virtues of Christ, teaching of Christ, cross of Christ, soul of Christ, flesh of Christ, resurrection of Christ, descent of Christ, ascension of Christ.

Holy Mary, holy apostles, holy disciples, holy successors, holy baptizers, holy leaders, [Col. 0585D] holy bishops, holy presbyters, holy deacons, holy subdeacons, holy readers, holy exorcists, holy martyrs, holy confessors, holy anchorites, holy monks, holy clerics, holy laypeople, holy virgins, holy wives, holy masters, holy servants, holy rich, holy poor, holy teachers, holy brothers, holy sisters.

May the names and memories of all these generally, their spirits and souls, their holy thoughts, holy words, holy works, merits in heaven, relics on earth, and the riches of God’s goodness, long-suffering, patience, and mercy—all these, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ—be shields, helmets, healings, aids, and breastplates for my soul, [Col. 0586A] my spirit, and my body, with all my persons within and without, from the sole of my foot to the crown of my head: for my sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch, flesh, and blood, with all my bones, nerves, inner parts, veins, marrow, joints, limbs, skin, and passages.

For through you, Jesus Christ, all things are made alive, inspired, changed, and healed. Protect me, Lord, on the right and on the left, before and behind, beneath and above, in the air, on the earth, in the waters, in the sea, in bending, rising, walking, sitting, standing, going about, watching, sleeping, in every place, at every hour, every day, every night, throughout all life. Help me, guard me, holy Trinity, almighty God.

Deliver me, Lord, from every past, present, and future evil: from the dangers of land and sea, from all beasts, phantoms, birds, four-footed creatures, and serpents. Defend me from fire and lightning, thunder, hail, snow, rain, winds, the opening of the earth, whirlwinds, earthquakes, all evil people, spells, and envious eyes.

I confess the wickedness of my sin; for I am a sinner, and born from sin. But you are the true, almighty God, without sin. I ask the Father through the Son. I ask the Son through the Father. I ask the Holy Spirit through the Father and the Son, that all vices may be removed from me and all holy virtues planted in me.

[Col. 0586C] Immense God, 108 from whom all things are, through whom all things are, in whom all things visible and invisible have been made, covering above, supporting below, surrounding your works outside, filling them within: guard me, Lord, your creature, forever. I invoke all these for my help. Through him.

## Psalm in Honor of Saint Mary

### (Psalm 44)

My heart has poured forth a good word; I declare my works to the King. My tongue is the pen of a swift-writing scribe. You are beautiful beyond the sons of men; grace has been poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever. Gird your sword upon your thigh, O most mighty. In your appearance and your beauty, advance, prosper, and reign. Because of truth and gentleness and righteousness, your right hand shall lead you wondrously. Your arrows are sharp; peoples shall fall beneath you into the hearts of the king’s enemies. [Col. 0586D] Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; the rod of uprightness is the rod of your kingdom. You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions. Myrrh, myrrh-drip, and cassia are on your garments, from ivory houses; by these the daughters of kings have delighted you in your honor. The queen stood at your right hand in a golden garment, surrounded by variety.

Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house. And the King shall desire your beauty, for he himself is the Lord your God, and they shall worship him. And the daughters of Tyre with gifts; all the rich among the people shall entreat your face. All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, clothed around with varied embroideries and gold fringes. [Col. 0587A] Virgins shall be brought to the king after her; her companions shall be brought to you. They shall be brought with joy and exultation; they shall be brought into the king’s temple. In place of your fathers, sons have been born to you; you shall appoint them princes over all the earth. I shall remember your name throughout every generation and generation. Therefore peoples shall praise you forever and ever.

**Prayer.** Christ the Lord, Word of the Father, through whom all things have been created and are created, preserve, we ask, your Church gathered from the diversity of peoples, so that while we love you with a pure heart through the righteousness of faith itself, we may deserve, with the Fathers, the dominion of the eternal age. Through him.

**Another prayer.** O Lord our God, whose throne remains [Col. 0587B] forever and ever, grant that we may lay open our works before you, our King, to whom they are known before they come to be, and through whom we know the powers that are present. Through him.

## Psalm of the Apostles

### (Psalm 18)

The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands. Day pours forth the word to day, and night reveals knowledge to night. There are no languages or speeches whose voices are not heard. Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. He has placed his tabernacle in the sun, and he himself is like a bridegroom coming forth from his chamber. He rejoiced like a giant to run his course; his going forth is from the highest heaven. His circuit reaches to its summit, and no one is [Col. 0587C] hidden from his heat.

The law of the Lord is spotless, converting souls; the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to the little ones. The ordinances of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts; the commandment of the Lord is bright, enlightening the eyes. The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring forever and ever; the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves. They are more desirable than gold and many precious stones, and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb. For your servant keeps them; in keeping them there is great reward.

Who understands offenses? Cleanse me from my hidden faults, and spare your servant from those belonging to others. If they do not dominate me, then I shall be spotless, and I shall be cleansed from the greatest offense. And may the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart always be pleasing in your sight, O Lord, my helper and my [Col. 0587D] redeemer.

As above. “To the saints who are”; “their sound has gone out into all the earth.” “You shall appoint them.” “Your friends, O God, have been greatly honored.”

109 **Prayer.** O Lord, before whom no one is hidden, from whose searching nothing concealed remains undisclosed: cleanse us from our hidden faults, spare your servants from those belonging to others, and grant that, in the heat of your examination, the purity granted by you may not be scorched.

## Psalm of the Martyrs

### (Psalm 32)

Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise befits the upright. Give thanks to the Lord with the lyre; sing to him on the ten-stringed psaltery. Sing to him a new song; sing well to him with shouting. [Col. 0588A] For the word of the Lord is right, and all his works are in faithfulness. He loves mercy and judgment; the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.

By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the breath of his mouth all their host. Gathering the waters of the sea as in a wineskin, placing the deeps in storehouses. Let all the earth fear the Lord; and let all who inhabit the world be moved before him. For he spoke, and they were made; he commanded, and they were created.

The Lord scatters the counsels of the nations; he rejects the thoughts of the peoples, and he rejects the counsels of princes. But the counsel of the Lord remains forever; the thoughts of his heart endure from generation to generation. Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom he chose as his inheritance.

From heaven the Lord looked down; he saw all the sons of men. From his prepared dwelling he looked upon all who inhabit the earth. He fashioned their hearts one by one; he understands all their works. A king is not saved by great power, nor shall a giant be saved by the abundance of his strength. A horse is deceptive for salvation; despite the abundance of its strength, it shall not save.

Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him and upon those who hope in his mercy, to rescue their souls from death and feed them in famine. Our soul waits for the Lord, for he is our helper and protector. For our heart shall rejoice in him, and we have hoped in his holy name. Let your mercy, O Lord, be upon us, just as we have hoped in you.

As above. “To the saints who are in his land.” “You crowned them with glory and honor.” “You have established, O Lord.”

[Col. 0588C] **Prayer.** Let your mercy, O Lord, be upon us, and instill in our souls patience to endure all things through the help of your protection. You who fashion human hearts individually, sanctify us by your hope; and because your eyes are upon those who [lacuna; perhaps “fear you”], grant us the fullness of your fear, so that you may also confer dignity upon us in your sight.

## Another Psalm of the Martyrs

### (Psalm 78)

O God, the nations have entered into your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem a place for keeping fruit. They have given the corpses of your servants as food to the birds of heaven, the flesh of your saints to the beasts of the earth. They have [Col. 0588D] poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them. We have become a reproach to our neighbors, a mockery and derision to those around us.

How long, O Lord, will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire? Pour out your wrath upon the nations that do not know you, and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon your name. For they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling. Do not remember our former iniquities; may your mercies quickly anticipate us, because we have become exceedingly poor.

Help us, O God our Savior; and for the glory of your name, O Lord, deliver us and be gracious to our sins for the sake of your name. Lest they should say among the nations, [Col. 0589A] “Where is their God?” Let the vengeance for the blood of your servants that has been poured out enter into your sight; let the groaning of the bound come before you. According to the greatness of your arm, possess the sons of those put to death.

And repay our neighbors sevenfold in their bosom the reproach with which they reproached you, O Lord. But we, your people and the sheep of your pasture, shall give you thanks forever; from generation to generation we shall proclaim your praise.

110 As above. “The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous.” “Precious in the sight of the Lord.” “The souls of the righteous.”

**Prayer.** Do not remember our former iniquities, Lord, nor let original guilt grieve us, whom a second birth regenerates in Christ. [Col. 0589B] Let your mercy therefore seize us, Lord, because the Creator of humanity is born as a human being, and the human being is taken up for glorification in God [perhaps “is to be glorified”].

## Psalm of the Confessors

### (Psalm 123)

“If the Lord had not been with us,” let Israel now say, “if the Lord had not been with us.” When men rose up against us, perhaps they would have swallowed us alive. When their fury raged against us, perhaps the water would have engulfed us. Our soul passed through the torrent; perhaps our soul would have passed through unbearable water. Blessed is the Lord, who did not give us as prey to their teeth. Our soul was rescued like a sparrow from the snare of the hunters. The snare was broken, and we were set free. [Col. 0589C] Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

As above. “The enemies have exhausted the sword [Vulgate: swords] to the end.” “You have destroyed all his fences.” “My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord.”

**Prayer.** Turn aside, Lord, the snares that those who try to hunt our souls set against us; and through the aid of your help confound the plots of those who oppose and capture us, because unless you are in us, hostile power can swallow us just as it can absorb us. Be both the guardian and the guide of your servants, so that they may not fall into the traps of spiritual wickedness, but may exercise with complete eagerness those flights by which they strive to come to you.

“Praise the Lord from the heavens.” Look back under the first feria.

**Litanies, as above.**

The righteous live forever. All who love your name shall glory in you. The saints shall exult in glory. Let them exult in the presence of God; with you, O Lord, is the fountain of life. God is wonderful in his saints. In the presence of the angels I shall sing to you. Hear, O Lord, my voice with which I cried out.

## Prayer of Saint Gregory

O sovereign Lord, almighty God, who are one Trinity—the Father in the Son, the Son in the Father, with the Holy Spirit—who are always in all things, who were before all things, and who shall be above all things, blessed God forever: [Col. 0590A] I commend my soul into the hands of your power, so that you may guard it by days and nights, by hours and moments.

Have mercy on me, God of the angels. Direct me, King of the archangels. Guard me through the prayers of the patriarchs, through the merits of the prophets, through the intercessions of the apostles, through the victories of the martyrs, through the faith of the confessors, through the intercession of all the saints who pleased you from the beginning of the world to the consummation of the age.

May Saint Abel pray for me, he who was first crowned by martyrdom. May Saint Seth pray for me, he who first began to invoke the name of the Lord. May Saint Enoch pray for me, he who walked with God and was taken from the world. May Saint Noah pray for me, whom God preserved in the flood because of his righteousness. May Melchizedek, the righteous king, pray for me, he who [Col. 0590B] met Abraham and blessed him.

May faithful Abraham plead for me, he who first believed and whose faith was reckoned as righteousness. May righteous Isaac intercede for me, he who was obedient to his father unto death, as an example of our Lord Jesus Christ, who was offered to God the Father for the salvation of the world. May blessed Jacob petition for me, he who saw the angels of God and of the Lord coming to his aid.

May blessed Joseph pray for me, he who interpreted the king’s dreams and was released from prison. May holy Job pray for me, great and patient, who committed no sin with his lips in all that happened to him. May blessed Moses pray for me, with whom God spoke face to face. May Jesus son of Nun pray for me, whom you chose, Lord, after Moses your servant.

May holy Samuel [Col. 0590C] the prophet pray for me, who blessed and anointed two kings over Israel. May holy David, whom you chose according to your heart, Lord, come to my aid. May the holy prophet Elijah plead for me, whom you raised to heaven in a fiery chariot. May blessed Isaiah pray for me, whose lips were cleansed by heavenly fire. May blessed Jeremiah stand by me, whom you sanctified in his mother’s womb.

May holy Ezekiel the prophet pray for me, who saw wondrous visions of God and prophesied the resurrection of the dead. May the chosen Daniel, beloved of God, plead for me, who interpreted the king’s dreams and was delivered from the lions’ den; and the three youths Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, who were delivered from the fire.

The twelve prophets: Hosea, Amos, Micah, Joel, Obadiah, Habakkuk, Jonah, Nahum, Zephaniah, Haggai, [Col. 0590D] Zechariah, Malachi; Esdras, Tobias, and the Maccabees. I invoke these and all the saints of the Old Testament for my help.

May the holy virgin Mary, mother of the Savior, pray for me; and holy John the Baptist, the forerunner of the Lord; and all the holy apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ: Peter and Paul, Andrew and John, the three Jameses, Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew, Thaddaeus, Simon, Barnabas and Matthias, Mark, Luke, and Stephen.

Through the merits of these and all the other saints of the New Testament, drive from me, Lord, the desire of gluttony, and give me the virtue of abstinence. Flee from me, spirit of fornication, and give me the ardor of chastity. Extinguish greed in me, and give me voluntary [Col. 0591A] poverty. Restrain my anger from me, and kindle in me great gentleness and love of God and neighbor.

Cut off from me, Lord, worldly sadness; increase spiritual joy in me. Drive away from me boastfulness of mind; grant me your fear and love, compunction of heart. Lessen my pride and perfect true humility in me.

I am an unworthy and unhappy man. Who will deliver me from this body of death, of sin, except your grace, Lord Jesus Christ? For I am a sinner, my offenses are innumerable, and I am not worthy to be called your servant. Awaken weeping in me; soften my hard, stony heart; kindle in me the fire of your fear, because I am dead ash.

Deliver my soul from the snares of the enemy and preserve me in your will. Teach me to do [Col. 0591B] your will, because you are my God. To you be honor and glory throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

## Litany of the Blessed Apostles, Martyrs Also, Confessors, and Virgins

[Col. 0591D] Collected from the book that blessed Jerome composed concerning the birthdays of the saints throughout the cycle of the year.

[Note: “From the book,” etc. He undoubtedly understands the Martyrology, which learned men consider to have been falsely attributed to Saint Jerome, although there are not lacking writers—serious men and of the highest standing—who affirm that Saint Jerome composed the Martyrology, or was the translator of Eusebius. See the admonition to this Martyrology, volume XI of the works of Saint Jerome, Verona edition, p. 471.]

[Note: It exists with variations in the prayer book of Charles the Bald, p. 94.]

## First Feria

Have mercy on us in our misery, merciful holy Trinity, and forgive all our sins which we have committed before your angels in your sight, through the merits, prayers, intercessions, and invocations [Col. 0591C] of all your saints, whose feast is celebrated on N. and whose names we now recite.

Deliver us, merciful Trinity, together with all our brothers and sisters, [The book of Charles the Bald adds: “together with our wife Yrmindrud and our children and all the Christian people”] from every past, present, and future evil: from death to life, from darkness to light, from hell to paradise, from evil to good, from ignorance to knowledge, from sins to true penitence, from all vices to perfect virtues, from every ambush of the enemy to heavenly medicine and divine protection, through the invocation of your triune name, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; for whoever faithfully and humbly invokes your name shall be saved.

[Note: Up to this point in the book of Charles the Bald; what follows differs.]

Therefore, humbly and faithfully [Col. 0591D] we ask you to erase and forget all our crimes through the intercessions and merits of your saints. Through their merits and prayers, grant that we may be fortified in all things by the help of your protection, that you may cause us to be rescued from eternal damnation and command us to be gathered among their number. Redeemer of our captivity, make us worthy to pray well and to be heard, and hear us with mercy.

## PRAYER

Which the blessed Fathers used to sing in their daily prayers after reciting the names of the saints.

[Note: [Col. 0595D] The prayers that follow under the names of Saints Hilary, Jerome, Pope Gregory, Augustine, Columbanus, and Ephrem are not found in their works. [Col. 0596D] Perhaps they are marked with these names because they were drawn from their writings.]

Through the merits, prayers, intercessions, sufferings, and suffrages of the saints, angels, archangels, patriarchs, prophets, blessed apostles, and all the holy martyrs and confessors, [Col. 0596D] and of the blessed virgins, O merciful Trinity, hear me, free me, defend me, redeem me, protect me, help me, save me, preserve me, enlighten me, and visit me.

Grant me, Lord, a contrite and pure heart that may see you, ponder you, and believe in you; chaste feet that may obediently serve your commandments; and restrained hands, raised to you without anger or vanity, which may labor for the benefit of neighbors and for mercy. Grant, Lord Christ, discerning lips that may bless, magnify, and proclaim you, and may always adore you with fear, trembling, and rejoicing; attentive ears that may hear your name, your law, and your words; humble eyes that may see you; a sense that may perceive you; understanding that may understand you; and a spirit that may always ponder and love you.

May the foot of pride not come upon me, and may the gift of the sinner not move me. May gluttony not dull me, and may fornication not defile me. May vainglory not rule me; may love of money not cover me; may anger not tear me apart; may grief not kill me. May acedia not empty me; may vain boasting not humble me; and may pride not destroy me.

But grant me, merciful Trinity, abstinence and chastity, voluntary poverty and gentleness; generosity, piety, and tranquility; mercy, mildness, forgiveness, humility, kindness, cheerfulness, [Col. 0597B] patience, modesty, sincerity, wisdom, harmony, peace, and charity. Have mercy on me, Lord; have mercy on me. Grant forgiveness for the past, amendment in the present, and protection for the future. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## SUNDAY HYMN

We praise you, O God; we acknowledge you as Lord. The whole earth venerates you, eternal Father. To you all the angels, to you the heavens and all powers; to you the cherubim and seraphim proclaim with unceasing voice:

“Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth. The heavens and the earth are full of the majesty of your glory.”

The glorious choir of the apostles praises you. The praiseworthy number of the prophets praises you. The white-robed army of martyrs praises you. Throughout the world the holy Church confesses you: the Father of immense majesty; your venerable, true, and only-begotten Son; and the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete.

You are the King of glory, Christ. You are the eternal Son of the Father. When you were about to take upon yourself humanity in order to redeem it, you did not disdain the Virgin’s womb. Having overcome the sting of death, you opened the kingdom of heaven to believers. You sit at the right hand of God in the glory of the Father. We believe that you will come to be Judge.

Therefore we beg you: help your servants, whom you redeemed with your precious blood. Grant that they may be numbered with your saints in eternal glory. Save your people, Lord, and bless your inheritance. Govern them and exalt them forever. Each day we bless you, and we praise your name forever and ever. Deign, Lord, to keep us this day without sin. Have mercy on us, Lord; have mercy on us. Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us, just as we have hoped in you. In you, Lord, I have hoped; I shall not be confounded forever.

## PRAYER

God, author and creator of all things, who are known as one in Trinity and three in unity, whose greatness the failing human tongue cannot describe, whom the angels unceasingly proclaim as “holy”: therefore we, your least servants, with unworthy mouths, do not raise up three holy ones but “Holy” three times in our vocal proclamation, so that harmonious melodies may proclaim praise sought from the earth. For this reason we beseech your goodness, most merciful Lord and Father: grant what we ask and forgive what we have done, so that, with our sins wiped away and our conscience pure and free, we may deserve to rejoice in your abundance. Through Christ.

## THE FAITH SET FORTH AT NICAEA BY THREE HUNDRED AND EIGHTEEN BISHOPS

We believe in one God, the almighty Father, maker of all things visible and invisible; and in one Lord, our Jesus Christ, the Son of God, begotten from the Father as the only-begotten—that is, from the substance of the Father: God from God, light from light, true God from true God; begotten, not made, *homoousion* with the Father—that is, of the same substance as the Father—through whom all things were made in heaven and on earth.

For us and for our salvation he descended, took flesh, and became human. He suffered and rose again on the third day. He ascended into heaven and sits at the right hand of God the almighty Father. From there he will come to judge the living and the dead. And in the Holy Spirit.

But those who say that there was once a time when he did not exist, and that he did not exist before he was begotten; and who say that he was made from things that did not subsist, or from another substance or essence; or who say that the Son of God is mutable or subject to change—the Catholic and apostolic Church anathematizes them.

## PRAYER OF SAINT HILARY

Which he appended to the twelve books he wrote about the Holy Trinity.

[Col. 0598C] Holy Trinity, I beg you, preserve the undefiled religious faith of my belief until the departure of my spirit. Grant my conscience this confession: may I always hold what I professed in the symbol of my rebirth, when I was baptized in the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—namely, that I may adore you as our Father, together with you adore your Son, and be found worthy of your Holy Spirit, who is from you through your only-begotten Son; for he is a competent witness to the faith for me, saying: “Father, all that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine.”

[[Note: [Col. 0597D] The words enclosed in brackets are absent from Hilary.] “My God, all that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine.”]

My God Jesus Christ, remaining in you, from you, and with you always as God, who are blessed forever and ever. Amen.

## PRAYER OF SAINT AUGUSTINE, BISHOP

[Col. 0598D] God of justice, I beseech you; God of mercy; invisible God; incomprehensible God; ineffable God; eternal, everlasting, blessed God; God, whose are all things, in whom are all things, under whom are all things, through whom are all things: spare my soul, spare my evils, spare my sins and crimes. Visit the sick, care for the ill, heal the suffering.

Give me a heart that fears you, a sense that understands you, and the eyes of the heart that see you. Give me a spark of your wisdom, which may show me the path of your justifications and teach me to avoid the snares of the enemy. Have mercy on me, because I have sinned, and because of the hardness of my heart I persist in the very death of my sins. I am defiled in mouth, heart, deed, and by every vice; I am covered with every crime. I ask forgiveness because I acknowledge my guilt. I confess my crimes to you; even if I did not confess them, they could not remain hidden from you. For you are the searcher of heart and kidneys; hidden things are manifested to you, and secrets are revealed.

Have mercy on me, Lord; do not allow me to perish; do not permit me to be consumed by eternal darkness and everlasting death. Remove from my heart an alien disposition; heal the stupor of my mind. Uproot from my inward parts the counsels of iniquity. Eradicate from my tongue the habit of slander, the readiness to lie, the vulgarity of speech, and heal all my acts by your art and medicine. Circumcise in me, Lord, the vices of heart and body.

Have mercy on me, God, because you know my deeds. If you had wished to pursue and punish my transgressions according to your judgment, long ago the earth would have swallowed me alive. But because the clemency of your majesty is so great that you allow no one to perish, and because you await all people’s return to repentance, giving them time to repent, grant the one who acts the ability to act, so that this time of your forgiveness, which in your goodness you deign to grant me, may not be in vain.

Have mercy on me, God; do not despise me or turn your face from me. I do not ask your mercy on account of my justice, but because of your clemency look upon me from the seat of your majesty and illumine the darkness of my heart with the ray of your splendor. Protect me, Lord, with the shield of truth and faith, so that the fiery darts of the devil may not pierce me. Whatever it is that my misery either does not dare to ask of you or does not understand how to ask, grant it according to your power; grant what may save my soul from death. As I depart from this enclosure of darkness, stretch out your hand to me and show me the light.

Have mercy on me, Lord; restore what is broken, heal what is corrupted, amend what is defective, and forgive what I have done; grant that I may not do it again. Merciful and compassionate God, who wish to save even barbarians and bring them to knowledge of the truth, I flee to you, Savior of the faithful. Have mercy on me, because I have greatly provoked you, made the enemy rejoice, and behold, I am dead in obeying him.

You, Lord, have mercy on the impious and on those who are without mercy; have mercy on my humility. For nothing is impossible with you, since my soul has been scattered beside hell. Show mercy, because you are kind and merciful toward your creation, you who will raise up bodies that do not exist on the day of resurrection.

Hear me, Lord, because my spirit has failed and my unhappy soul is exhausted. Even my body, which I have defiled, has wasted away; I cannot even live because I did not believe. Forgive my sin through repentance; bring me, the contrite, to life; illumine me with the fire of your splendor and kindle my heart, so that, receiving confidence in your mercy and forgiveness, I may keep your commandments during the remaining time of life that you grant me, and may not depart from your fear, but may serve you more devoutly than I do now.

Therefore spare me and bring me to life, almighty God, Lord Jesus Christ, creator of the universe, the world’s only hope. Grant me first that I may ask you rightly and conduct myself as one worthy of being heard by you. Increase your gifts in me, Lord, so that my soul may love you and become free from every vice of desire.

I ask you, Father; I beseech you, Son; I implore you, Holy Spirit, that I may escape the misery of the world and that you may grant me the everlasting joys of the eternal kingdom. Return now, my God, and do not forget me forever; do not abandon me perpetually, and do not permit me to fall into the power of demons.

Although I lie in offense, you are nevertheless merciful, kind, patient, and greatly compassionate. You abandon no one and despise no one who comes to healing; rather, offering the mercies of your clemency freely, you await sinners so that they may return. For how many criminals, entangled in many disgraces, have reached forgiveness through the grace of your goodness? Just as you freely granted pardon to many who did not deserve it, so may you deign to grant forgiveness to me, unworthy as I am, because of your ineffable mercy, almighty God, who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

## PRAYER OF SAINT GREGORY

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who sit upon the seventh throne, beneath whose feet all things tremble: have mercy on me, who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them.

Have mercy on me, who measured the height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, and the depth of the abyss; who, by your perpetual wisdom, vaulted the heavens and adorned them with stars, and painted the earth with flowers; whom the world cannot contain, yet you rest in a pure heart.

Make my heart undefiled, Lord, who separate day from night, change the tongues of beasts, and give them wisdom; whom various chattering birds recognize with a voice of sweetness, praising their Creator. Glorious are you, Lord, and glorious are your works, you who made what did not exist. You are just, Lord, and just is your judgment; great and wondrous are your works.

Blessed are you above all blessings. God, inseparable Trinity, who are one and not solitary: one divinity, threefold majesty, coequal glory, Alpha and Omega, beginning and end. Our God and King before the ages, you who worked salvation in the midst of the earth. God, who bring the age to its old age, yet do not grow old with the age.

[Col. 0600D] To you I stretch out my hands in the likeness of a cross; before you I humble myself; toward you I shall rise again. May your right hand raise me up, Jesus Christ, who remain in the Father and the Father in you forever. We believe, Lord, in your coming and your resurrection. You rule over us.

Lord, before you examine me, have mercy on me. Heal the wounds of my sins, because I have sinned against you. Cleanse me from my hidden faults, Lord. Enlighten my heart and my understanding with the light of your serenity. May my understanding taste you above all things. Give me understanding, so that I may know your testimonies and keep them in my heart.

Give me your grace, because there is no one who may recover . . . Father of orphans, protector of widows, pardoner of the needy, confessor of penitents: grant me forgiveness, me whom you formed from clay, and thoughts that do not break faith. Teach me to do your will. Whatever you command, help me yourself to fulfill it, so that I may not sin against you again; but give me the desire for every good work.

Lord, in your justice deliver me from my sins, from every evil, from every danger, from every heresy, and from all wicked desires. Establish me in every good work; visit my pains and heal what is not fitting for you; and let what is dark in me receive the name of light. Before you, Lord, is all my desire, and my groaning is not hidden from you.

Give me, Lord, strength against the devil’s snares, and enable me to resist Satan when he incites me. Give me the weapons of virtue and the breastplate of your strength. May no excessive pleasure steal upon me; may no stench of my former corruption defile me. [Col. 0601B] Take from me slippery and useless thoughts and secret suggestions.

God, who can give more than we ask or understand, may my voice move your mercy, you who are one in Trinity and three in unity. Do not destroy me with my sins, because you did not come to save the righteous but to call sinners back to repentance; you are the lover of repentance—have mercy on me.

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, my strength, my foundation, my great and patient liberator and protector, my refuge and power, my helper and deliverer, light of light, fountain of light, sun of justice, star of day, who inhabit the world, whose earth is lofty and heavenly, whose throne is beyond estimation and whose glory is incomprehensible, whom the hosts attend with fear, [Col. 0601C] whose face awakens the abysses and causes the mountains to waste away: hear the prayer of your servant, my God, through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who is the splendor of true light, the gate of life, the way of salvation, the burning lamp, heavenly food, living bread, drink from an everlasting spring, the Word who in the beginning was with God, together with the Holy Spirit, who proceeds from the Father and traverses the circuit of heaven.

What, then, my God, what do I ask, except the Lord God? Supreme, best, most powerful, most merciful, most just, most holy, most present, most beautiful, stable and incomprehensible, immortal; changing all things, never new, never old; renewing all things without age; destroying the proud, who do not know; always acting, always at rest; gathering and needing nothing; carrying and filling; protecting, creating, nourishing, and perfecting; seeking, although nothing is lacking to you.

You love without agitation; you are jealous and secure; you repent and do not grieve; you grow angry and remain tranquil; you change works but do not change your purpose; you receive what you find and have never lost it; you are never needy and rejoice in gains; you are never greedy and demand interest; you overpay as though you owed a debt, although no one possesses anything that is not yours.

You repay lost debts without losing anything; good without quality, great without quantity, Creator without need, holding all things without position, wholly present everywhere without place, eternal without time, making mutable things without any change, and suffering nothing. Hear me, hear me, Lord.

For you are my living and true God, my holy Father, my gracious Lord, my great King, my just Judge, my one Teacher, my timely Helper, my most powerful Physician, my most beautiful Beloved, my living Bread, my eternal Priest. My God, my true light on the way to the homeland; my holy sweetness, my straight way, my splendid wisdom, my pure simplicity, my peaceful harmony, my safe protection, my good portion, my everlasting salvation, my great mercy, my strongest patience, my immaculate victim, my accomplished redemption, my future hope, my perfect charity, my holy resurrection, my eternal life.

I beseech you, implore you, and ask you: let me walk through you, reach you, and rest in you. Hear me, hear me, hear me, Christ, who live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit.

## PRAYER OF SAINT GREGORY THE POPE

I have sinned, Lord, before you; I have sinned also before your angels. Deal with me, your little servant, according to your mercy. To you, Lord, belongs mercy; to you, Lord, belongs justice. Heal me, Lord, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved, because hell will not confess you, nor will death praise you. The living, the living person will confess you, as I do today.

Intercede for me, holy Mary, mother of our Lord Jesus Christ. Most blessed and glorious Mother, help me. Intercede for me, holy Peter, prince of the apostles, and release me from the bonds of my sins. Intercede for me, a sinner, holy Paul, apostle of Christ, chosen vessel. [Col. 0602C] Intercede for me, unworthy, guilty, and sluggish one, holy Andrew. Intercede for my evils, holy James. Intercede for my misdeeds, holy John, beloved of God. Intercede for my sins, holy Philip. Intercede for my sins, holy Bartholomew. Intercede for my infirmities, holy Thomas. Intercede for my offenses, holy Matthew. Intercede for my iniquities, holy James. Intercede for my crimes, holy Thaddeus. Intercede for my transgressions, holy Simon. Intercede for my vanities, holy Matthias.

I beseech you, apostles of Christ, by the remembrance of you, to have mercy on me, your little servant, and help me in every way. I beseech you, nine orders of angels—angels, archangels, virtues, powers, principalities, dominions, thrones, cherubim, and seraphim—to intercede for me, so that Christ, the Son of the living God, may be propitious to me.

I beseech the riches of your goodness, forbearance, and patience, Jesus Christ, Son of God, our Savior: have mercy on me and be propitious to me, a sinner, because you do not desire the death of a sinner but that he should turn and live; nor do you extinguish a smoldering wick, nor break a bruised reed. Make me like one of your hired servants, and from a servant let me become your friend; and let your will be done, as in heaven and on earth.

## PRAYER OF SAINT JEROME, PRIEST

Lord Jesus Christ, who deigned to create me in your image and redeem me with your precious blood; who fashioned my members within my mother’s womb and brought me forth into the light of this life: [Col. 0603A] I pray your most sweet goodness to deign to illumine me with your heavenly light, show me the ways of paradise, and lead me to the harbor of eternal salvation.

Most merciful Lord, deign to kindle within me the fire of your love, which may consume my sins and continually kindle me toward desire for you; and may the Holy Spirit dwell in my heart, teaching me to do your will.

Most loving Lord and Father, soften my hard and stony heart. Grant me compunction of heart, so that with humility, purity of heart, and charity I may pour forth before your clemency abundant tears over the guilt of my sins.

Grant me, Lord, the tears of Mary, who anointed your feet with perfume, drenched them with tears, and wiped them with her hair. Grant me [Col. 0603B] the faith of the thief who, hanging on the cross, confessed you, saying: “Remember me, Lord, when you come into your kingdom” (Luke 23:42); and deserved to hear: “Amen, I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise” (ibid., verse 43).

Grant me, almighty God, that on the day when you command my soul to be separated from my body, I may deserve to hear a merciful sentence, and that the holy angels may lead my soul to the joys of the righteous. But may the wicked angels depart from me in sorrow.

May my prayer be directed to you, Lord, like incense in your presence. Hear, Lord, my voice with which I have cried to you; have mercy on me and hear me. Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.

## THE SAME AUTHOR

[Col. 0603C] Give me, Lord, compunction of heart and tears for my eyes, so that day and night I may mourn all the days of my negligence with humility, purity of heart, and charity. May my prayer draw near in your presence.

If you are angry against me, Lord, whom shall I seek as a helper, or who will have mercy on my infirmities? Remember, Lord, that you called the Canaanite woman and the Publican to repentance, and received Peter when he wept. So may you deign to receive my prayers also, merciful God. Save me, Savior of the world, who reign.

## PRAYER OF SAINT JEROME

I truly believe you, Lord Jesus Christ, and truly confess you, because you truly redeemed us; truly, because you gave us life; truly, because you saved us. You are the stronger Strong One, victor in battle, author of life. You are the resurrection of the dead. We are your vessels; you are our potter.

We ask you, Lord, to fill the empty with your Spirit and preserve what is full. We believe you in the Father; likewise we confess the Father in you; we also venerate the Holy Spirit in both. We worship the triune God in persons, one in the substance of divinity.

Cleanse me, Lord, your vessel, and sanctify what you have made. Empty me of wickedness and fill me with grace. Grant me always to maintain fraternal charity; let me forget evils and not seek what belongs to others. May I always love you alone, the one and true Creator of all creatures, who kill and give life, lead down to the underworld [Col. 0604A] and bring back, remaining forever in Trinity throughout the ages of ages.

## PRAYER OF SAINT MARTIN

God of glory, who are one and true, who alone are just, in whom all things, under whom all things, and through whom all things were made: hear me as I pray, just as you heard the three children from the furnace of blazing fire. Hear me as I pray, just as you heard Jonah from the belly of the whale. Hear me as I pray, just as you heard Susanna and freed her from the hand of wicked witnesses. Hear me as I pray, just as you heard Peter at sea and Paul in chains.

Spare my soul; spare my deeds; spare all our crimes, you who reign with the Father and the Son forever.

## PRAYER OF SAINT COLUMBANUS

[Col. 0604B] Lord God, destroy and uproot whatever the adversary plants in me, so that, once iniquities have been destroyed, you may implant understanding and good work in my mouth and heart; so that in work and will I may serve you alone, understand your commandments, and seek you yourself.

Give me remembrance. Give me charity. Give me chastity. Give me faith. Give me everything that you know to pertain to the usefulness of my soul. Lord, do good in me, and grant me what you know to be necessary, you who reign.

## PRAYER OF SAINT ISIDORE

You, Lord, are the true teacher and giver, advocate and judge, bestower and protector; terrible and merciful, helper and comforter; you give sight to blind minds; you make possible for the weak what you command; you are so kind that you wish to be asked continually, and so generous that you permit no one to despair.

Grant what, with you as giver, we rightly seek; spare us and lead us to that contemplation where we can no longer err. Grant me to do what, inspired by you, I have presumed to say. Grant me to fulfill what I have admonished others to do, so that you who have granted pious speech may also confer approved action upon your servants.

Deliver us, most kind lover of humanity, from that danger, lest, as the Apostle says, while I preach to others I myself may be found rejected. You truly know how weak we are; you recognize by what sort of enemy we are oppressed. The unequal struggle seeks you; mortal weakness calls upon you, because it is the glory of your majesty if the roaring lion is overcome by a weak sheep, if the most violent spirit is conquered by the feeblest flesh.

May the one who fell from heaven be subdued here while you fight on our behalf, so that, although by your permission we suffer his power for a time, we may in no way be swallowed by his insatiable jaws. Make him sad because of human joy, him who rejoices in our offense, Christ Jesus, Savior of the world.

## THE SAME AUTHOR

[Note: [Col. 0603D] From the books of the *Synonyms*.]

With what weeping shall I begin to weep over my evils? With what tears shall I mourn my crimes? With what lamentations shall I bewail my anguish? My sins have taken away my sense of pain.

O tears, where have you withdrawn? Where are you, fountains of tears? Where are you, wave of sorrow? Where are you, lamentations? Where have you fled, weeping? Where have you gone, cries of mourning? [Col. 0605A] Return, I beg you, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Return; come forth and fill my eyes with tears.

Be moved, fountains of tears; sprinkle me with weeping; flow over my face; moisten my cheeks; water my countenance. Give me anxious and bitter mourning. For I, unhappy and miserable, worthy of weeping and pity, the most unhappy and miserable of all, behold my filthiness and acknowledge my guilt.

I know that I am a sinner, and I see how disgraceful I am. I reproach myself as unjust; I accuse myself as impious. I ask you, Lord, to forgive me; I acknowledge my iniquity.

Among all people I have fallen more grievously; among all I have fallen more shamefully; among all I have been more subject to sin; more than the rest I have succumbed to carnal pleasure. I have surpassed all the carnal in the squalor of lust, and by my crime I have overcome the evils of all the impious, so that scarcely could the torments of Tartarus suffice for my evils.

There is no sin beyond my sin; there is no iniquity beyond my iniquity. And now, God of supreme clemency, because I make my offenses known to you and do not hide them from your justice, I beseech your mercy; I implore your mercy. I implore your compassion; I ask your clemency. Blot out my sins; wash away my crimes. Cleanse the stains of my sins; purge the pollution of my crimes; wipe away the filth of my offenses; wash away the defilement of my iniquities.

Do not delay my cleansing, God. I offer my whole self to you to be healed; may my soul receive salvation. Give healing to my wound. God, grant a remedy for my illnesses; after the blows of my wounds, restore me whole.

I am wounded; I seek a physician. I am sick; I ask for a remedy. My flesh has been consumed; my appearance has wasted away. My bones are dried up; my limbs have withered. I have drawn near to corruption; the shadow of death has seized me. Darkness has covered me; the gloom of hell has enveloped me. The horror of darkness has oppressed me.

Teach me to do your will, because you are my God. To you be honor, glory, strength, and power forever and ever. Amen.

## PRAYER OF SAINT ISIDORE
Come to my aid, my God, before death comes, before death destroys me, before Tartarus seizes me, before the flame burns me, before darkness [Col. 0605D] envelops me, before I perish without end. Help me, my God, before the fire of Gehenna devours me, before I am tormented without limit. Woe to me, a wretched man, polluted by every contagion! Woe to me, the worst of all sinners! Woe to me, who have become the cesspool of every crime! Alas for me, who have surpassed the whole magnitude of sins! Alas for me, whose iniquity has exceeded the whole magnitude of transgressions! I beseech you, all you saints: come to the aid of my miseries; mourn my destruction. Weep for me, wretched and outcast. Weep for me, dead and abominable. Weep for me, heaven and earth. Mourn for me, all the elements. Let the whole human race groan for me. Take up lamentation over me; obtain pardon for me with your tears, and pour out prayers for me, the impious one; water the earth with tears [Col. 0606A]. I am full of crimes, full of every vice: I am a vessel of iniquity. The marks of my crimes are recognized throughout all my limbs. There is nothing that I have reserved for righteousness; I have surrendered myself wholly to wickedness. Every vice that I conceived in the flesh I carried out in action. Every crime that I thought of I completed. I brought every evil thought to the effort of completion. This is why, confused among human beings, I cannot raise my eyes to heaven. For I carry disgrace upon my face. I blush at all my actions. The guilt of my conscience bows my face [123]. The shame of my deed is constantly before my eyes. Caught everywhere by my heart, I am confounded: I do not dare look confidently upon anyone. For I have lost faith, defiled piety, polluted holiness, and corrupted religion with vices [Col. 0606B]. I have violated every divine and human law. I have hastened into everything lawful and unlawful. Have mercy on me, Lord; have mercy on me, who reign.

## Prayer of Saint Ephrem the Deacon

Lord God and my Savior, why have you forsaken me? Have mercy on me, for you alone are the lover of all. Save me, a sinner, for you alone are without sin. Rescue me from the mire of my iniquities, so that I may not be stuck there forever. Deliver me from the mouth of my enemy: for behold, like a roaring lion he desires to devour me. Stir up your power and come, that you may save me; flash forth your lightning. Scatter the enemy’s power, most kind lover of humankind. God, I adjure you by your mercies: do not [Col. 0606C] set me with the goats at your left hand, with those who have provoked you. Do not say to me, “I do not know you”; but, because of your great mercy, grant me unceasing contrition of heart and weeping; and sanctify me, so that I may become a temple of your grace, through you, Jesus Christ.

## Prayer for the Whole People, as it is contained in the History of the Kings

Spare, Lord, spare your people, whom you redeemed, Christ, with your blood, so that you may not be angry with us forever. We beseech you, Lord, in all your mercy, that your fury and your anger may be taken away from this place and from your holy house, for we have sinned. We have sinned against you, Lord, and you are angry with us [Col. 0606D], and there is no one who can escape your hands; but we entreat you that your mercy may come upon us, you who spared Nineveh. Let us cry out as we invoke the Lord, that he may look upon the downtrodden and grieving people; may he protect his holy temple, so that it may not be defiled by the impious, but may have mercy on us.

Let us all cry out to the Lord, saying: “We have sinned against you, Lord; be patient with us, and rescue us from these evils, which daily increase against us. Forgive, Lord, the sins of your people, according to the abundance of your mercy, just as you were gracious to our fathers. Be gracious to us, and let your glory fill the whole earth. Remember, Lord; say to the striking angel: ‘It is enough; restrain your hand, and let the slaughter that rages among the people cease, and do not [Col. 0607A] destroy every living soul.’ Rise up, Lord; help us and deliver us for your name’s sake.”

## Prayer of Ephrem the Deacon

Place my tears in your sight, Lord, according to your promise, so that my enemy may turn back and, terrified, be thrown into confusion when he sees me in the place that your mercy has prepared. While the enemy expects to see me in the place that he prepared for me because of my sins, let him see me in the place of light and eternal life; and, turning away into darkness, let him be confounded, because his will has in no way been accomplished.

Thus, most kind one, thus, lover of humankind, thus, you who alone are without sin, pour out upon me your immeasurable and boundless mercy, and [Col. 0607B] grant that both I and those who love you may become heirs of your kingdom; and, seeing your glory, may we adore your goodness; and may we say together, when we have been deemed worthy to see the insatiable beauty of your majesty:

“Glory to the Father, who made us; glory to the Only-Begotten Son, who healed us; glory to the Holy Spirit, who renewed us. Holy Trinity, one God, protect us beneath the shadow of your wings, you who are blessed forever.”

## Prayer for a Prosperous Journey and Voyage

I urgently ask for the swiftest help of God the Father. I implore the aid of Jesus Christ, who was born of the Virgin Mary. May I also always enjoy the protection of the Holy Spirit, here or in exile. May Christ take away from me [Col. 0607C] every danger and every dart of demons. May enemies and robbers not seize me, nor thieves, nor the plunderers of the world. May neither the waves of the sea, nor rivers, nor waters, nor any powers harm me. May neither darkness, nor winds, nor the river, nor sails filled with [Note: [Col. 0607D] The passage is corrupt.] winds, nor favorable sea winds harm me; may I be released from all dangers. May Christ with me conquer the harsh and deadly beasts of land and water; may he conquer the life-giving [F., deadly?] weapons of the air; may he conquer [124] all the flashes of thunder. May he conquer every serpent’s poison; may he conquer the fierce enchantments of the world, so that none of all these things that we have mentioned may harm me or my companions.

May I be safe, my companions safe, and may we proceed unharmed without loss. May our ship be sound amid the waves of the sea, and our horses and sails sound upon the land; may our money be transported safely, so that it may be suitable for our needs [Col. 0607D]. May our enemies not be harmful to us, even though evil plans break forth. In Christ’s eternal name, may all roads be opened fully before me: whether I climb the steep heights of the mountains, whether I descend the hollows of the valleys, whether I travel . . . along the vastest roads of the forests, through the densest thickets, may I proceed along a level and bright road as far as the appointed place . . . .

Lord Jesus Christ, I beseech you by your mercy and clemency to grant me forgiveness for my sins. Open to me the door of life, and let the prince of darkness not meet me. Let not the foot of pride come upon me, and let not a foreign hand touch me; but receive me according to your word [Col. 0608A], and lead me to the banquet of your feasts, where all your friends feast with you. You are Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God, reigning with the Father and the Holy Spirit forever and ever.

## Prayer of Saint Augustine, Which He Appended to the Fifteen Books He Composed on the Holy Trinity

Lord God, we believe in you, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. For Truth would not say, “Go, baptize the nations in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew XXVIII, 20), unless you were Trinity. Nor would you command us, Lord God, to be baptized in the name of one who is not the Lord God. Nor would the divine voice say, “Hear, Israel: the Lord your God [Col. 0608B], the Lord is one” (Deuteronomy VI, 4), unless you were Trinity in such a way that you were one Lord God.

And if you yourself were God the Father, and the Son were your Word, Jesus Christ himself, and the Holy Spirit your gift, we would not read in the writings of truth, “God sent his Son” (Galatians V, 4); nor would you, Only-Begotten, say concerning the Holy Spirit, “The Father will send him in my name, and I will send him to you from the Father” (John III, 17).

Directing my attention toward this rule of faith, insofar as I could, insofar as you enabled me to be able, I sought you and desired, through understanding, to see what I had believed; and I discussed and labored greatly. Lord my God, my one hope, hear me, lest, wearied, I become unwilling to seek you; but let me always seek your face ardently. You give strength for seeking, you who [Col. 0608C] have caused yourself to be found and have given ever greater hope of finding you.

Before you are my strength and my weakness: preserve the one, heal the other. Before you are my knowledge and my ignorance: where you have opened to me, receive me as I enter; where you have closed, open to me as I knock. May I remember you, understand you, and love you. Increase these things in me until you form me completely.

I know that it is written [Augustine: “that it is written”]: “In much speaking you will not escape sin” (Proverbs X, 19). But would that, while preaching your word and praising you, I spoke only what I ought: I would not merely escape sin, but would acquire a good merit; however much you might have deserved, I would speak [Augustine: “however much I might speak in this way”]. For no blessed man would command sin concerning you to his genuine son in faith, to whom he wrote, saying: “Preach the word; be urgent in season and out of season” [Col. 0608D] (II Timothy IV, 2).

Must we say that the one who did not keep silent about your word, Lord, not only in season but also out of season, spoke too much? Yet for that reason it was not “much,” because it was only what was necessary.

Deliver me, my God, from the much speaking that I suffer inwardly in my wretched soul before you, while I flee for refuge to your mercy. For I am not silent in my thoughts, even when I am silent in speech [Augustine: “in my words”]. And if I thought only what pleased you, I would certainly not ask you to free me from this much speaking. But my thoughts are many such as you know human thoughts to be, because they are empty (Psalm XCIII, 11).

Grant me not to consent to them, and, whenever they delight me, nevertheless to reject them, nor to linger in them as though drowsing; and let them not have such power over me that anything from them proceeds into my actions, but, with you protecting me, let my judgment and conscience immediately remain secure from them.

A certain wise man, speaking about you in his book, which is now called Ecclesiasticus by its proper name, says: “We say many things and do not arrive; and the consummation of all discourse is he himself” (Ecclesiasticus XLIII, 29). Therefore, when we have arrived at you, these many things that we say and do not arrive at will cease; and you will remain one, all things in all things [125]. Without end we shall say one thing, praising you as one, and, having ourselves also been made one in you, Lord God, one. [Note: [Col. 0609D] In Augustine, this prayer concludes as follows: “God Trinity, whatever I have said about you in these books, let your people acknowledge as their own; whatever is from me, may you and your people forgive.”] God Trinity, forgive me [Col. 0609B] all my sins, preserve me in the integrity of this faith and in the perfection of good works, free me from all the snares of the devil and of human beings, and protect me beneath the shadow of your wings, you who are blessed forever.

## Hymn of Blessed Bishop Sedulius [Note: [Col. 0609D] This hymn is published in volume VI of the Lyons edition of the Library of the Fathers, p. 471, under the following title: “The hymn of Coelius Sedulius [Col. 0610D] the presbyter, in acrostics, containing the whole life of Christ.” From there we have taken the variant readings. Let the reader note that the initial letters of the stanzas of this poem reproduce the entire alphabet.], on the Birth, Baptism, Power, Betrayal, Passion, Resurrection, and Ascension of Our Lord Jesus Christ

From the rising of the sun’s pivot,

to the farthest boundary of the earth,

let us sing Christ the ruler,

born of the Virgin Mary.

The blessed author of the world

put on a servant’s body,

so that, by freeing flesh through flesh,

he might not lose those whom he had created.

The closed womb of the mother

is entered by heavenly grace;

the maiden’s womb bears

secrets that she had not known.

The house of the chaste body [Al., breast]

suddenly becomes God’s temple:

untouched, knowing no man,

she conceived the Son by the Word.

The woman in childbirth brought forth him

whom Gabriel had foretold,

whom John, enclosed within his mother’s womb,

had sensed while leaping.

He endured lying upon hay;

he did not shrink from the manger;

and he was fed with a little milk—

he through whom not even a bird hungers.

The choir of the heavenly beings rejoices,

and the angels sing to God;

and the Shepherd, Creator of all,

is made known openly to the shepherds.

Impious enemy Herod,

why do you fear Christ’s coming?

He does not seize mortal kingdoms,

who gives heavenly realms.

The Magi went by the way they had come [Al., which they had seen],

following the guiding star.

They seek the light through a gift [Al., with light];

through the gift they confess God.

The throng of mothers resounds,

mourning their slaughtered children;

the tyrant consecrated

thousands of them as victims to Christ [Al., as a victim].

The heavenly Lamb touched

the baths of pure water;

by washing away the sins

that he had not brought with him,

he removed them from us.

He gave faith in his miracles,

to have the Father [Al., to show himself to be God the Father],

healing weakened bodies

and raising corpses [Al., resurrecting them].

A new kind of power:

the water jars redden [Al., the waters redden];

and the wave, commanded to pour forth wine,

changed its nature.

The centurion, kneeling,

prays for the servant’s salvation;

the abundance of the believer’s fervor

extinguished the fires of fever.

Peter walks upon the waves [Al., walking],

lifted up by Christ’s right hand [Al., Christ’s right hand lifts him];

the path that nature had denied

faith prepared.

On the fourth day, already stinking,

Lazarus received life;

freed from the bonds of death,

he became a survivor of himself [Al., and became free from all bonds].

A garment touched

stops streams of hot blood [Al., horrid blood];

by the weeping of the suppliant,

which waters it [Al., while the suppliant’s weeping waters it],

the flow of blood was halted [Al., the flowing blood dries up].

Freed from every sickness [Al., from every bodily ailment],

commanded suddenly to rise,

the sick man carried his bed

again on his own feet.

Then that Judas, the executioner,

dared to betray the Master;

he offered peace with a kiss,

which he did not possess in his heart.

The truthful one is handed over to the deceitful;

the impious man scourges the pious;

the innocent one, fixed to the cross,

is joined to robbers [Al., is joined to them].

After the Sabbath, certain female companions were carrying myrrh to Xyro [Al., Xero; perhaps read Xro, that is, “Christ”]; [Al., corpori, “to the body”] an angel addressed them:

“A living man is not enclosed by a tomb” [Al., “the living one is not enclosed in a tomb”].

Come, let us all sing

with sweet hymns

of Christ’s triumph over Tartarus,

who redeemed us when we had been sold [Al., who redeemed you when you had been sold].

The envy of the jealous dragon

and the mouth of the worst lion,

the only-begotten one of God trampled,

he who restored himself to the heavens [Al., and restored himself to the heavens].

Glory to the unbegotten Father,

glory to the Only-Begotten,

together with the Holy Spirit,

through everlasting ages.

## Prayer

Grant, Lord, that readers may make progress, and that those seeking your law may receive remission of all sins, so that we who greatly desire to reach the light of your Scriptures may not be darkened by any sins that obscure us. Draw us to yourself by the power of your omnipotence. Do not abandon to their own will those whom you redeemed with precious blood. Do not allow your image in us to be obscured; if it is defended by your aid, neither the devil nor we ourselves may overturn your gifts, because everything is fragile that attempts to oppose you.

Hear [Col. 0611C] us, merciful King, against our sins; and first remove them from us, before you can justly condemn us because of them in your judgment. Why does our own iniquity lie in wait for us? Why do our sins battle against us? They desire to overthrow your creature, though they themselves possess no substantial firmness [lacuna] the devil—why does he pursue us with insatiable pain? Did we give him counsel so that he might become proud against you, his Lord, and fall from the blessedness bestowed on him, when he possessed such great marks of power through you? Let it be enough that he struck us in Adam [Col. 0612A]; why does the impious accuser pursue us with daily deceptions?

And just as he does not cease to attack our frailty, so may he, confounded by your powers, depart. Do not permit, good King, the fiercest enemy to accomplish his wishes in us, he who chooses gravely to offend you. Why does he circle us like a roaring lion? Why does he strive to devour us? Once, in holy baptism, we renounced him; once, we professed that we believed in you, Lord.
