for the sailor in the shipwrecked world—

you, whom the sacred blood

poured from the Lamb’s body anointed.

### Also, another hymn of that same Fortunatus on the cross of our Savior Jesus Christ

The banners of the King advance;

the mystery of the cross shines forth,

upon which the Creator of flesh,

having taken flesh, was suspended on the gallows.

With his inward parts fastened by nails,

his hands and feet extended [Col. 1389C],

he was sacrificed here as the victim

for the sake of redemption.

Moreover, wounded

by the terrible point of the spear,

he poured forth water and blood

to wash us from sin.

What David sang

in faithful song has been fulfilled,

when he said to the nations:

“God reigned from the wood.”

Beautiful and radiant tree,

adorned with the King’s purple,

chosen as worthy wood

to touch such holy limbs.

Blessed is the tree from whose arms

the price of the world *(alternative: age)* hung;

it became the scales of his body

and carried off the prey of Tartarus.

[Col. 1389D]

You pour forth fragrance from your bark;

you surpass honey in sweetness;

give place to fruitful produce;

clap your hands in noble triumph.

Hail, altar; hail, victim,

of the glory of the Passion,

through which life endured death

and by death restored life.

### Prayer for our relatives and for all faithful departed

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, we humbly beseech you for the spirits of your male and female servants N., whom from the beginning of this age you commanded to be summoned to you: deign, Lord, to give them a place of light, a place of refreshment and rest; grant that they may pass through the gates of hell and the ways of darkness, and may remain in the dwelling places of the saints and in the holy light which you once promised to Abraham and his seed.

Let their souls suffer no harm [Col. 1390A]. When that great day of resurrection and recompense has come, deign, Lord, to raise them again together with your saints and elect, and wipe away their offenses and sins down to the last farthing, so that together with you they may obtain the life of immortality and the eternal kingdom through eternal rest. And the rest. “Do not hand them over to the beasts.” And the rest. “The souls of the righteous.” And the rest.

### Prayer for any faithful departed person

Almighty and merciful God, we beseech your kindness, because by your judgment we are either born or brought to an end: receive into eternal rest the soul of our brother N., whom your compassion has commanded to pass from the habitation of this world, and permit it to be joined in the resurrection to the company of your elect, so that in eternal blessedness it may remain with them without end, through the soul which you redeemed.

Receive, Lord, together with your servants him who confessed you in the common life, and establish him in everlasting life. Through, and so forth.

### Prayer for the departed

[Col. 1390B]

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant N. from the dangers of hell, from the dangers of darkness, from many persecutions, and from the fires of the flames of Gehenna.

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant N., as you delivered Noah through the flood of the ages.

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant N., as you delivered Abraham from Ur of the Chaldeans.

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant N., as you delivered Lot from the city of the Sodomites.

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant N., as you delivered the people of Israel from the hand of the Egyptians.

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant N., as you delivered Moses from the hand of Pharaoh, who went before the people of Israel in the wilderness.

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant N., as you delivered David from the hand of the giant Goliath.

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant N., as you delivered Elijah and Enoch from this world.

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant N., as you delivered Susanna from the hand of the rulers.

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered Daniel [Col. 1390C] from the lions’ den.

Deliver, Lord, the soul of your servant N., as you delivered Jonah from the belly of the whale.

Thus may you deign to deliver the soul of our brother N. from all dangers of punishments, and command that it enjoy eternal goods with your elect.

Through. “In everlasting memory he shall be.” And the rest. “Eternal rest.” May he obtain a share in the first resurrection and be deemed worthy of eternal life. Amen.

### In the name of God, from the book of the blessed apostles, martyrs, confessors, and virgins which the blessed Jerome composed concerning their anniversaries throughout the cycle of the year

Here begin the names which, as has been handed down by the holy fathers, are to be read daily.

Have mercy on us wretched ones, merciful holy Trinity, and forgive all the sins we have committed before your angels in your sight, through the merits, prayers, intercessions, and invocations of all your saints, whose feast is celebrated today [Col. 1390D]—N. and those whose names we now recite.

Deliver us, merciful Trinity, together with all our brothers and sisters, from every past, present, and future evil: from death to life, from darkness to light, from hell to paradise, from evil to good, from ignorance to knowledge, from sins to true repentance, from every vice to perfect virtues, and from all the snares of the enemy to heavenly medicine.

Grant us divine protection through the invocation of your threefold name, of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, because whoever faithfully and humbly invokes you will be saved.

Therefore we humbly and faithfully ask you to erase and forget all our wicked deeds through the intercessions and merits of all your saints.

Angels, archangels, virtues, powers, principalities, dominions, thrones, cherubim, seraphim, patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs, confessors, holy bishops, holy presbyters, holy deacons, and all [Col. 1391A] holy members of the Church, anchorites, hermits, monks, holy virgins, holy widows, holy wise women, and all the saints who have gone before us from Adam to the present day: pray for us.

Holy Mary, pray for us. Holy Mary, intercede for me, a sinner. Holy Mary, help me at the hour of my departure. Holy Michael, pray for us. Holy Gabriel, pray. [Col. 1391B] Holy Raphael, pray. Be gracious, spare us, Lord. Be gracious, deliver us, Lord. From every evil, deliver us. From every temptation, deliver us. From every evil thought, deliver us. From every iniquity, deliver us. From every impurity of heart and body, deliver us. From every poverty and hunger, deliver us. From every tribulation, deliver us. From the danger of death, deliver us. From the snares of the devil, deliver us. From everlasting death, deliver us. From every evil desire, deliver us. From sudden and unforeseen death, deliver us. From every scandal, deliver us. [Col. 1394C] From every adversity, deliver us. By your cross, deliver us.

We sinners, we beg you, hear us. That you would graciously grant us peace, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously grant us forgiveness of our offenses, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously grant us remission of all our sins, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously grant us the intercession of all your saints, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously pour the grace of the Holy Spirit into our hearts, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously grant us your holy charity, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously grant us right faith, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously grant us firm hope in your goodness, Lord Jesus, we beg you. [Col. 1394D] That you would graciously grant us eternal life, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously grant us perpetual light, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously grant us praise of your holy name, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would grant us to perform true repentance, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously deliver us from everlasting death, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would remove plague and pestilence from our land, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would graciously bestow your mercy upon us, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would grant us abundance of crops, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would grant us health, Lord Jesus, we beg you. That you would grant us calm skies, we beg you. That you would grant us seasonable rain, we beg you. [Col. 1395A] That you would graciously preserve the entire Christian people, redeemed by your precious blood, we beg you. That you would graciously preserve all our spiritual brothers in the true religion, we beg you. That you would graciously grant perpetual peace to our elders, foreordained by God, we beg you. That you would graciously have mercy on those people who have been commended to our prayers, we beg you. That you would graciously have mercy on all the souls of Catholic Christians, Son of God, we beg you.

Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us. Christ, hear us. Kyrie, have mercy.

### Prayer of a certain wise man

Through the merits, prayers, intercessions, sufferings, and suffrages of all these holy martyrs and confessors and blessed virgins, most merciful Trinity, hear me, deliver me, defend me, redeem me, protect me, help me, save me, preserve me, enlighten me. [Col. 1395B] Grant me, Lord, a contrite and pure heart that may see you, think of you, and believe in you; and chaste feet that may obediently minister according to your commandments; and self-controlled hands, lifted to you without anger or vanity, which may labor for the benefit and mercy of my neighbors.

Grant, Lord Christ, discerning lips that may bless you, magnify you, and proclaim you, and that may always adore you with fear, trembling, and rejoicing; attentive ears that may hear your name, your law, and your words; humble eyes that may see you; a faculty that may sense you; an understanding that may understand you; and a soul that may always think of you and love you. Let the foot of pride not come against me, and let the hand of the sinner not move me.

Let gluttony not dwell in me; let fornication not defile me; let vainglory not rule me; let avarice not overwhelm me; let anger not tear me apart; let sadness not kill me; let sloth be emptied out; let the desire for empty glory not humble me; and let pride not destroy me. Rather, gracious Trinity, grant me abstinence and chastity, voluntary poverty, gentleness, generosity, piety, tranquility, mercy, mildness, indulgence, humility, kindness, cheerfulness, patience, moderation, and sincerity. Have mercy on me, Lord; have mercy on me.

Grant me forgiveness for past crimes, correction for present ones, and protection from future ones. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who with you …

### Prayer of Saint Augustine, which he appended to the fifteen books he composed on the Holy Trinity

Lord our God, we believe in you as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. For Truth would not have said to the apostles, “Go, baptize the nations in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,” unless you were Trinity. Nor would you have commanded us, Lord God, to be baptized in that name, unless the Trinity were Lord God. Nor would the divine voice have said, “Hear, Israel: the Lord your God is one Lord,” unless you were Trinity in such a way that you were one Lord God—unless you, God the Father, were yourself he; and the Son, your Word, Jesus Christ, were himself he; and your gift, the Holy Spirit.

We would not read in the writings of Truth, “God sent his Son,” nor would you, Only-Begotten, say of the Holy Spirit, “Whom the Father will send in my name,” and, “Whom I will send to you from the Father.” Directing my intention toward this rule of faith, as much as I could and as much as you made me able, I sought you, and desired by understanding to see what I believed, and I argued and labored greatly. Lord God, my only hope, hear me, lest, wearied, I become unwilling to seek you; but let me always seek your face ardently.

You give ways to the one who seeks, you who have made yourself discoverable, and you have given ever greater hope of finding you. Before you are my strength and my weakness: preserve the one, heal the other. Before you are my knowledge and my ignorance. [Col. 1396A] Where you have opened to me, receive me as I enter. Where you have closed, open to me as I knock. May I remember you, understand you, and love you. Increase these things in me until you form me whole.

I know it is written: “In much speaking you will not escape sin.” But would that, by proclaiming your word and praising you, I spoke only of you—not merely escaping sin, but also acquiring as much good merit as possible. Thus would I speak; for a blessed person would not receive sin from speaking of you. [Note: [Col. 1395D] The passage is defective.] He wrote to his true son in the faith, saying: “Preach the word; be urgent in season and out of season.” Should we say that this man did not speak much, who not only in season but also out of season did not keep silent about your word, Lord? Yet for that reason it was not much, because it was only what was necessary.

Deliver me, God, from the much speaking that I suffer inwardly in my miserable soul before you, as I flee to your mercy. For I am not silent in my thoughts even when I am silent in speech. And indeed, if I thought only what pleased you, I would not ask you to deliver me from this much speaking; but my thoughts are many, such as you know human thoughts to be, since they are vain.

Grant me not to consent to them; and, whenever they delight me, nevertheless to condemn them, not to linger in them as though drowsing, and not to let them have such power over me that anything from them proceeds into my actions. At least let my judgment concerning them be safe, and my conscience safe under your protection.

A certain wise man, speaking of you in his book—which he himself calls *Ecclesiasticus*—said: “We say many things, and do not arrive; and the sum of all speech is he himself.” When, therefore, we have arrived at you, these many things that we say and do not arrive at will cease, and you will remain one, all things in all things; and without end we shall say one thing, praising you as one, and, made one in you, we too shall be one.

Lord God, one God in Trinity, whatever I have said in these books that is yours, let your own recognize as yours; but if anything is my own, may you and yours forgive me.

### Here begins a prayer of Saint Prudentius

[Col. 1396C]

O God, parent of all, giver of the soul, O Christ God,

from whose mouth the one Spirit, God, subsists.

With you guiding me, I am ruled; with you as prince, I lead my life.

With you as judge, pale with fear I tremble; with you as that same judge,

I take hope that whatever I do may be pardonable before you,

however unworthy of pardon I may be, whatever I may do or say.

I confess; willingly forgive and spare the one who confesses.

I have deserved every evil, but you, good judge, take away

what I have deserved, and favorably bestow better things on the one who prays.

Grant to my soul, when at last it leaves the lodging

of this body, built of sinews, skin, blood, bile,

and bones—material which, corrupted by luxury, its inhabitant cherishes in too close an embrace—that, when the mournful hour

has closed these eyes and the trampled [F.: trampled upon] material lies there,

and the mind, stripped bare, enjoys its own eyes,

that it may not see some savage one from the race of brigands,

cruel, swift, threatening in face and voice,

terrible, who might drag me, stained with the sprinkling of my morals,

[Col. 1396D] headlong, like a robber, as I fall,

and plunge me into black caves,

exacting everything down to the smallest quarter.

Many is the dwelling in the Father’s treasures, Christ,

set apart in unequal places. Now I ask for a blessed home

in that region: let there be there chaste companies of men

who disdain the valuation of dust.

May your true riches always be there; may ever-flowering

virginity be bright, its mind cut off and chastened. [Note: [Col. 1396D] The passage is corrupt.]

But for me it is enough if no face of the Tartarean minister

should meet me, and if the greedy flame of Gehenna

does not devour this soul plunged into the deepest furnaces,

since, because of sin, it is necessary that in this way

the sad corporeal fire of Avernus consume me.

At least may the slow fires breathe forth

soothing vapors, and may the heat grow mild as its fervor fades.

[Col. 1397A] May immense light glorify others, and times bound with crowns;

may gentle, light punishment burn me.

### Prayer of Bishop Eugenius

Immense God, King, by whom the structure of the world endures,

what I, a wretched servant, ask, mercifully accomplish.

Let me have right faith, opposed to false sects.

Let me have, above all, present correction of morals.

Let me be dear, humble, truthful, present in due season.

Silent about secrets, and cautious in the speech of my tongue.

Give me a faithful companion; give me a steadfast friend always.

Give me a gentle, sober, frugal, and chaste servant.

Let poverty not torment me, nor sickness cripple me.

Let blessed health and sufficient nourishment accompany me.

Let riches, arrogance, and quarrels of strife be absent,

as well as envy, luxury, and the shameful levy of the belly.

May I injure no one by crime, nor be injured by crime.

Thus may I be able to wish what is good, so that the power to do wrong may withdraw.

May I never desire, do, or utter anything shameful.

May my mind desire you, my tongue sing of you, and my action proclaim you.

[Col. 1397B] Grant, Father who thunder on high, a billowing rain of tears,

by which I may be able to dissolve the burdens of my sins.

Grant, I pray, help by which I may conquer the world,

and traverse the course of life with peaceful step.

And when the final day has opened the urn of death,

grant forgiveness to him whose guilt removes his crown.

### Prayer of the priest Bede

O eternal God, the world’s one hope of life,

grant me firm aid in so great a crisis,

lest weak flesh succumb to powerful tyrants.

Remember me as like ashes, wind, and shadow;

but by the covering of your compassion, which shines forever from eternity,

you, coming from on high, clothe yourself in flesh,

so that flesh might overcome the airy blasts.

If battles roar and the hostile trumpet condemns,

under your leadership, trusting in you, may easy victory enrich me,

so that, free, with you protecting me from deep snares,

I may flourish, great King, through the heights of your temple.

For our love thirsts for your courts, [F.: our love / our lover],

sweet ornament, where it may hear sweet songs

of praise from the angels.

### Also by the same author

Faithful, remaining alone as salvation for the wretched in the world,

protect your servant from death, great King.

If she alone makes ready against countless weapons,

and, as the beauty of grass, so my life flees,

may yours always snatch [object uncertain in the source] from the mouth of deceit.

With a two-edged sword you strike the savage serpent,

and the wandering camps of the ancient standard-bearing God;

and the harsh soldier summons his men to bloody arms.

No water-snake (*hydros*) troubles breasts bound to you.

May I deserve, enthroned on high, to approach the ways of light,

and, exalted, to stand among the sacred choirs above.

May the joyful dwelling glorify [object uncertain in the source] through the fields,

and may David’s sacred melody resound from his mouth.

### Prayer of Saint Augustine

God, creator of the universe, grant me first that I may ask you rightly, [Col. 1397D] then that you may make me one whom you will deliver, and afterward that you may deliver me.

God, by whom faith awakens us, hope raises us, and charity joins us; God, through whom we conquer the enemy; I beseech you, God, through whom we receive the means not to perish altogether. God, by whom we are admonished to keep watch; God, through whom we hope for good things from evil ones; God, through whom we flee evils and pursue good things; God, through whom we are not harmed by adversities; God, through whom we serve well and rule well; God, through whom we say that things we once thought ours are alien, and things we once thought alien are ours: hear me, hear me, hear me, my God, my Lord, my King, my Father, my cause, my possession, my honor, my house, my homeland, my salvation, my light, my life. Hear me, hear me, hear me, Lord, in that manner of yours known to few.

Now I love you alone, follow you alone, seek you alone, and am ready to serve you alone, because you alone rule justly. I desire to belong to you. Command, I beg you, and order whatever you wish. [Col. 1398A] But heal and open my ears, with which I may hear your voice; heal and open my eyes, with which I may see your signs. Let your door be opened to me as I knock.

Teach me how one reaches you. You possess nothing except the will; I know nothing except that passing and perishable things must be rejected, and sure and eternal things sought. I do this, Father, because this alone I know, but I do not know how one reaches you. Suggest it to me; show it to me; provide me with provisions for the journey.

If those who flee to you find you through faith, give me faith; if through virtue, virtue; if through knowledge, knowledge. Increase hope in me; increase faith; increase charity.

Holy Peter, intercede for my sins. Holy Paul, intercede for my weaknesses. Holy Andrew, intercede for my offenses. Holy James, intercede for my evils. Holy John, lover of the Lord, intercede for my most wretched deeds. Holy Philip, intercede for my vain thoughts. Holy Bartholomew, intercede for my crimes. Holy Matthew, intercede for my iniquities. [Col. 1398B] Holy Thomas, intercede for my offenses. Holy James, intercede for my wicked deeds. Holy Thaddeus, intercede for my transgressions. Holy Simon, intercede for all my vanities. Holy Matthias, intercede for my hidden faults.

I beseech you, all apostles of Christ, by the remembrance of you, to have mercy on me, your servant, and to help me with your aid in every necessity.

I ask the nine orders of angels—the angels, archangels, virtues, principalities, powers, dominations, thrones, cherubim, and seraphim—to intercede for me, so that Christ, the Son of the living God, may be propitious to me, and that I may deserve to obtain his mercy here and in the future.

I beseech the riches of your goodness, your forbearance, and your patience, Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, Savior and Redeemer of the world: be propitious to me, a sinner. You do not desire the death of a sinner, but that he should turn and live. You will not extinguish the smoking flax, nor break the bruised reed. Make me like one of your hired servants, [Col. 1398C] so that from being a servant I may become your friend, and may your will be done, as in heaven so on earth.

Grant me, Lord, compunction of heart and tears, so that day and night I may weep over all the days of my negligence, with humility, purity of heart, and charity. Let my prayer draw near in your sight, Lord. If you are angry against me, Lord, whom shall I seek as helper, or who will have mercy on my weaknesses?

Remember that you called the Canaanite woman and the publican to repentance, and received the weeping Peter. Most merciful Father, receive my prayers also in this way, merciful God, and save me, Savior of the world, who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

### Also by the same author

Save me, Lord, King of eternal glory, who alone can save. Grant me both the will and the action and the completion of what pleases you and is beneficial to me. Grant help in disturbance and tribulation, comfort in persecution, and strength in every time of temptation. Deign to grant me forgiveness for past evils, correction of present vices, and protection from future sins.

God, who foreknow the future and see things that have passed as though they were present, Lord, deign to open the eyes of my heart and make my soul acceptable to you, so that your love may always inflame my breast, my conversation with you may be throughout the day, and I may recognize your visitation at night. For your utterances are sweet, Lord, in my mouth. Receive my spirit into your perpetual peace.

I invoke you, Lord, whom all the choirs of the saints attend and glorify with fear and trembling. Do not abandon my soul, so that the one whom you have confounded in your desire may not dominate it. I invoke you, enlightener, savior, and redeemer of human beings. I cry to you; hear me, Lord, and loose the bonds of my sins in which I am held bound— you who, with the Father, and so forth.

### Also from the foregoing

[Col. 1399A]

My Lord and my God, who have no lord, but all things are subject to your creation: do not despise me, your unworthy servant, but, counting me among your faithful servants, make me rejoice before the sight of your glory.

For you said: “I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.” And again: “I do not desire the death of a sinner, but that he should turn and live.” I, with you, Lord, inspiring me, wish to turn; fulfill my desire for good, and grant forgiveness for past offenses, protection from future vices, and correction of present crimes, so that I may live.

May I advance toward you, the pious Lord and the sweetness of immeasurable compassion, and reach you, who for the human race deigned to descend to earth, and, pouring out your precious blood, called the nations to the grace of baptism and freed them from pagan error.

Wretched that I am, I have never kept what I promised in baptism. I therefore repent of having done what I wickedly did. Receive the tears of one who repents; have mercy, merciful one, and forgive what I have done, and grant that I may not do it again.

Look, Lord, upon my dangers in which I stand, and upon the evils by which I am surrounded, and upon the many adversities with which, through my own merit, I am shaken. Deliver me, save me, protect me, and defend me, so that my enemies may not laugh at me, because you are my God.

You are my only hope; in you alone I trust. I hope for comfort from no human being. Govern me like a merciful father, so that after so many and such storms of the world raging on every side, under your guidance I may deserve to reach the harbor of eternal salvation and, with the others whom you have rescued, praise you, my Lord, throughout infinite ages of ages. Amen.

### Prayer to the Father

Lord God, almighty Father, who ineffably begot before all ages the consubstantial and coeternal Son, who with him and with your Holy Spirit, proceeding from you and from that same Son, created all things visible and invisible: I adore you, I praise you, and I glorify you. [Col. 1399C] Be gracious, I beg you, to me, a sinner, and do not despise me, the work of your hands; rather save me and help me for the sake of your holy name.

### Prayer to the person of the Son

Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who are true and almighty God, splendor and image of the Father, and eternal life, with whom the Father and the Holy Spirit have one substance, equal honor, the same glory, and coeternal majesty: I adore you, I praise you, and I glorify you. I beg you, do not allow me to perish; rather save me and help me by your gratuitous gift, me whom you deigned to redeem with your precious blood.

### Prayer to the person of the Spirit

Holy Spirit, Lord God almighty, who, being coequal, coeternal, and consubstantial with the Father and the Son, proceed ineffably from them; who descended upon the same Lord Jesus Christ in the form of a dove and upon the holy apostles in fiery tongues: [Col. 1399D] I adore you, I praise you, and I glorify you. Drive away from me, I beg you, the darkness of all iniquity and faithlessness; kindle in me the light of your mercy and the fire of your most holy and most sweet love.

### Prayer to the most holy and undivided Trinity

Almighty, eternal, ineffable Lord God, without end or beginning, whom we confess as one in Trinity and threefold in Unity: you alone I adore, you I praise, you I glorify, and to you, merciful and compassionate, I render thanks, because you have granted me, stripped of the night of faithlessness and error, to become a participant in your grace.

Complete in me, I beg you, Lord, the work of your mercy begun in me. Grant me always to think, speak, and do what is pleasing to you; and, guarding me everywhere by your gratuitous compassion, make me, unworthy and wretched as I am, reach your vision, you who are one.

### Prayer to the Lord Jesus Christ

[Col. 1400A]

Lord Jesus Christ, king of virgins, lover of integrity, cleanse my heart from all the arrows and snares of the enemy, and extinguish in me every fire of lust. Grant true humility, tranquility, and patience to my breast. Kindle my mind with the goads of your charity, so that, hating every way of iniquity, I may be pleasing to you throughout all the days of my life, you who with the Father …

### Prayer to Saint Mary

Mary, of singular merit, the one mother and virgin without equal, whom the Lord guarded inviolate in mind and body, so that you might be worthy to be the one from whom the Son of God fashioned for himself a body, the price of our redemption: I beseech you, most merciful Lady, through whom the whole world has been saved, intercede for me, most filthy and most defiled by every iniquity, so that although, because of my iniquities, I deserve nothing but to undergo the punishment of eternal damnation, yet, saved by your merits, most radiant Virgin, I may obtain the everlasting kingdom. [Col. 1400B] Through the Lord.

### Prayer to the holy apostles

Most holy apostles of my Lord Jesus Christ—most blessed Peter, Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon, Thaddeus, Matthias, Barnabas, Luke, and Mark—with all the disciples of my Lord Jesus Christ, pray for me, so that the Lord may draw me away from the world as he drew you away from it, and grant me to follow his footsteps, even at the end of your procession.

### Prayer to the venerable Benedict

I beseech you, most blessed Benedict, beloved of God: intercede for your servant … and for all this your holy congregation, and for all who serve under your rule, and likewise for the whole Christian people. Intercede also for me, your wretched servant, so that the Lord may cleanse my heart, my mouth, and my actions from every [Col. 1400C] vice. May he grant me to keep all that he commanded and to observe the path of your holy rule, which I promised I would keep.

### Prayer to several confessors

I beseech you, most blessed confessors and teachers of Christ—Cyprian, Basil, Gregory, Athanasius, Eusebius, Ambrose, Martin, Augustine, Jerome, Germanus, Leo, John, and Isidore—deign to intercede for me, a sinner, so that the Lord may grant me to keep what you taught and make me rejoice in your fellowship.

### Prayer of Pope Gregory

Sovereign Lord, almighty God, who are one Trinity: the Father in the Son, and the Son in the Father, together with the Holy Spirit; who are always in all things, were before all things, and will be through all things, blessed God forever. Amen.

I commend my soul into the hands of your power, so that you may guard it day and night, at every hour and moment. Have mercy on me, God of the angels. Guard me through the prayers of the patriarchs, through the merits of the prophets, through the suffrages of the apostles, through the victories of the martyrs, and through the faith of the confessors who pleased you from the beginning of the world.

May holy Abel pray for me, who was first crowned through martyrdom. May holy Enoch pray for me, who walked with God and was taken from the world. May holy Noah pray for me, whom the Lord preserved in the flood because of his righteousness. May faithful Abraham plead for me, who first believed God, and whose faith was reckoned as righteousness. May holy Isaac intercede for me, who was righteous and obedient to his father unto death, as an example of my Lord Jesus Christ, who was offered to the Father for the salvation of the world.

May blessed Jacob petition for me, who saw the angels of God coming to his aid. May blessed Moses pray for me, with whom the Lord spoke face to face. May holy David, whom you chose, Lord, according to your heart, come to my aid. May the prophet Elijah plead for me, whom you raised to heaven in a fiery chariot. [Col. 1401A] May the prophet Elisha pray for me, who raised a dead boy after his own death. May holy Isaiah pray for me, whose lips were cleansed by heavenly fire. May blessed Jeremiah assist me, whom you sanctified, Lord, in his mother’s womb. May the holy prophet Ezekiel pray for me, who saw wondrous visions. May the chosen Daniel, beloved of God, be entreated for me, who interpreted the king’s dreams and was twice delivered from the lions’ den.

May the three youths whom you delivered from the fire come to my aid. And may the twelve prophets—Hosea, Joel, Amos, Obadiah, Habakkuk, Micah, Jonah, Nahum, Zephaniah, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi, and Ezra—assist me. I invoke all these for my help.

May all the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ—Peter and Paul, Andrew and John, the two Jameses, Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew, Barnabas and Matthias—and all the martyrs and all your saints, Lord, intercede for me.

Drive from me, Lord, the desire for gluttony, and give me the virtue of abstinence. Flee from me, spirit of fornication, and give me the ardor of chastity. Extinguish greed in me, and give me voluntary poverty. Restrain my anger, and kindle in me profound sweetness of soul and love of God and neighbor. Withdraw from me, Lord, desire for this world, and give me voluntary poverty. Cut away from me, Lord, worldly sadness, and increase spiritual joy in me. Expel the boastfulness of my mind, and grant me compunction of heart. Lessen my pride, and perfect true humility in me, because I am an unworthy and wretched man. Who will deliver me from this body of death, except the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ? For I am a sinner, and my offenses are innumerable, and I am not worthy to be called your servant.

Awaken weeping in me; soften my hard and stony heart; kindle in me the fire of fear and love of you, though I am the ashes of death. Deliver my soul from all the snares of the enemy, and preserve me in your will. Teach [Col. 1401C] me to do your will, because you are my God; to you belong honor and glory throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

### Another prayer

Christ, spare me and have mercy on me, not according to my merits but according to your great mercy. I beseech your goodness: do not despise a sinner; do not reject me, but receive me according to your word, and I shall live, and do not put me to shame in my expectation.

Have mercy on me, Lord, because I have sinned against you. Grant me a fountain of tears, fountain of life and light of light. Grant me in the present life true repentance for my sins and perseverance in good.

Lord, hear my prayer, you who live and reign, God, forever and ever. Amen.

### Another prayer.

God, compassionate and merciful, who also will to save the barbarians and bring them to knowledge of your truth, to you [Col. 1401D], the Savior of the faithful, I flee for refuge. Have mercy on me, because I have greatly provoked you and, agreeing with the enemy, have made him rejoice, because I have fallen into the death of sin. You, Lord, who bestow mercy upon the impious and upon those who are without mercy, upon the wretched and upon their neighbors, have mercy on my humility; for with you, Lord, nothing is impossible. Show mercy to your creature, because you are kind and merciful, and because you will also raise human bodies on the day of resurrection. Hear me, Lord, because my spirit has failed and my soul is wretched; my body, too, has wasted away because of uncleanness, and because of my iniquity I am no longer worthy to live.

Forgive me, Lord; I repent of my sins. Give me life through your mercy, and grant me a contrite and humbled heart, which you do not despise. Give me confidence in your mercy and forgiveness, so that, during the remaining time of life that you grant me, I may keep your commandments and never depart from your fear, but may devoutly serve you [Col. 1402A] and sincerely fulfill your will. Spare me, because in your goodness I confess all my sins before your holy angels and before righteous people. Lord, have mercy on me, so that I may instruct others also and lead them to your holy service. Lord, give me life and strengthen me in your will; grant me perseverance in good works and the necessary vigilance against all the enemy’s snares, as well as knowledge and strength to resist his temptations. Have mercy on me and hear me, Lord my God. You who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

### Against the envy of men

Deliver us, Lord, from the barking of the worst men, so that the filthy contagions of their slanderous vomit may not pollute our purity, which comes from you. We beseech you, merciful Ruler, God, who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

### Daily prayer

[Col. 1402B] Almighty and eternal God, we humbly beseech you not to permit us to perish, because we are your creatures. Grant us a period in which to live, so that, before the day of our departure, we may deserve to please you through true repentance. Through the Lord.

### Confession and prayer of Saint Augustine from his books of Confessions

O Lord Jesus, who have mercy on all who seek you with a pure heart, how far I wandered through my memory, seeking you! For no one finds you anywhere unless your mercy reveals you in his memory. From the time when I learned of you with a pure heart, I have not forgotten you. For wherever I found truth, there I found you, my Lord. Therefore, from the time when I learned of you, you remain in my memory, and there I find you whenever I remember you, and I delight in you.

For these are my holy delights, which you gave me in your mercy, looking upon my poverty. You gave me this gracious gift in my memory, that you might remain in it. Where, then, did I find you [Col. 1402C], so that I might learn of you, unless also above myself, in you—for you are everywhere, my God, full and perfect? And whoever seeks you with a pure heart, in your mercy you implant yourself in the memory of the one seeking you, so that there he may find you.

For you alone are truth, and you preside everywhere; you answer all who consult you at once, and you clearly answer even those consulting you about different things. But not all clearly hear your answer. Your best servant is the one who does not chiefly look to hear from you what he himself has carnally desired, but rather desires what he has heard from you.

Woe to me, wretched man, that I loved you so late, beauty so ancient and so new! For by your holy grace you called me, broke through my deafness, enlightened my heart, and drove away my blindness. You gave me pure understanding, so that I might know you; you also gave me love, so that I might love you; and you gave me the will, so that I might burn with longing for your holy peace.

For when I have clung to you with a holy will, no pain [Col. 1402D] or labor will harm me; rather, all my life will be alive and full of your grace, because when you fill a person, you lift him up; but when I am not full of you, I am a burden to myself. My joys that ought to be mourned contend with my sorrows that ought to be rejoiced in, and I do not know on which side victory stands. My evil sorrows contend with my good joys, and I do not know on which side victory stands.

Woe to me, Lord; have mercy on me! Woe to me! Behold, I do not hide my wounds: you are the physician, and I am sick; you are merciful, whereas I am wretched. For what is human life upon earth but temptation? And is all my hope not in your very great mercy?

Grant, Lord, that we may both will and be able to accomplish what you command, and command what you will. You command us to practice self-restraint, but no one can be self-restrained except by your gift. And this itself is wisdom: to know whose gift it is. Through self-restraint, indeed, we are gathered into the members of your body and brought back into unity, from which we have flowed out into many things.

For he loves you less than he ought [Col. 1403A] who loves anything together with you. O love, which always burns and is never extinguished! You are true charity; you are pure charity. My God, extinguish in me every evil desire and kindle in me the sweetest charity.

You command self-restraint, merciful God; give what you command. Certainly you command me to restrain myself from the desire of the eyes and from ambition for this world. Yet the images of such things still live in my memory, fixed there by habit, and they present themselves to me. Can your hand not heal all the sicknesses of my soul, almighty God, and by your more abundant grace extinguish even the wanton impulses of my actions?

Increase in me, Lord, increase more and more in me your gifts, so that my soul may follow you within me. You who, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, are one God, one Lord, living and reigning through all things and above all things, forever and ever. Amen.

### Another prayer of the same author against illusions in sleep

Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on me and restrain in [Col. 1403B] me every movement of unlawful desire, so that it may not rebel against me even in dreams, nor compel me to commit shameful acts of corruption—acts by which animal images in dreams seek to seduce me even to the emission of the flesh. Let my mind not even consent to the evil persuasion.

For that I should not desire anything of this kind, however slight, which could be restrained by a nod—even in the chaste affection of one sleeping—is no great thing for you, almighty God, who are able to do beyond what we ask or understand. Yet I have now told you, my good Lord, how far I still remain in this form of my evil, rejoicing with trembling in what you have granted me and mourning over the fact that I am still imperfect, hoping that you will perfect your mercies in me, until complete peace belongs to my inward and outward parts when delay has been swallowed up in victory.

Grant and accomplish this, almighty God, who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

### Another prayer against the vice of gluttony

[Col. 1403C]

Almighty and most gentle God, with your grace inspiring me and your mercy assisting me, I try daily to resist evil temptations. I invoke upon myself the help of your grace, and I refer the burning of my spirit to you, because I have no counsel concerning this matter from anywhere else but from you, my God, my mercy.

At last I hear your commanding voice: “Let not your hearts be weighed down with surfeiting and drunkenness.” Merciful one, I beg you to keep drunkenness far from me. Have mercy, lest it deceive me. Yet surfeiting sometimes steals upon your servant; have mercy, so that you may turn it away from me. For no one can be self-restrained unless you grant it.

You bestow many good things on us when we pray, and whatever good we received before we prayed, we received from you; and that we later came to know this, we also received from you. I heard another word of yours: “Do not go after your desires, and turn away from your will.” I also heard, through your gift, the saying I have loved so much: “Neither, if we eat, shall we abound, [Col. 1403D] nor, if we do not eat, shall we fail.” This is understood thus: neither will food make me rich, nor will hunger make me wretched, because the soul is refreshed by fasting.

I heard another saying: “I have learned to be content in whatever state I am. I know how to abound; I know how to suffer need. I can do all things in him who strengthens me.” Christ, merciful God, strengthen me; give me the will and the ability to do what you command; command what you will. From this it is evident, my holy God, that you grant the accomplishment of what you command to be done.

Rescue me, most loving God, from every temptation and from every evil. And who is there, Lord, who is not carried beyond the fears of necessity? Whoever he may be, your mercy is great; your name deserves to be magnified. But I am not such a one, because I am a sinful man. Nevertheless, I always magnify your name, O holy Father Christ, who intercedes with you for my sins, who conquered the world. Count me at least among the sound members of your body, because your eyes have seen my imperfection.

All your righteous will be written in your book [Col. 1404A] through you, giver of all good things, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit live and reign, one God, forever and ever. Amen.

### On daily prayer

Incline, O God, to help me; Lord, hasten to assist me. Three times, with the Gloria. Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, in your name I will lift up my hands. Almighty God, deign to help me, and grant me knowledge, understanding, and a good will, together with catholic faith, for your service. Lord, you are the one who came to save sinners; save us. God, let it be as you will, as pleases you. Most merciful Lord God, deign to assist me. For you know what is necessary for us.

### Here begins the confession

God of immeasurable mercy, God of boundless compassion, God, creator and restorer of the human race, who purify the hearts of those who confess to you and absolve those who accuse themselves [Col. 1404B] before the sight of your divine clemency from every bond of iniquity: with all my groans I implore your power to grant me, according to the multitude of your mercies, a pure confession before you concerning all my sins of which my conscience accuses me, and to grant me true and worthy repentance for all these things—for whatever I have sinned in evil thoughts, perverse reflections, evil consent, wicked counsel, desire and unclean delight, idle words, malicious deeds, sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch.

For you, merciful God, gave me the individual members of the body, suited to human use, for the working out of the salvation of my soul. But I, most wretched and sinful of all, despised you, the author of eternal salvation, and, persuaded by the enemy who was preparing eternal fires for me, consented to them.

I fell into sins; I collapsed into transgressions; in each of my members I exceeded the measure of nature, and most impiously made myself subject to wicked and perverse [Col. 1404C] labors. My feet were exceedingly swift to run toward evil, following lust, but weak in obeying your commandments. My legs were strong to support me in evil. I gladly bent my knees toward fornication rather than adoration. In my thighs and genitals I did not fear contaminating myself beyond measure with every uncleanness, and I made myself guilty at every hour.

My belly and all my inner parts are continually distended with surfeiting and drunkenness. In my kidneys and loins I burn with the most shameful desire, through diabolical illusion and the flame of lust. My sides do not fear committing the wantonness of wickedness. I strengthened my back for sinful deeds and raised my neck in carnal pride. I subjected my shoulders to carrying the burdens of wickedness and continually offered my arms to seductive embraces.

My hands are full of blood and polluted with every filth, ready for every evil work and sluggish for doing any [Col. 1404D] good. My mouth is polluted with a wicked kiss and stained by evil desire; with wanton and babbling words it has abundantly defiled me, and with lies. Ever devoted to gluttony and drunkenness, never satisfied with carnal desires, my tongue has been profaned by slander and every deceit. My throat continually burns with insatiable greed. My ears are suited to deceitful speech, ready for every evil and deaf to every good.

In my nostrils I have often delighted in sinful odors and have not recoiled even from the stench of transgressions. What, then, shall I say of my eyes, which have made me liable to many crimes and turned away all the perception of my heart? To them I consented in every lust; they also perverted me by their evil gaze when, although rarely, I worshiped you, Lord, in your sanctuary, and they dragged every movement of my body toward unclean desires.

And my head, which rises above all the other members, I have rarely ever inclined toward you, Lord [Col. 1405A], my Creator; rather, I made it agree with the other members in every evil. My heart, full of deceit and wickedness, I have never purified with pure repentance; I have often polluted it with diabolical illusion and have never sufficiently washed it with true confession.

In recounting these things, Lord, I am not blaspheming your creature in me; rather, most loving God, I ask you for medicine for myself. For I recognize that in all my members I am guilty beyond measure, because I know that my sins are as innumerable as the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea.

Moreover, I confess myself subject to sadness, acedia, vainglory, greed, sloth, and all eight principal vices. But you, Lord, knower of hidden things, who said that you prefer the repentance of sinners to their death, to you I reveal all the secrets of my heart. Look upon me and have mercy on me; grant the fountain of tears and the forgiveness of all sins to me, who ask with an inward confession of the heart.

Renew and restore in me, most loving Father, whatever [Col. 1405B] has been corrupted by action, word, or finally thought through diabolical deceit. Join me, a member of the body of the Church, to the unity of your redemption, and admit me, who have confidence in nothing but your mercy, to the sacrament of your reconciliation.

Through Jesus Christ, your only-begotten Son, our Lord and Savior, who with you and the Holy Spirit are one God, one Lord, reigning through immortal ages, forever and ever. Amen.

### Another prayer

God, glory of the righteous and mercy of sinners, who said, “I do not desire the death of a sinner, but rather that he should turn and live”: receive me, most loving Father, your penitent servant, because I confess to you all my transgressions and sins, whatever I have sinned before you and before your holy angels—in thought, word, and deed, in all vices and sins alike.

I confess my guilt in pride and arrogance [Col. 1405C], by which I consider myself to have been most grievously polluted, and in all the sins that arise from them; in disobedience, wicked presumption, obstinacy, contention, arrogance, and stubbornness; in gluttony, by which I consider myself occupied beyond measure, and in all the vices generated by it; in dishonorable joy, buffoonery and laughter, empty talk, uncleanness of heart and body alike, instability of mind, lust and drunkenness, immoderate feasting, and fornication, by which I feel myself polluted in many ways, and in all the crimes that spring from it.

I confess blindness of mind, evil and harmful sight, vain and shameful hearing, immoderate taste, criminal smell, most wicked touch, consent to evil pleasure, excessive love of my own will, danger to life, wantonness and insolence, lack of restraint in evil desire, wicked counsel, hatred of your commandments, negligence, and disregard of the life to come.

I also consider myself deeply submerged in greed beyond measure [Col. 1405D], and in the whole sequence of crimes that proceed from it: envy and deceit, theft and robbery, perjury and lying, false witness, restlessness of mind, unjust judgment or fraud, contempt for truth, forgetfulness of eternal blessedness, and hardness unto death.

Then, in anger and irascibility, I consider myself excessively corrupted, and in all the sins that arise from that root: swelling of mind, quarrel and dissension, insult, love of reviling or revenge, hatred, impatience, curses and blasphemies, unjust indignation, and remembrance of my injury.

I fear that I am also excessively subject to immense acedia and to every stain of crime that bursts forth from its tinder: sleepiness, sloth in good works, inconstancy, wandering of mind, fear of labor, weariness of heart, delay and indulgence, and unjust sadness inflicted in me by the ancient enemy. I greatly fear [Col. 1406A] that I am wrapped in its most wicked seed: malignity of spirit, harshness of tongue, bitterness of words, resentment, faintheartedness, the vice of vainglory, and all the evils that proceed from it.

I consider myself greatly corrupted by boasting, arrogance, indignation toward my neighbors, discord, hypocrisy, and innumerable sins. Moreover, I could have helped many who were placed in affliction and distress by your grace, and freed many from tribulation and anguish, but because my sins delayed me, I did less of this than I ought. Often I knowingly passed by evil and neglected to speak good. Therefore I now feel most gravely guilty, and I confess myself guilty.

But you, Lord, who know all things before they happen, to you I will disclose all the crimes of my heart. I humbly implore your mercy, that you may consign forever to oblivion everything I have sinned before you and everything of which my conscience accuses me—whether I have confessed it, or whether through negligence or forgetfulness I have concealed it in thought, [Col. 1406B] word, deed, or my negligence.

You, God of infinite mercy, who are accustomed to help all who call upon you in truth, I beseech you with a suppliant mind to grant me, during the time of this life, salutary compunction from the depths of my heart, true repentance, pure confession, worthy amendment in all things, and an abundant fountain of tears with which I may mourn the evils I have committed.

For if there are any of the things named above with which I have not been polluted, it is your kindness, Lord, that defended me. But I know that whatever evil I have done has resulted from my heedlessness or even my ignorance. Nevertheless, I am your creature, Lord, and you redeemed me with your most sacred and precious blood.

Have mercy on me and grant me fruitful lamentation, so that I may not commit again the things that must be mourned. You, most merciful Lord, giver of all good things, grant me true humility against the spirit of pride, by which I may overcome every evil of pride; worthy self-restraint against gluttony and evil desire [Col. 1406C]; and, against the uncleanness of fornication, chastity of heart and body and the mortification of every wicked pleasure, together with assiduity in fasting and prayer and a holy practice of vigils.

Grant that, through the mercy of your grace, I may overcome every temptation of the devil; against greed, generosity pleasing to you, and strength and knowledge to overcome all that arises from it; against the impulse of anger, patience and moderation of spirit, so that everything that proceeds from anger may be extinguished in me.

Against acedia in good works, grant perseverance and zeal for the holy struggle, so that I may fulfill your will in all things, insofar as your kindness grants this gift in me. Against sadness, grant me, Lord, spiritual joy, through which all the evils of the vices may be utterly uprooted.

Against vainglory, grant me complete faith, firm hope, and perfect charity, so that I may deserve to love you with my whole heart, my whole mind, and all my strength; here also to receive the full forgiveness of all sins [Col. 1406D]; and in the future to possess eternal joy.

Grant this to us, O Son of God, remaining and reigning with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God in Trinity and in perfect unity, forever and ever. Amen.

### Prayer which the priest says over a penitent

God of clemency, God of mercy, God of forgiveness, deign to be propitious to our supplications and mercifully receive your penitent servant, also through the intercessions and merits of all your saints. Grant him holy compunction of heart, true repentance, and pure confession concerning all his past, present, and future sins; a place for satisfaction and a period for amendment; also an abundant fountain of tears, so that he may worthily mourn the heap of his transgressions; and the necessary vigilance, so that he may not again commit what must be mourned.

Forgive him, Lord; forgive all his crimes and sins [Col. 1407A] in thought, word, and deed alike. Henceforth strengthen and preserve him perfectly in the paths of righteousness and in the work of your will, so that among your faithful ministers he may remain entirely faithful in keeping your commandments, receive true forgiveness here, and possess eternal life in the future, through you, Christ Jesus, who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

### Pure confession

Truhtin dir uvir duih oigihlik allero minero suntiono enti missatatio. Alles desihio missa sparh eddo missateta eddo missadahta uvosto enti uvercho enti Kidancho desihkihukkiu eddoni gahukkiu Desib uvizzanto hiteta eddo un uvizzanto notak eddo un notak slaffanti eddo uvachenti mein suartio entilugino. Hyridono enti un rehteeufizur heiti huorono souvieloihsio ssiteta enti un rehtero firinlustio inmuose io tranche enti in un recheteno slafe daztumir truh tin hinist enti hinad hauverdos [Col. 1407B] farge pan dazih foradinem uagom uns hamentisi enti dazisi in deser uveralti minero missatatio hrivum enti haum sharabapen muozzi solih hosodino miltidasim alles uvaltantio truhtin.

“Lord (Truhtin), to you I confess every one of my sins (suntiono) and misdeeds (missatatio): everything that I mis-spoke, misdid, or misthought, in word, deed, and thought; whatever I concealed or hid; what I did knowingly or unknowingly, under compulsion or without compulsion, asleep or awake. I confess/deny [uncertain: entilugino] my blackness (suartio, perhaps ‘guilt’). [Uncertain:] through unrighteous desire (un rehtee ufizur), how often I have sinned, and through unrighteous greedy desire in food and drink and in unlawful sleep. May you, Lord, forgive me here and hereafter, so that I may make amends before your eyes and, in this world, repent of my sins; the final wording is corrupt or uncertain, ending with an appeal to the mercy of the all-powerful Lord.”

You, Lord, merciful Ruler and compassionate God, we beseech you, suppliant and trembling, that through your mercy you may deign to enlighten our actions with your grace and, by assisting us, bring them to a good end—you who reign, God in Trinity. Forever and ever. Amen.

### Another confession

Holy Lord, almighty Father and merciful God, who said that you prefer the repentance of sinners to their death, we beseech you that by your holy grace you may deign to enlighten our hearts and grant us most salutary compunction, by which we may humbly recognize ourselves and our sins and mourn them beneficially; and that, concerning all our transgressions and sins of which our conscience does not accuse us [Col. 1407C], we may make a pure confession before you and before your holy angels and perform worthy works of repentance.

Thus we confess to you all our sins, both capital and minor: all pride, vainglory, and boasting; sacrilege and homicide, if in any way we have been polluted by them; fornication and adultery; every lust by which we have been stained in any manner; all greed and evil desire; all gluttony and drunkenness; hatred and envy; anger and every disturbance of mind; lying and false witness; excessive speech, slander, and every idle word; perjury; fraud, theft, and robbery; curses or wicked flattery; and indiscreet silence.

We confess that we may have angered poor people who cried out and neglected their care; that we did not visit the sick and those held in chains; that we were lazier and slower than we ought to have been in holy prayer; that we came late to church; that, while others were fasting, we did not restrain our own gluttony [Col. 1407D].

We confess sleep and acedia, every torpor and idleness, wicked zeal, and all our vices and negligences, whether in thought, speech, or evil deed; whatever way we have sinned, knowingly or unknowingly, willingly or unwillingly, sleeping or awake.

Most merciful Father, grant us true and fruitful repentance for all our sins and negligences and all our carelessness before the day of our departure, and grant us worthy and necessary amendment through good works, so that, by the merits and intercessions of the saints and all your perfected ones, we may deserve true forgiveness, through your gift, Lord, and with your help, who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

### Confession to be recited during the solemn celebration of Mass

Receive my confession, my only hope of salvation [Col. 1408A], my Lord and my God. I am lost through gluttony, drunkenness, fornication, lust, sadness, acedia, sleepiness, negligence, anger, greed, envy, malice, hatred, slander, perjury, falsehood, lying, vainglory, frivolity, and pride; and altogether through thought, speech, action, and all the senses I have been destroyed. You who justify the impious and give life to the dead, justify me and raise me again, Lord my God, who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

### Prayer before receiving the Eucharist

Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who by the will of the Father, with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, gave life to the world through your death, deliver me through this sacred body and blood of yours from all iniquities and every evil. Make me obey your commandments, and never deign to separate me from you forever.

### Prayer before the altar

[Col. 1408B]

God, be gracious to me, a sinner, because you are immortal and without sin. You alone, Lord my God, are blessed, and you bless all things; you are holy, and you sanctify, Lord my God. Forgive me, your unworthy sinful servant, because I am a sinner and unworthy, because I presume to invoke you at your holy altar, because I have sinned before you and before your angels. But grant me forgiveness for my transgressions, establish me in your holy Church and in the faith of the orthodox, and teach me to do your will all the days of my life. You who live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

### Prayer of Saint Ambrose before Mass

Before the sight of your divine majesty I stand guilty, daring to invoke your holy name. Have mercy on me, Lord, a sinful man; forgive the unworthy priest through whose hands this offering appears to be offered. Spare one polluted beyond others by the stain of capital sins, and do not enter into judgment with your servant, [Col. 1408C] because no living person will be justified in your sight—especially those weighed down by vices and the pleasures of the flesh.

Remember, Lord, that we are flesh. In your sight even the heavens are not pure; how much less are we earthly human beings, unclean like a menstrual cloth. We are unworthy, Jesus Christ, to be among the living, but you, who do not desire the death of a sinner, grant forgiveness to us who are established in the flesh, so that through the labors of repentance we may enjoy eternal life in heaven through you, Jesus Christ, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

### Another prayer of the same author

Forgive me, Lord, because when I am compelled to pray, when through my unclean lips I take your holy name upon them and confess the secrets of unclean acts, I have no words before you that are free from guilt. For you know the wounds of my conscience and the hidden things of my understanding; you alone recognize my uncleannesses.

Have mercy on me, Lord; forgive me as I handle the secrets of your mystery [Col. 1408D], and do not judge him unworthy of your mercy whom you permit to pray for others. Though you do not recognize in me the testimony of good work, do not at least refuse the ministry of the stewardship entrusted to me, Savior of the world, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit live and reign throughout all ages, forever and ever. Amen.

### For making particular prayers

Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ; you are my mercy, have mercy on me. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may believe in you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may know you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may love you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that my soul may live in you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that my flesh may rejoice in you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that my life may be perfected in you.

Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, Savior, my salvation, my strength. Have mercy, Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, my consolation, my illumination [Col. 1409A]. Have mercy, Lord God, Trinity and Unity.

I praise you, I adore you, I confess you, my peace, my hope, my light, my beauty, my blessedness. To you be praise, to you glory, to you thanksgiving, always and everywhere, forever and ever.

Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, you are my mercy; have mercy on me. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may ask you rightly. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may make me worthy to be heard. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may hear me. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may teach me your holy will. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may nourish me in your charity. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may enlighten me with your Holy Spirit.

Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may believe in you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may know you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may love you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that I may hope in you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, [Col. 1409B] so that you may rescue me from perpetual death. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may grant me true repentance for all my sins. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may grant me forgiveness of all my sins. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may rescue me from every tribulation. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may free me from every uncleanness of heart and body. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may extinguish in me the tinder of lust. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may free me from the devil’s snares. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may free me from unclean thought. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that you may free me from every evil. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that my soul may live in you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that my flesh may rejoice in you. Have mercy, Lord; have mercy, Christ, so that my life may be perfected in you.

Have mercy, Lord God, Father, my glory, my soul. Have mercy, Christ, Savior, my salvation, my strength. Have mercy [Col. 1409C], Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, my consolation, my illumination. Have mercy, Lord God, Trinity and Unity.

I praise you, I adore you, I confess you, my peace, my hope, my praise, my light, my beauty, my blessedness. To you be praise, to you glory, to you thanksgiving, always and everywhere, through everlasting ages.

### Pure prayer to the praise of God
Source/review notes: Repetitions, unusual Trinitarian formulas, editorial notes, and source boundary fragments are retained.

Be present, true light, Father, almighty God. Be present, light from light, Word and Son of God, almighty God. Be present, Holy Spirit, harmony of Father and Son, almighty God. Be present, living and almighty God, Father and Son and Holy Spirit. Teach faith, awaken hope, pour in charity. To will is within my reach, but this is not from me but from you: to leave the world and lands and seek heaven; but willing without your help is a feeble wing. Give faith wings, that I may fly upward to you. Now [I confess] faith in you, through you, concerning you. I confess you one in substance, a Trinity [Col. 1409D] in persons. I confess both three as one and one as three. I confess Father and Son and Holy Spirit, O blessed Trinity. God, Lord, Paraclete, O blessed Trinity. Charity, grace, communion, O blessed Trinity. God is charity, Christ is grace, the Holy Spirit is communion: O blessed Trinity. Begetter, begotten, regenerator, O blessed Trinity. True light from light, true illumination, O blessed Trinity. Invisible invisibly, visible invisibly, invisible visibly, O blessed Trinity. Fountain, stream, irrigation, O blessed Trinity. From one are all things, through one are all things, in one are all things, O blessed Trinity. From whom, through whom, in whom are all things, O blessed Trinity. Living life, life from the living one, life-giver of the living, O blessed Trinity. One from himself, one from one, one from both, O blessed Trinity. He who is from himself, he who is from another, he who is from both, O blessed Trinity. But every being is always in the three, and every being equally in each, O blessed Trinity. Truthful Father, truth Son, truth Spirit, O blessed [Col. 1410A] Trinity. Therefore one Father, *Logos*, Paraclete, which is substance, O blessed Trinity. One essence, one power, one goodness, O blessed Trinity. God, blessedness, in whom, from whom, and through whom all things whatsoever are blessed are blessed, O blessed Trinity. God, true and highest life, in whom, from whom, and through whom all things whatsoever truly and supremely live live, O blessed Trinity. God, good and beautiful, in whom, from whom, and through whom all things whatsoever are good and beautiful are good and beautiful, O blessed Trinity. God, whom faith awakens us to [seek], hope raises us to, charity joins us to, O blessed Trinity. God, who commands us to ask, causes us to find, and opens to those who knock, O blessed Trinity. God, above whom is nothing, outside whom is nothing, without whom is nothing, O blessed Trinity. We invoke you, we adore you, we praise you, O blessed Trinity. Hear, hear, hear, O blessed Trinity. Our hope, our salvation, our honor, O blessed Trinity. Increase faith in us, increase hope, increase charity, O blessed Trinity. Deliver us, [Col. 1410B] save us, justify us, O blessed Trinity. For your mercy has delivered us, have mercy, Lord, O blessed Trinity. Have mercy, Lord, because by your mercy we believe in you, O blessed Trinity. Have mercy, Lord, because by your mercy we have come to know you, O blessed Trinity. Have mercy, Lord, because by your mercy we hope in you, O blessed Trinity. Have mercy, Lord, because by your mercy we love you, O blessed Trinity. We all adore you as one Lord, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, O blessed Trinity. Grant forgiveness of sins, bestow eternal life, give peace and glory, O blessed Trinity. O blessed, and blessed, and glorious Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit! O blessed Trinity! O blessed, blessed, glorious Unity, Father, Son, Holy Spirit! O blessed Trinity! O true, supreme, eternal Trinity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit! O true, supreme, eternal Unity, Father, Son, Holy Spirit! Have mercy on us, have mercy on us; have mercy on us, O blessed Trinity. To you be praise, to you glory, to you thanksgiving for everlasting ages, O blessed Trinity. When thoughts of vainglory or pride attack you, examine yourself, whether you have kept all God’s commandments, whether you love your enemies, whether you rejoice in the glory of your enemy, whether you grieve at his downfall, whether you hold yourself to be an unworthy servant and more sinful than all human beings; and again, rising early from your own bed before you undertake any task, say: “All human beings enter the kingdom of God because of their righteousness, but I alone, because of my sins, fear that I shall inherit everlasting punishments unless your mercy comes to my aid. I have sinned, Lord; have mercy on me, and do not permit me, your creature, to perish. Rather, look upon me, turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities; and for the glory of your name, Lord, deliver us, and be favorable toward our sins for the sake of your name.”

## On the eight principal vices, whose names are these:

[Col. 1410D] Pride, gluttony, fornication, avarice, anger, acedia, sadness, cenodoxy—that is, vainglory.

From pride arise every disobedience, every presumption, every obstinacy, quarrels, heresies, and arrogance.

From gluttony arise foolish merriment, buffoonery, frivolity, idle talk, bodily uncleanness, instability of mind, drunkenness, and lust.

From fornication arise blindness of mind, inconstancy of the eyes, immoderate love, danger to life, wantonness of life, petulance and every form of self-indulgence, hatred of God’s commandments, enervation of the mind, unjust desires, and neglect of the life to come.

From avarice arise envy, thefts, robberies, murders, lies, perjuries, plunder, violence, unrest, unjust judgments, contempt for truth, forgetfulness of future blessedness, and hardness of heart.

From anger spring the swelling of a guilty mind, insults, shouting, indignation, presumption, blasphemy, bloodshed, murders, desire for revenge, and remembrance of injuries.

From acedia arise drowsiness, laziness in good works, [Col. 1411A] instability of place, wandering from place to place, trembling, weariness of labor, murmuring of the heart, and empty talk.

From sadness arise malice, resentment of spirit, faintheartedness, bitterness, and despair.

From cenodoxy—that is, vainglory—arise boasting, arrogance, indignation, discord, desire for empty glory, and hypocrisy, that is, the simulation of a good work.

With the Lord’s help, all these evils can easily be conquered: first, pride by humility; gluttony by abstinence; fornication by chastity; avarice by wisdom; anger by patience; acedia by persistence in good works; evil sadness by spiritual joy; and vainglory by the love of God.

## Prayer against the vices

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, we beseech your mercy from the depths of our heart, that through the prayers and merits of all your saints you may grant us a pure conscience, contempt for earth, [Col. 1411B] and regard for heaven; hatred of sins and love of righteousness. Take worldly anxiety away from us, and grant us perfectly your holy fear. Drive from us the appetite of gluttony, and give us the virtue of abstinence. Put to flight from us the spirit of fornication, and pour into us the ardor of most holy chastity. Extinguish in us every evil desire, and grant voluntary poverty. Restrain anger from us, and kindle in us the most gentle charity toward God and neighbor. Expel from us boasting and vainglory, and grant us saving compunction. Remove pride from us, and perfect true humility in us. Merciful God, scatter from us altogether all the riches of the vices, and grant us the keeping of your commandments. Against impatience, pour in upright patience; against hatred and envy, brotherly charity; against detraction or murmuring, your most holy praise always; and against all vices together, the grace of blessing. Raise up in us an abundant fountain of tears, and soften our hard heart [Col. 1411C] through true repentance; and grant that we may attribute to your glory in all things whatever good things your everlasting grace works in us; that we may always know ourselves to be sinners, yet never cease from your praise or work, but always accomplish your will with persevering constancy. Through.
